items.title: Preparedness of osteopathic medical students to address vaccine hesitancy: training and confidence.
items.abstract: Context Vaccine hesitancy poses a growing threat to public health, contributing to measles resurgences and declining childhood vaccination coverage in the United States. Although physicians remain among the most trusted sources of vaccine information, formal training in vaccine communication is not consistently integrated into medical curricula. Osteopathic medical education emphasizes whole-person, patient-centered care, which closely aligns with the skills required for effective vaccine counseling. However, the preparedness of osteopathic medical students for vaccine-related communication has not been well characterized. Objectives This study aimed to assess osteopathic medical students' perceptions of their curricular preparation for vaccine-related communication, as well as clinical-year students' real-world experiences and confidence in addressing vaccine hesitancy during rotations. Methods A prospective cross-sectional anonymous online survey was administered via Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) to medical students enrolled in Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) programs across the United States. Participants were recruited through Student Osteopathic Medical Association (SOMA) communication channels and institutional listservs. The survey assessed demographics, clinical exposure to vaccine discussions, confidence in addressing vaccine hesitancy, curricular preparation, and perceived training needs utilizing 5-point Likert-scale items. Ordinal logistic regression and Welch's t tests compared preclinical (Osteopathic Medical Student [OMS]-1/2) vs. clinical (OMS-3/4) students, OMS-3 vs. OMS-4 students, and clinical vaccine discussion groups. Odds ratios (ORs) and p values were calculated on 95 % confidence intervals (CIs) between groups. Results A total of 1,415 osteopathic medical students completed the survey. Overall, 87.1 % reported no formal vaccine communication training, with 88.6 % of OMS1/2 students and 85.3 % of OMS3/4 students agreeing or strongly agreeing that vaccine communication should be formally included in their curriculum. Compared with preclinical students, clinical students were less likely to report adequate curricular preparation for addressing vaccine hesitancy (OR=0.67, 95 % CI [0.55, 0.81;] p Conclusions Osteopathic medical students recognize vaccine hesitancy as a routine clinical challenge, agree that additional training in counseling would be helpful, and although clinical exposure builds confidence, this may occur unevenly and without structured design; formal training would help build this competence earlier and more equitably. Evidence-based tools, including motivational interviewing, simulation, and standardized patient encounters, align closely with osteopathic principles of whole-person care. Integrating these approaches into required curricula represents a practical and necessary step toward preparing future physicians to navigate both vaccine-related conversations and difficult conversations effectively.

items.title: The Defensive Origin and Reconstruction of Human Morality: An Instinct-Driven Theory of Moral Formation and Transformation
items.abstract: Abstract This paper introduces the Instinct-Driven Moral Reconstruction (IDMR) Theory, a theoretical framework proposing that human morality and ideological systems emerge from the interaction between fundamental biological self-defense mechanisms and the demands of social life. The central hypothesis is that morality is not the primary origin of defensive behavior; rather, moral and ideological systems developed as adaptive intermediaries that translate primitive defensive mechanisms into socially organized behavior. Within this framework, self-preservation serves as a foundational biological principle, while moral norms and ideological beliefs function as culturally constructed and adaptable systems that regulate protection, cooperation, conflict, and aggression. The theory further proposes that these moral structures are not necessarily stable. When perceived existential threats activate fundamental defensive mechanisms, previously established moral judgments may undergo substantial reconstruction. Under such conditions, actions ordinarily considered immoral, including aggression against other groups, may be reinterpreted as morally justified or even obligatory acts of collective defense. Crucially, IDMR distinguishes this process from a simple reduction in moral restraint. The proposed mechanism involves the transformation of moral evaluation itself, whereby defensive aggression can become subjectively perceived as a moral duty. The framework integrates evolutionary psychology, moral cognition, social learning, identity-related threat perception, and computational modeling. It presents formal mechanisms, testable hypotheses, and potential research directions for examining the origins, internalization, and threat-induced reconstruction of moral systems. Historical phenomena such as ideological radicalization, wartime propaganda, and collective violence are discussed as potential applications, while recognizing that these events involve additional political, institutional, and historical factors. Ethical Considerations: The authors explicitly acknowledge the potential dual-use risks of research on defensive motivation and moral reconstruction. The framework is intended to support scientific understanding, resistance to psychological manipulation, and the prevention of destructive propaganda—not to facilitate coercion, radicalization, or violence. The theory is presented as a falsifiable conceptual proposal rather than an empirically established account of morality's evolutionary origins. Author: TrinityLabo Keywords: Moral Evolution, Self-Defense Instinct, Moral Reconstruction, Evolutionary Psychology, Moral Cognition, Ideological Formation, Threat Perception, Collective Aggression, IDMR Theory

items.title: Optimizing Rib Remodeling: A Data-Driven Model for Personalized Waist Contouring.
items.abstract: Rib cage remodeling procedures, like rib osteotomy with osteosynthesis, have shown promise for waist narrowing in aesthetic surgery. However, the ideal osteotomy location and bending angle remain poorly defined. This preclinical, proof-of-concept study aimed to: (1) quantify how osteotomy location and rib bending angle affect rib apex displacement using a large, computed tomography (CT) dataset, and (2) develop a data-driven framework as a first step toward guiding selection of rib number, osteotomy site, and bending angle tailored to individual waist contour goals. Using the open-source RibFrac CT dataset, 600 ribs (300 eleventh [XI] and 300 tenth [X]) were segmented with the RibSeg deep learning tool. A custom MATLAB script simulated 15 bending scenarios per rib by varying osteotomy location (7 cm, 8 cm, 9 cm from midline) and bending angles (10°, 20°, 30°, 45°, 55°). Displacement at the rib apex was computed using a chord-perpendicular method. A graphical user interface (GUI) allowed for manual interaction, and a linear mixed-effects model quantified the effects of angle, osteotomy location, and their interaction. Both bending angle and osteotomy distance significantly affected apex displacement (p < 0.001), with a negative interaction indicating reduced effect of angle at more lateral osteotomy points. Rib X showed greater displacement overall than rib XI. This proof-of-concept model establishes a biomechanical foundation for individualized rib remodeling planning. While prospective clinical validation is needed, the framework is adaptable to patient-specific imaging across age, sex, and BMI, and may ultimately support personalized surgical decision-making.

items.title: Structural brain abnormality, pharmacotherapy, and treatment resistant schizophrenia management: a systematic review and critical appraisal.
items.abstract: Introduction Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) affects up to 30% of patients with schizophrenia and carries a substantial burden, yet clozapine, the only antipsychotic specifically indicated, is delayed by years because resistance is recognized retrospectively. Neuroimaging may provide objective biomarkers to shorten this delay. Methods We searched PubMed and Scopus to June 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. We included peer-reviewed neuroimaging studies investigating TRS, covering structural, functional, and metabolic modalities; studies not addressing TRS were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies and RoB 2 for randomized trials. Findings were synthesized qualitatively, without meta-analysis. Results Of 1502 identified records, 1179 were screened and 94 studies were included (44 structural, 18 functional, and 32 metabolic). TRS was characterized by extensive abnormalities in frontal cortical, limbic, and white matter pathways and, compared with treatment-responsive schizophrenia (nTRS), by the absence of striatal dopaminergic hyperactivity, alongside functional and metabolic alterations in frontal and cortico-subcortical circuits. Evidence concerning ultra-treatment-resistant schizophrenia (uTRS) remains scarce. Conclusions Neuroimaging findings support a distributed cortico-subcortical phenotype and a non-dopaminergic, potentially glutamatergic pathophysiology in TRS. However, the evidence remains constrained by small, heterogeneous, predominantly cross-sectional studies, with uTRS still poorly investigated. Protocol registration PROSPERO (CRD420261437825).

items.title: Mediators of the Link Between Parental Monitoring and Youth Adjustment: A Review of the Evidence.
items.abstract: Objective By what mechanisms does parental monitoring affect youth adjustment? This paper aimed to review every published study that has tested a statistical mediator of monitoring→adjustment. Method We searched for studies that (a) enrolled elementary-, middle-, and/or high-school aged youth, (b) measured parental monitoring as parent action (vs. e.g., knowledge), and (c) tested a statistical mediation model linking monitoring to any form of youth adjustment. Results Thirty-nine papers have tested a mediator of the link from monitoring → adjustment. Most papers used cross-sectional data (26 of 39) on typically developing samples (33 of 39). All papers were non-experimental. Only one of 39 papers made a substantial effort to rule out potential confounding-most adjusted for just a few measured covariates. Across the 39 papers, 79 out of 173 tests of mediation were statistically significant (46%). Of the significant tests, 59 indicated beneficial effects of monitoring, and 20 indicated detrimental effects of monitoring. There was at least one statistically significant test for 42 distinct pairs of mediator and outcome, but only six mediational chains (X→M→Y) had been replicated in more than one paper. Effect sizes for single mediators were typically small (median standardized ab = -0.02) and suggested multiple mediators would be needed to explain the total effect (median percent mediated = 24%). Of relevance to Stattin and Kerr's (2000) classic argument, we found only one paper testing whether youth disclosure mediates the link between monitoring and adjustment. Conclusion There are now many published tests of the mediators linking parental monitoring to youth adjustment. However, few have been replicated, and fewer still have been rigorous. As a result, the extant evidence can be reconciled with many (if not all) major theories about how parental monitoring works.

items.title: Longitudinal Associations Among Helicopter Parenting, Parent-Child Intimacy, and Adolescents' Internet Addiction.
items.abstract: Introduction Parenting styles and parent-child relationships are important family factors associated with adolescent internet addiction, yet their longitudinal and joint associations remain unclear. This study examined the bidirectional associations among helicopter parenting, parent-child intimacy, and internet addiction, as well as the joint associations of helicopter parenting and parent-child intimacy with internet addiction. Methods Participants were 437 Chinese adolescents (50.80% girls; M = 12.84 years, SD = 0.91). Data were collected at three time points at 6-month intervals. Cross-lagged panel models were used to examine longitudinal associations, and response surface analysis was conducted to investigate the joint associations of helicopter parenting and parent-child intimacy with internet addiction. Results Cross-lagged panel models indicated reciprocal prospective associations between parent-child intimacy and internet addiction. In the response surface analyses, neither maternal nor paternal helicopter parenting or parent-child intimacy showed significant linear associations with internet addiction from T1 to T2. However, both mother-child and father-child intimacy were negatively associated with internet addiction from T2 to T3. Significant positive slopes along the line of incongruence were also observed in both models, whereas the interaction and quadratic effects were nonsignificant. Conclusions Parent-child intimacy showed prospective associations with adolescent internet addiction that varied across measurement intervals. Prevention efforts should pay particular attention to adolescents experiencing low parent-child intimacy.

items.title: Psychodiagnostic Markers and Linguistic Indicators of Psychological Capital: A Theoretical Model of Complementarity Within the Structural-Functional Paradigm of Human Capital
items.abstract: Rapid epochal transformations call for rethinking human capital as a dynamic emergent entity with a complex architecture of endogenous components: educational-competence, health, social, and psychological capital. Within this architecture, psychological capital (PsyCap) acts as a cross-cutting moderator that determines the extent to which the educational-competence core is converted into socio-economic outcomes. This raises the significance of PsyCap psychodiagnostics while exposing the limitations of reflective self-report instruments, which capture momentary self-assessments and remain vulnerable to social desirability bias.The article aims to substantiate the integration of linguistic indicators into PsyCap assessment and to develop a matrix model mapping the four HERO components (hope, efficacy, resilience, optimism) onto classes of linguistic indicators. Drawing on systemic, structural-functional, and interdisciplinary approaches, the study uses construct validity criteria to frame linguistic indicators as external correlates within the nomological network of PsyCap.The model matches hope with achievement and goal-setting markers, efficacy with markers of confidence and control, resilience with register flexibility and reduced negative affect, and optimism with positive-emotional and forward-oriented language. Linguistic indicators cannot replace standardized instruments; rather, they constitute a complementary data source, provided that linguistic and cultural adaptation, control of socio-economic confounders, and ethical safeguards against profiling are ensured. The study builds a conceptual bridge between psychodiagnostics and psycholinguistics and outlines a pathway toward the culturally adapted operationalization of PsyCap assessment in Ukrainian psychology.

items.title: Social Bonds as Predictors of a Central Symptom of Problematic Short-Form Video Use Across Genders: A Network Analysis and Machine Learning Study.
items.abstract: Introduction Problematic short-form video use (PSVU) has emerged as a pressing public health issue. Although research on this topic is expanding, few studies have systematically explored the complex predictors of problematic short-form video use across genders. This study sought to combine network analysis and machine learning (ML) to decode the associations between social bonds and problematic short-form video use across genders. Methods A cross-sectional survey of 2076 Chinese adolescents (51.73% girls, mean age = 13.75) assessed problematic short-form video use, social bonds (attachment, commitment, involvement, belief), and demographic information. Results Results indicated that PSVU2 (i.e., increasing time for satisfaction) was the central symptom of problematic short-form video use across genders. ML findings revealed that commitment was the most predictive dimension for the central symptom of problematic short-form video use in both boys and girls, followed by belief, involvement, attachment, and demographic information at the dimension level. At the factor level, the top six factors with the greatest predictive contributions in girls were academic engagement, prosocial behaviors, mindfulness, responsibility, belief in a just world, and grit. In boys, these factors were responsibility, academic engagement, mindfulness, grit, parent-child relationships, and belief in a just world. Conclusions These findings offer both theoretical insights and practical guidance for intervention strategies targeting adolescent problematic short-form video use.

items.title: Urban Ecology Compiler: An AI-Assisted Geospatial Framework for Compiling Natural-Language Planning Goals into Spatial Ecological Interventions
items.abstract: Urban ecological planning requires the integration of environmental information, spatial constraints, budget considerations, and competing sustainability objectives. However, translating high-level natural-language planning goals into geographically grounded and actionable ecological interventions remains a complex task. This paper presents the Urban Ecology Compiler, an AI-assisted geospatial decision-support framework that translates natural-language urban planning objectives into structured, spatially explicit ecological intervention plans. The framework combines large language model capabilities with geospatial data processing and environmental information to interpret planning objectives, evaluate spatial constraints, and generate intervention proposals within specified budget limits. It supports ecological planning objectives including flood resilience, urban greenery, heat reduction, and biodiversity enhancement. The system integrates geospatial technologies and data sources including OpenStreetMap, Copernicus Sentinel, Open-Meteo, and OpenElevation. Proposed interventions include green corridors, rain gardens, bioswales, permeable pavements, and other nature-based solutions. Spatial outputs are represented using GeoJSON and visualised through an interactive geospatial interface. The paper documents the system architecture, methodology, implementation, and experimental evaluation. An internal benchmark involving 200 compilations reports 94.2% valid GeoJSON generation. These results represent internal experimental evaluations and should not be interpreted as independent real-world validation. The framework is intended as a prototype for AI-assisted urban ecological planning and decision support. Its outputs are designed to support preliminary planning and exploration rather than replace expert assessment or field-based environmental validation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Geospatial Decision Support, Urban Ecology, Large Language Models, GeoAI, Nature-Based Solutions, Sustainable Urban Planning, Environmental Planning, Spatial Optimisation, Climate Resilience.

items.title: Apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) causes disruption of glypican-1 recycling and processing in ApoE4/4 fibroblasts and induced neurons.
items.abstract: The apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) isoform confers increased risk of developing Alzheimer's disease. ApoE2 and ApoE3 can be S-nitrosylated (Cys-SNO), but not ApoE4. The recycling heparan sulfate (HS) proteoglycan glypican-1 (GPC1) can also carry SNO and release HS by a Cu/NO dependent cleavage. ApoE3/3 and ApoE4/4 fibroblasts and the respective induced neurons (-iN) were exposed to inhibitors of NO-synthases (NOS), to NO donor or ascorbate and examined by immunofluorescence microscopy. Exposure to NO donor increased co-localization between ApoE3-SNO and GPC1 in ApoE3/3 fibroblasts. Co-localization between ApoE3 and GPC1 diminished when cNOS/NOS3 was inhibited in ApoE3/3 fibroblasts. Exposure to NO donor or ascorbate indicated almost fully utilized capacity to release HS from GPC1. When nNOS/NOS1 and iNOS/NOS2 were inhibited in ApoE3/3-iN, release of HS decreased, and exposure to ascorbate again showed that the capacity to release HS was almost fully utilized. In ApoE4/4 fibroblasts endosome transport was retarded and HS and GPC1-SNO accumulated in late endosomes. Inhibition of cNOS/NOS3 in ApoE4/4 fibroblasts had no effect on HS release but inhibition of iNOS/NOS2 had a substantial effect. Exposure to NO donor or ascorbate revealed unutilized capacity to release HS from GPC1. In ApoE4/4-iN, nNOS/NOS1 and iNOS/NOS2 were major producers of NO. Inhibition of nNOS/NOS1 and iNOS/NOS2 in ApoE4/4-iN again showed unutilized capacity to release HS. We propose that expression of ApoE4, which retards endosome trafficking, but also activates iNOS/NOS2, results in accumulation of GPC1-SNO and slow exit of HS from endosomes which can be restored by ascorbate.

items.title: Predictors of in-hospital mortality, sepsis and prolonged length of stay in burn patients: a ten-year monocentric experience and comparison with the Baux and revised Baux scores.
items.abstract: Burn mortality is usually predicted with the Baux and revised Baux scores, which do not include comorbidity; the independent role of psychiatric disease is also poorly defined. We reviewed 793 consecutive burn patients (630 adults, 163 children) admitted to a regional referral centre between 2016 and 2025. In adults, logistic models for in-hospital mortality, sepsis, and prolonged length of stay (at least 30 days) used age group, burn size by total body surface area, inhalation injury, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index as covariates, with internal bootstrap validation. Adult in-hospital mortality was 7.8% (49 of 630); no child died. Independent predictors of mortality were age 85 years or older (odds ratio 18.9), burn size 40% or more (odds ratio 40.6), inhalation injury (odds ratio 4.29), and a comorbidity index of 2 or more (odds ratio 14.2). Psychiatric disorders, not captured by the comorbidity index, were also independently associated with mortality (odds ratio 2.83). The multivariable model, a Baux-based model, and a revised Baux-based model (both including the comorbidity index) had almost identical discrimination (optimism-corrected 0.941, 0.955, 0.957; pairwise p>0.05). For sepsis and prolonged stay, burn size and age dominated, while comorbidity lost significance; the crude association between sepsis and mortality disappeared after adjustment, whereas sepsis remained strongly associated with prolonged stay (adjusted odds ratio 10.8). A multivariable model discriminates as well as the Baux scores while allowing comorbidity and psychiatric history to be quantified.

items.title: Diagnosis and management of benign vocal fold lesions in children: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Purpose Pediatric benign vocal fold lesions (BVFLs) are a common cause of chronic dysphonia in children, yet evidence on their diagnosis and management remains heterogeneous and unsystematized. This review aims to critically synthesize the available evidence on diagnostic strategies, comparative treatment outcomes, and indications for surgical management of BVFLs in the pediatric population. Methods This PRISMA-compliant systematic review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2000 and March 2026. Eligible studies included patients aged ≤ 18 years with endoscopically confirmed BVFLs and reported diagnostic or treatment outcomes. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized descriptively with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. Results Ten studies including 559 children were analyzed. Vocal fold nodules accounted for 86.7% of lesions, and flexible laryngoscopy was the most commonly used diagnostic tool. Conservative management was used in 88.0% of patients, with improvement rates of 75.5%-87.5% and no reported complications. Surgery was performed in 12.0%, with improvement rates of 79.2%-100%; one study reported postoperative complications in 20% of patients. Surgical indications were not standardized, and median follow-up was 4.5 months. Conclusion Conservative management, primarily behavioral voice therapy, is safe, effective, and should remain the first-line treatment for pediatric BVFLs. Surgery is an appropriate secondary option for structural or refractory lesions, but requires stringent patient selection given the risk of permanent vocal fold damage. Evidence gaps in standardized surgical indications, outcome measures, and long-term follow-up represent priorities for future prospective multicenter research.

items.title: NBD-F derivatization and rapid separation of catecholamines and their O-methylated metabolites using flow-gated micellar electrokinetic chromatography.
items.abstract: Catecholamines function as neurotransmitters and hormones in the brain and the sympathetic nervous system. Measurements of these compounds are important in neuroscience research, clinical diagnosis, and drug development. Their O-methylated metabolites, particularly metanephrine and normetanephrine, are established biomarkers used in the biochemical evaluation of pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas. The objective of this study was to evaluate 4-fluoro-7-nitro-2,1,3-benzoxadiazole (NBD-F) as the fluorogenic agent for the rapid separation and sensitive detection of these compounds using flow-gated capillary electrophoresis (CE). Experimental results showed that NBD-F in excess of the analytes readily reacted with amino and phenolic hydroxyl groups of catecholamines, resulting in fully NBD-substituted, tri-NBD derivatives. Similarly, the O-methylated metabolites of catecholamines were also fully NBD-substituted, forming di-NBD derivatives. These derivatives were separated with micellar electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC) within 80 s. Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in the sample solution might facilitate the derivatization of catecholamines, whereas SDS in the separation buffer enhanced fluorescence intensity of the derivatives. The limits of detection (LODs) were estimated to be 1.7 nM for dopamine and 1.3 nM for norepinephrine, representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previously reported LODs obtained using the MEKC/NBD-Cl method. The method was further applied to the analysis of urine and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples to demonstrate its applicability. These results demonstrate the potential of the NBD-F/MEKC approach as a sensitive and rapid analytical method for catecholamines and their metabolites and as a useful biochemical tool for neuroscience research.

items.title: Sex, but not age, drives transcriptome-wide gene expression variation in a turtle with female-biased longevity.
items.abstract: Sexes frequently differ in life-history traits including body size, lifespan, and age at sexual maturity. Organismal aging, the progressive decline in physiological function and cellular resilience over time, is a central component of sex-specific life histories, yet the mechanisms driving sex differences in aging remain largely unresolved. Long-term mark-recapture efforts reveal a striking pattern of female-biased longevity in painted turtles (Chrysemys picta) (lifespan: males = 24 years, females = 48 years). This species exhibits temperature-dependent sex determination, and thus, provides a compelling system to test for the molecular underpinnings of sex-specific aging in the absence of sex chromosomes. Here, we assess how sex, age, and their interaction affect gene expression in the blood transcriptomes of wild adult painted turtles (N = 93) spanning the entire lifespan. We identified widespread gene expression differences between females and males (2,347 genes; 13.4% of all filtered genes). In contrast, only six genes showed significant linear relationships with age in both sexes. We also employed a machine-learning approach that identified distinct genes in each sex for which expression was predictive of age. Age-related gene expression patterns highlight both conserved molecular pathways with known roles in organismal aging (e.g., insulin/insulin-like signaling and target of rapamycin) as well as novel gene targets. These findings suggest sex-specific molecular processes may contribute to observed sex differences in demographic aging in this species. More broadly, this work underscores the need for future studies disentangling the environmental and developmental contributions to sex-specific survival trajectories in species with diverse sex determination systems.

items.title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole.
items.abstract: The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged 'lake' at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) planktonic microbes for shotgun metagenomics and solid-phase extracted dissolved organic matter for untargeted metabolomics from 21 stations at depths ranging from 2 to 600 m during a 10-day research cruise in December 2019. We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota, Thermoproteota, Planctomycetota, and Actinobacteriota. We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. Correlations between microbial taxa and metabolite classes show potential links between nitrifying archaea and halogenated compound cycling. We further supported these findings using the functional annotation of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and protein clusters showing enrichment of nitrification and halogen cycling genes, suggesting the presence of specialized degradation and biosynthetic pathways, directly connecting microbial metabolism to the observed geochemical conditions. These findings demonstrate that the submerged acid lake contains specific microbially driven biogeochemical processes under acidified and low-oxygen conditions, providing a natural model for future extreme ocean acidification scenarios. With this multi‑omics approach, we were able to connect the microbial metabolism with this unique environment, thereby expanding our understanding of how both are interconnected. Video Abstract.

items.title: Ecological succession in Glomeromycota: How to know a hawk from a handsaw.
items.abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungal communities in the roots of terrestrial plants present strong seasonal changes over the growing season, but the drivers and ecological consequences of those temporal dynamics remain poorly understood. We present and review here three competing, but not mutually exclusive, hypotheses about AM fungal seasonality. Each of them assumes a different controlling factor, namely plant host, intrinsic AM fungal dynamics, and climate, but they can all potentially explain seasonal trajectories, while simultaneously contributing invaluable insights on the functioning of arbuscular mycorrhizal systems. We synthesize evidence in support of and against each of these three hypotheses. We then summarize insights that could be gained from testing these hypotheses and propose experimental designs to disentangle their relative contributions to belowground seasonality. We therefore contribute a testable framework for designing multi-time-point metabarcoding studies to disentangle drivers of belowground seasonality.

items.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
items.abstract: Sleep is accompanied by coordinated changes in neuronal activity and cerebral hemodynamics. However, cortical hemodynamic signatures across sleep stages remain poorly characterized, partly because most human electroencephalography (EEG)/functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies are limited in duration, rarely capture deep or Rapid-Eye-Movement (REM) sleep, have low sampling rate, or rely on a sleep-deprivation paradigm, which limits the generalizability of findings. Here, we combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in healthy young adults, as a bedside technology to monitor cortical hemodynamic fluctuations. We recorded fNIRS using an optimal, personalized, locally dense bilateral frontoparietal montage, alongside peripheral physiology recordings (respiration, photoplethysmography, mean arterial pressure). We computed oscillatory components of oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin (HbO-HbR) spectra across sleep stages using wavelet-based time-frequency analysis. Additionally, we analyzed within the same regions an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset (no REM recorded). Our results are suggesting that across frontal and parietal regions, slow-frequency (0.002-0.1Hz) power increased during N1 sleep in HbO and then progressively attenuated across N2 and N3 sleep, in HbO, HbR, and fMRI. REM showed a re-emergence of very-low-frequency power (<0.01Hz) in HbO and HbR. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15-0.5Hz; overlapping respiratory-band) were selectively enhanced during NREM sleep (largest increase during N3) and returned toward wake-like levels during REM in frontal regions, with regional differences. Peripheral signals captured systemic physiology oscillations but did not reproduce the cortical stage-specific patterns. Together, our findings provide a cortical characterization of sleep-stage hemodynamic organizations that can serve as a reference for future mechanistic and clinical sleep studies.

items.title: From physical symmetry to aesthetic value: investigating symmetry-induced attractiveness enhancement with fMRI.
items.abstract: Facial symmetry contributes to perceived attractiveness, but how physical symmetry is linked to subjective aesthetic evaluation in the brain remains unclear. In this study, we used fMRI to examine BOLD responses to identity-matched symmetrical and asymmetrical faces while participants rated either facial attractiveness or facial symmetry. Behaviorally, symmetrical faces were rated as both more symmetrical and more attractive than asymmetrical faces, although the attractiveness enhancement varied across facial identities. To link the physical symmetry manipulation to subjective evaluation, we modeled two complementary measures: trial-by-trial raw ratings and identity-matched changes in ratings induced by the symmetry manipulation. The categorical contrast between symmetrical and asymmetrical faces identified left superior temporal/supramarginal activity during attractiveness evaluation, but this pattern was not confirmed by the direct task comparison. Rating-based parametric analysis showed that lower attractiveness ratings were associated with greater activity in the superior frontal gyrus and middle occipital gyrus. Exploratory gain-based analyses further suggested that symmetry-induced attractiveness gain was associated with activity in ventral occipito-temporal regions, with stronger attractiveness-gain than symmetry-gain modulation in the left occipito-temporal cortex. Together, these findings suggest that fMRI responses to facial symmetry are better characterized by considering subjective symmetry-induced changes in attractiveness than by categorical symmetry contrasts alone.

items.title: Genetic and anatomical correlates of velopharyngeal insufficiency in patients with cleft lip and/or palate: implications for interdisciplinary assessment.
items.abstract: Objectives To characterize velopharyngeal closure patterns (VPCPs) in patients with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) associated with cleft lip and/or palate and to examine their associations with cleft phenotype, associated nasal anatomical findings, and genetic or syndromic classification. Materials and methods A retrospective, analytical, single-center observational study was conducted involving 43 patients aged 5-48 years with VPI associated with cleft lip and/or palate who were assessed at a tertiary cleft palate unit between 2018 and 2021. VPI was diagnosed through the integration of perceptual speech assessment and findings obtained by flexible nasopharyngoscopy. VPCPs were classified according to the Skolnick and Croft criteria. Associations between categorical variables were analyzed using exact tests when low expected cell frequencies precluded reliable use of Pearson's chi-square test. Cramer's V was reported as a measure of effect size. Results Isolated cleft palate was the most frequent phenotype (41.9%), followed by cleft lip and palate (32.6%), submucous cleft palate (23.3%), and labioalveolar cleft (2.3%). A genetic or syndromic diagnosis was identified in 34.9% of patients, with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome being the most frequent diagnosis. The coronal VPCP predominated (44.2%). Conclusions In this retrospective single-center cohort, cleft phenotype was associated with genetic or syndromic classification and nasal septal deviation, whereas the coronal pattern was the most frequent VPCP. These exploratory findings emphasize the need for standardized prospective documentation of VPI severity, anatomical findings, and functional speech characteristics before these relationships can be adequately examined in larger multicenter cohorts. Clinical relevance Integrated characterization of cleft phenotype, velopharyngeal closure pattern, associated nasal anatomy, and genetic or syndromic classification may contribute to a more comprehensive interdisciplinary assessment. The findings of the present study do not establish causal relationships or support specific surgical or speech-language pathology treatment recommendations.

items.title: Respiratory Infections at Mass Gatherings: A Travel-Medicine Review with Hajj and Umrah as a Longitudinal Case Study.
items.abstract: Mass gatherings combine international mobility with dense, repeated contact and can amplify respiratory infections across travel corridors. Hajj, Umrah and Kumbh Mela, offer a uniquely recurrent case study, while other religious or sporting mega-events, and music or cultural festivals provide contrasting exposure systems. A focused narrative review was conducted of peer-reviewed studies, systematic and scoping reviews, and authoritative public-health guidance. Searches and project evidence synthesis prioritized publications from January 2021 to August 2026, with selected foundational sources. We examined respiratory symptoms, laboratory detections, clinical disease, vaccination, antimicrobial use and resistance, surveillance, environmental modifiers, and pre-, during-, and post-travel practice. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias scoring was undertaken. Respiratory risk is determined less by attendance alone than by contact intensity, duration, ventilation, vocalization, shared accommodation, traveler susceptibility, and pathogen circulation. Recent Hajj evidence confirms a substantial burden of respiratory symptoms and clinical consultations, but estimates vary because denominators range from volunteers and tested samples to healthcare encounters. Rhinovirus, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and bacterial pneumonia remain important. There is continued abuse of antibiotics for predominantly viral syndromes and acquisition of resistant organisms link individual care to global antimicrobial resistance. Syndromic, laboratory, event-based, genomic, and wastewater surveillance are complementary, not interchangeable. Heat, dust, air quality, fatigue, and differential access to protective infrastructure modify respiratory symptoms, severity, and care seeking. Comparative events share mechanisms but not directly transferable rates. Travel-medicine practice should treat mass gatherings as longitudinal exposure systems spanning preparation, transport, the event, and return. Layered vaccination, risk-based masking, ventilation and crowd-flow measures, prompt diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and explicit travel histories, can reduce respiratory morbidity while preserving denominator discipline and access to protective infrastructure.

items.title: Needle phobia: confronting a neglected factor in travel vaccine hesitancy.
items.abstract: Patients with needle phobia present with disproportionate fear, anxiety, or avoidance of needles that can disrupt access to healthcare services. Needle phobia creates a barrier to public health measures including travel vaccine uptake. This narrative review analyses these challenges by examining the psychological, sociocultural, and clinical determinants of needle phobia and how they can be addressed in travel medicine practice. The literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. Only articles published in English were included, with a focus on work published in the last 10 years to align with advancements in vaccine technology and psychological interventions for needle phobia. Key data extracted from studies included population characteristics, prevalence and severity of needle phobia, intervention strategies, vaccine hesitancy trends, and emerging vaccine technologies. Individuals with needle phobia are twice as likely to be vaccine hesitant as non-phobic individuals. Needle phobia often originates from a learned fear response, with 62-81% beginning in childhood, decreases with age, and has a higher prevalence among females (up to two-fold). Prior fainting is more than twice as common in travellers who fear injections (16.5% vs 6.9%). Therapeutic support includes pain management techniques that minimise the physical and psychological discomfort associated with vaccination, distraction interventions, graduated exposure therapy, and applied tension that counteracts vasovagal syncope by using muscle tension techniques. Non-injection vaccine modalities such as oral, intranasal, and microarray patch vaccines may alleviate needle phobia and enhance vaccine compliance. Advances in vaccination technology have the potential to revolutionise how vaccines are administered in travel medicine practice. Needle phobia represents a significant and often overlooked barrier to vaccine uptake. Addressing this issue requires the integration of both clinical and psychological interventions, along with the adoption of promising technological advancements in vaccine delivery.

items.title: How older adults express loneliness in everyday life: a qualitative content analysis.
items.abstract: Loneliness among older adults is a significant public health concern, associated with mental and physical health outcomes. Although loneliness is widely studied, less is known about how older adults' express loneliness in everyday language. Understanding these expressions is important for improving screening instruments and communication strategies. The aim of this study is to describe how older adults express their everyday experiences of loneliness. A descriptive qualitative design was employed using semi-structured face-to-face interviews with 16 community-dwelling older adults aged 80 years and above living in Sweden. Participants were purposively sampled from a national panel study based on prior reports of loneliness. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using inductive manifest content analysis. The analysis focused on the words and phrases that the participants used when they talked about loneliness. An overarching theme of difficulty in expressing loneliness was identified. Three main categories described how loneliness was expressed: (1) Feelings of loneliness, including descriptions of unpleasant emotions, varying intensity, and fluctuation over time (2). Indirect expressions of loneliness, where participants described loneliness through experiences such as boredom, slowness, emptiness, or through reactions to loneliness such as shame, and resignation (3). Relational expressions, where loneliness was framed in terms of missing social contact, lack of meaningful relationships, and perceived separation from others. Older adults often express loneliness indirectly, using language that reflects their experiences without explicitly labeling them as loneliness. Approaches that only rely on direct questions of loneliness may therefore overlook older adults who express their negative experience without explicitly naming loneliness. Incorporating indirect expressions into screening, communication, and intervention strategies may improve the detection and support of loneliness in older populations.

items.title: Climate Change Adaptaion Strategies And Biodiversity Conservation In Himachal Pradesh
items.abstract: Himachal Pradesh stands at a critical juncture where rapid development and climate pressures threaten its rich biodiversity. The state, positioned as a front-runner in India’s ecological policy experiments, has pursued innovative green energy agendas, community-driven conservation, and ambitious habitat protection measures. Despite this, however, a number of persistent issues such as habitat fragmentation, unregulated tourism, human-wildlife conflict, and disruptions brought about by climatic changes keep destabilizing the area’s fragile ecosystems. This paper examines some of the recent trends within environmental law, state policy measures, and civil society activism, their implications for conservation and sustainability. Much emphasis will be laid on emerging conservation measures such as the Green Energy State program, decentralization of renewable energy through solar panchayats, and resilience against climate change in forestry management. Through the assessment of these current challenges and emerging conservation measures, the importance of an integrated and multidisciplinary approach will become evident.

items.title: How to survive as mountain dwellers: palaeopathological study of European leopards
items.abstract: Abstract Previous morphofunctional analyses linked Pleistocene leopards from the eastern Pyrenees to rocky mountainous habitats, within a broader interpretation of European leopard ecology. Such environments are expected to increase exposure to falls, missteps and difficult landings during locomotion and prey capture. Here we develop the palaeopathological dimension of this interpretation by examining two pathological leopard ( Panthera pardus ) forelimb elements from Late Pleistocene European cave assemblages: a radius from Grotte de la Carrière, France, and a fifth metacarpal from Tut de Fustanyà, Iberia. External morphology and computed-tomography images reveal pronounced diaphyseal enlargement, irregular periosteal bone formation, cortical reorganization and persistent deformation, most consistent with remodeled fractures. Substantial reparative bone documents survival beyond the acute injury and through an extended phase of osseous repair. Comparisons with pathological leopards, lynxes, cave lions and saber-toothed felids support the diagnostic assessment and place these injuries within a broader record of skeletal trauma. We propose that the fractures reflect the mechanical risks of locomotion and hunting in steep, rocky terrain. The pathological evidence adds an individual life-history dimension to the postcranial adaptations previously recognized in European leopards. Integrating the lesions with the morphological and environmental evidence, we interpret them as potential traumatic consequences of the mountain-associated way of life proposed for European Pleistocene leopards. Their extensive repair also documents the capacity of injured individuals to survive within this demanding ecological setting.

items.title: The Forecasting Proficiency Test: A General Use Assessment of Forecasting Ability
items.abstract: Accurate predictions about the future are crucial for optimizing policy choices, but finding skilled forecasters is challenging. Prior work relied on forecasting tournaments to identify generalist "superforecasters" who made accurate predictions across domains, but these tournaments take months to complete and require large concurrent samples to compare performance among individuals. We solve these problems by developing a one-hour Forecasting Proficiency Test (FPT) that explains 75% of the variance in forecasters' accuracy about a wide variety of events. The FPT provides standardized percentile scores normed to a large (N=1,147) test development sample based on a combination of reusable real-world forecasting questions and standalone cognitive tests. Which questions and tests are included is highly customizable. Forecasting questions are the best predictors of forecasting proficiency, but cognitive tests help stabilize score distributions and facilitate score exchangeability across different custom test versions even as forecasting questions and resolution dates change. The FPT is primarily a practical tool for decision-makers who rely on accurate predictions to make decisions. However, it is based on one of the largest dedicated psychometric studies ever conducted on human forecasting, which also provides insight into the cognitive mechanisms that drive forecasting proficiency and guidance for future researchers interested in studying the psychology of forecasting.

items.title: Measuring Cognitive Demands in Professional Esports
items.abstract: Practice may improve certain cognitive skills more than others because those skills are called upon more frequently during an activity. Professional esports provides a means of measuring these demands during gameplay because match records capture the information available to players and their responses as events unfold. This study introduces the Telemetry and Replay Analysis of Cognitive Exposure (TRACE) framework, which measures seven dimensions of cognitive demand in professional esports. The analysis used records from 314 professional DOTA 2 matches, covering 558 distinct player accounts and approximately 2,184 player-hours of competition. TRACE defines four measures at the player level (cognitive control capacity, task switching, inhibitory control, and dynamic attention) and three measures at the team level (visuospatial working memory and updating, decision-making under uncertainty, and feedback learning). Hierarchical Bayesian models estimated each dimension in its original units and on a common percentile scale, accounting for differences among teams, matches, and hero-role combinations. By identifying comparable situations across matches, TRACE can quantify how often players encounter a given demand and how they respond when it arises. This transforms routinely recorded match replays into a source of large-scale behavioral data for cognitive psychology.

items.title: Introducing the One-Shot Download Task: Testing the validity of a new and simple measure of online pro-environmental behavior
items.abstract: AbstractMeasures of actual pro-environmental behaviour are increasingly in environmental psychology due to their increased ecological validity over self-report measures. Here we introduce a new such measure, the One-Shot Download Task (OSD), a brief online behavioural measure in which participants choose between incurring personal costs (completing a tedious task) or environmental costs (downloading unnecessary files associated with carbon emissions). Two studies were conducted (Study 1: N = 104; Study 2: N = 96) that assessed the OSD’s criterion validity by examining associations with measures of eco-anxiety, environmentally minded consumer behaviour and environmental attitudes, while Study 2 also tested whether social influence in the form of exposure to “watching eyes” stimuli increased pro-environmental choices in the task. It was found that OSD scores positively correlated with environmentally minded consumer behaviour and the Preservation dimension of environmental attitudes, but not with eco-anxiety or Utilization attitudes. Furthermore, participants exposed to watching eyes selected significantly more environmentally friendly options (higher scores on the OSD). These findings provide initial evidence for the validity of the OSD as a measure of actual pro-environmental behaviour, demonstrating expected relationships with established environmental constructs and sensitivity to social influence. Given its simplicity, low cost, and accessibility, the OSD offers a practical addition to the growing range of behavioural measures available to environmental psychological researchers, although further validation is warranted.

items.title: Perceived treatability is not evidence of diagnostic validity and benefit: A response to Hastings and Hahn on borderline personality disorder
items.abstract: Hastings and Hahn report that a borderline personality disorder (BPD) label can improve selected treatment beliefs among clinical psychology trainees. However, more favourable clinician expectations should not be interpreted as evidence that receiving the diagnosis benefits patients. Perceived treatability, treatment efficacy, treatment safety, and patient benefit are distinct constructs. This distinction is particularly important given documented negative effects associated with dialectical behaviour therapy and broader limitations in the systematic assessment and reporting of treatment-related harm in psychotherapy research. Hastings and Hahn's vignette design also presupposes rather than evaluates the legitimacy of the BPD construct and cannot address diagnostic bias, harms arising from classification, or the lived consequences of diagnosis and subsequent care. Their findings therefore demonstrate a change in selected clinician beliefs, not improved care or net patient benefit. Claims of diagnostic benefit require evidence addressing treatment safety, patient-defined outcomes, diagnostic validity and bias, and lived experience.

Claims of diagnostic benefit require evidence addressing treatment safety, patient-defined outcomes, diagnostic validity and bias, and lived experience.

items.title: TO MONETIZE OR NOT: INFLUENCE OF INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES AND GENDER IN MONETARY VALUATION OF MEANINGFUL EXPERIENCES
items.abstract: Money is a universal measure of value that influences most decisions. For centuries, humans have used it to exchange goods and experiences. Research in psychology and behavioral economics, however, shows that there may be limits to what individuals are willing to exchange for money. This study examined the monetary values people assign to personal experiences, and whether willingness to engage in monetary valuation differs between males and females. Five hundred and twenty-nine participants completed an online survey in which they provided the minimum amount of monetary compensation it would require to complete ten separate hypothetical scenarios, with the option to refuse any task. The hypothetical tasks ranged from temporary restrictions and social isolation to public disclosure, loss of memories and permanent identity changes. Based on the results from previous economic decision-making studies, we hypothesized that females would refuse to price tasks more than males and that males would request higher compensation for priced tasks. We also hypothesized that permanent or identity-altering tasks would result in higher refusal rates than temporary ones in both genders. Whether resistance to monetary valuation is a consistent individual tendency was also examined. Our results showed that participants who refused to price one hypothetical task were more likely to refuse other tasks. While no gender differences were observed for any task regarding the monetary value requested, females refused significantly more tasks than males (4.43 vs. 3.17, p < .001). Refusal rates were highest for permanent or identity-altering tasks and lowest for temporary tasks. Lastly, refusal rates for loss of digital pictures/videos were nearly identical to losing contact with friends and family. Together, these findings suggest that monetary valuation involves two separate decisions: whether or not to assign a monetary value and, if so, how much to request. Individuals differ consistently in their willingness to engage in monetary valuation, and gender influences the decision to engage rather than with the amount requested.

items.title: The Forecasting Proficiency Test: A General Use Assessment of Forecasting Ability
items.abstract: Accurate predictions about the future are crucial for optimizing policy choices, but finding skilled forecasters is challenging. Prior work relied on forecasting tournaments to identify generalist "superforecasters" who made accurate predictions across domains, but these tournaments take months to complete and require large concurrent samples to compare performance among individuals. We solve these problems by developing a one-hour Forecasting Proficiency Test (FPT) that explains 75% of the variance in forecasters' accuracy about a wide variety of events. The FPT provides standardized percentile scores normed to a large (N=1,147) test development sample based on a combination of reusable real-world forecasting questions and standalone cognitive tests. Which questions and tests are included is highly customizable. Forecasting questions are the best predictors of forecasting proficiency, but cognitive tests help stabilize score distributions and facilitate score exchangeability across different custom test versions even as forecasting questions and resolution dates change. The FPT is primarily a practical tool for decision-makers who rely on accurate predictions to make decisions. However, it is based on one of the largest dedicated psychometric studies ever conducted on human forecasting, which also provides insight into the cognitive mechanisms that drive forecasting proficiency and guidance for future researchers interested in studying the psychology of forecasting.

items.title: Navigating Safety in Reproductive Health Self-Care Interventions in Ghana: A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: IntroductionReproductive health self-care interventions are growing rapidly in Ghana, but there is limited evidence on the quality-of-care provisions that ensure safety for end-users and health professionals. This study explored how quality of care and safety are experienced and maintained within reproductive health self-care interventions in Ghana, using a self-care-specific conceptual framework.Materials and MethodsUsing an exploratory qualitative approach, underpinned by the Quality-of-Care Framework for Self-Care, we interviewed 29 end-users and 19 professionals, comprising health providers, program managers, digital referral agents, and community facilitators across Accra, Tamale, Cape Coast, and Sunyani. The study spanned six sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) domains: family planning, abortion, HIV/STI, maternal and child health, general SRHR, and cervical cancer. Data was analysed using thematic analysis techniques in Dedoose, grounded in both deductive and inductive principles.ResultsKey outcomes include the following: Technical Competency – Despite barriers, end-users felt sufficiently empowered to access self-care services. although professionals required continuous capacity strengthening to keep pace with the evolving ecosystem; Client Safety – End-users preferred access to medical eligibility information, but professionals were while professionals expressed concerns about potential misuse; Information Exchange – Information on family planning self-care services was more openly available than across other SRHR domains; Interpersonal Connection and Choice – End-users reported more positive experiences with remote services than facility-based care, although professionals faced operational constraints that affected consistent delivery of quality care; Continuity of Care – Follow-up care was better integrated across health facilities than alternate service delivery points, with periodic stockouts disrupting continuity efforts.ConclusionIn exploring how quality of care and safety are experienced and maintained within reproductive health self-care interventions in Ghana, this study found that end-users and professionals have adopted interim measures to maintain some level of safety amid policy and institutional inadequacies. However, the sustainability of these measures is uncertain, posing a serious risk to public health if not prioritised in the short term.

items.title: Predictors of knowledge of ticks, tick-borne diseases and engagement in protective behaviours: an analysis of survey data from England
items.abstract: BackgroundTicks pose a considerable threat to both animal and human health, with tick-borne diseases presenting substantial economic and public health burdens. Although engaging in protective behaviours can reduce the risk of tick bites, and subsequently disease risk, factors that are associated with uptake of such behaviours, and knowledge of ticks and tick-borne diseases, are underexplored within England. Method An online survey was conducted with 1,400 adults residing in England. Multiple linear regression analyses were performed for the outcomes of knowledge of ticks and tick-borne diseases, and engagement with protective behaviours. Results Participants had a mean knowledge score of 20 out of a possible 35 (57.14% correct responses), and participants engaged in fewer than two protective behaviours on average. Many participants provided ‘don’t know’ responses to questions, with 62.05% of participants providing at least one ‘don’t know’ response. Among those who had heard of ticks, knowledge of ticks was associated with higher perceived severity of disease, self-efficacy, social norms and self-reported knowledge. Engagement with protective behaviour was positively associated with belonging to a Black ethnic group, a suspected previous tick encounter, seeing or hearing information about ticks and higher knowledge about ticks and tick-borne diseases. There were no other sociodemographic factors associated with knowledge of ticks, or engagement in protective behaviours.ConclusionsThese findings provide insight into the factors associated with knowledge of ticks and engagement in protective behaviours in a sample of adults from England. However, these results also highlight that knowledge about ticks and tick-borne diseases is incomplete in the English population. Further work is needed to design and evaluate interventions aimed at increasing knowledge about ticks and TBDs and assess their impact on engagement in protective behaviours.

items.title: Rethinking Smartphones and Sleep: A Fine-Grained Within-Person Analysis of Evening Smartphone Use and Sleep
items.abstract: Inadequate sleep is a public health concern associated with adverse health and well-being outcomes. Evening smartphone use is frequently cited as a potential contributor, prompting widespread recommendations to avoid it. However, rigorous evidence to support these recommendations is limited. Using device-based smartphone use data and experience sampling data collected over 10 days, we examined within-person associations between evening smartphone use and five self-reported sleep-related outcomes: shuteye time, sleep latency, sleep duration, difficulty to fall asleep, and sleep quality. We examined these associations in two samples (N = 184 and N = 185) to test replicability. To investigate robustness and temporal dynamics, we assessed smartphone use across four equal-length time windows covering different segments of the evening. Across both samples and all time windows, greater-than-usual evening smartphone use was consistently associated with earlier shuteye time. Associations with the other sleep-related outcomes were less consistent, with most estimates indicating no significant relationship. Overall, our findings align with previous intensive longitudinal research that has likewise found little evidence of concerning associations between evening smartphone use and sleep. Our results challenge the assumption that evening smartphone use is inherently harmful to sleep and underscore the need to reconsider blanket recommendations to avoid it.

items.title: Spontaneous emergence of action decisions and slow ramping in a deep brain-constrained model of frontotemporal areas
items.abstract: Abstract Humans are capable of voluntarily initiating actions that are spontaneous—not triggered by any sensory event in the immediate context. In such cases, how does the brain make a decision that the time to act has come? To investigate this question, we used a 6-area brain-constrained neural-network model to account for the neurophysiological and anatomical features of relevant areas of the cortex. To replicate the experimental settings under which volitional non stimulus-triggered button-presses are performed, we analysed the network activity in the absence of any “sensory” input: we observed spontaneous ignitions of previously-learned “perception–action” circuits (linking “visual” information to corresponding “hand/finger movement”) caused by the accumulation of noise within them, which we took as model correlates of self-generated decisions to act. The time to first spontaneous circuit ignition was then used to build a simulated waiting-time histogram. We found that, for select values of the parameters, the network autonomously “decided” to act (or to wait) in a way that accurately reflected participant behaviour under such conditions. Additionally, we found that when the model’s macroscopic behaviour matched that of participants, its microscopic activity prior to a spontaneous ignition event also reproduced the pre-movement slow ramping neural signal (the readiness potential, or RP) experimentally recorded using electroencephalography. Reproducing both behavioural and brain indices of spontaneous voluntary movements, the present brain-constrained architecture offers a neuro-mechanistic explanation of the emergence of endogenous action decisions in the human brain in the form of memory traces’ spontaneous ignitions. Our results also speak to the ongoing debate over the interpretation of the RP, suggesting that, rather than reflecting motor preparation (a decision outcome), the emerging RP is pre-decisional, with overt movement being the result of a distributed perception–action circuit spontaneous ignition.

items.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
items.abstract: The integration of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) can be used to characterize temporal and spatial components of neural activity during unfolding mental experience. Here we introduce a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with measures of continuous behavior and spontaneous mental experience. Data components, organized in Brain Imaging Dataset Structure (BIDS) format, include fMRI, EEG with carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling ratings, and mental health surveys, from 24 healthy adults. Tasks included the gradual-onset continuous performance task and resting state with intermittent experience sampling of 13 unique thought dimensions (36 repetitions, including 468 total ratings, per participant). The same protocol was completed on two different days, yielding approximately 1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI data per individual. The dataset may be used to explore the behavioral and experiential relevance of brain activity during the wakeful resting state. The dataset also provides a means to study the reliability of relationships between fMRI and EEG features across sessions within individuals.

items.title: Cognitive networks reconstruct mindsets about STEM subjects and educational contexts in high-schoolers, undergraduates, experts and their digital twins
items.abstract: Attitudes toward STEM develop from the interaction of conceptual knowledge, educational experiences, and affect. Here we use cognitive network science to reconstruct group mindsets as behavioural forma mentis networks (BFMNs). In this case, nodes are cue words and free associations, edges are empirical associative links, and each concept is annotated with perceived valence. We analyse BFMNs from $$N=981$$ observations spanning high school students, university students, and early-career STEM experts, alongside LLM (GPT-OSS) “digital twins” (group-level synthetic counterparts, not individual-level copies), prompted to emulate comparable profiles. Focusing also on semantic neighbourhoods (“frames”) around key target concepts (e.g., STEM subjects or educational actors/places), we quantify frames in terms of valence auras, emotional profiles, network overlap (Jaccard similarity), and concreteness relative to null baselines. Across student groups, science and research are consistently framed positively, while their core quantitative subjects (mathematics and statistics) exhibit more negative and anxiety-related auras, amplified in higher math-anxiety subgroups, evidencing a STEM-science cognitive and emotional dissonance. High-anxiety frames are also less concrete than chance, suggesting more abstract and decontextualised representations of threatening quantitative domains. Human networks show greater overlap between mathematics and anxiety than GPT-OSS. The results highlight how BFMNs capture cognitive-affective signatures of mindsets towards the target domains and indicate that these synthetic counterparts approximate cultural attitudes but miss key context-sensitive, experience-based components of human educational anxiety.

items.title: The relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust among college students: a serial mediation model
items.abstract: Abstract Objective The present study sought to examine the relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust among a sample of college students, as well as the mediating roles of social support and psychological resilience in this relationship. Methods A questionnaire-based survey was conducted among 526 college students from several universities in Liaoning Province, China, of whom 504 valid questionnaires were retained for final analysis after data screening. The data were collected using the following instruments: the Physical Activity Rating Scale, the Interpersonal Trust Scale, the Perceived Social Support Scale, and the Psychological Resilience Scale. Statistical analyses were conducted to examine the relationships among variables and to test the proposed mediation model. Results The results demonstrated that: Results: (1) Physical exercise is positively correlated with college students’ interpersonal trust, and its direct predictive effect on interpersonal trust is weak but robust; (2) Physical exercise can positively predict social support and psychological resilience; (3) Social support can positively predict psychological resilience and college students’ interpersonal trust, and psychological resilience can also positively predict college students’ interpersonal trust; (4) Social support and psychological resilience play important mediating roles between physical exercise and college students’ interpersonal trust, with three mediating effect paths: physical exercise → social support → interpersonal trust; physical exercise → psychological resilience → interpersonal trust; physical exercise → social support → psychological resilience → interpersonal trust. Conclusions This study examined whether physical exercise was associated with interpersonal trust among college students. The results of the study support this hypothesis, with physical exercise demonstrating a weak but robust positive correlation with interpersonal trust among the sample of college students. The findings suggest that social support and psychological resilience independently mediate the relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust and also operate as a serial mediation pathway between the two.

items.title: Development of a Digital Violence Prevention E-Module to Strengthen Harmonious Social Interaction among Elementary School Students
items.abstract: Abstract Violence in elementary schools in Indonesia is still a serious problem that hinders student development. This research aims to develop an E-Mode of Violence Prevention Education designed to strengthen the harmonization of harmonious life in the elementary school environment. This study uses a 4D development model which includes the Define, Design, Develop and Disseminate stages which involve the validation of experts, teachers and students in four elementary schools in Gorontalo Regency. The results of expert validation show that the E-Module meets the criteria of "very valid" with an average score above 85%. The limited trial showed that more than 85% of students rated the E-Module as practical, easy to use, and attractive. Data analysis through the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test showed that the pretest and posttest data were normally distributed (Sig.>0.05). The results of the paired samples t-test showed significant differences in students' knowledge, attitudes, and skills before and after the use of the E-Module (p = 0.001). The effect size calculation (Cohen's d) ranged from 1.34–1.86 with a very large category, which confirms the strong influence of the E-Module in improving the competence of violence prevention. Thus, this E-Module is valid, practical, and effective, and is able to be widely implemented as part of creating harmonious harmony of life in the elementary school environment.

items.title: Listening and Mirroring: The Effects of Verbal Attunement and Behavioral Mimicry on Social and Empathic Perceptions of Embodied AI Agents in VR
items.abstract: As embodied agents take on increasingly social and relational roles in VR, visual realism and embodiment alone may be insufficient; users must also perceive these agents as emotionally attuned, supportive, and humanlike. Prior work suggests that verbal attunement and nonverbal mimicry can each improve users’ social evaluations of embodied agents. However, behavioral mimicry has largely been studied outside of real-time, conversational AI interactions, leaving limited understanding of how users respond when an agent simultaneously generates contextually responsive dialogue and adapts its nonverbal behavior during an immersive conversation. To address this gap, we developed an embodied AI counselor that combines conversational AI with real-time facial-expression and posture mimicry, while producing either verbally attuned or neutral responses. We evaluated the system in a 2 × 2 within-subjects study with 20 participants, manipulating verbal attunement and behavioral mimicry. Results showed that verbal attunement was the most reliable driver of perceived empathy. Behavioral mimicry showed a marginal relationship with perceived humanness, while greater mimicry exposure showed preliminary, exploratory positive associations with empathy, positivity, and humanness, particularly among female participants. Together, these findings show that multimodal synchrony is not a simple additive strategy for designing empathic conversational agents in VR and underscore the need to consider how verbal and nonverbal behaviors are combined during real-time interaction.

items.title: Game-Based versus Training-Based Virtual Reality for Cognitive Rehabilitation in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Dementia: A Systematization of Design Paradigms, Outcomes, and Evaluation Rigor
items.abstract: Therapeutic exercises play a crucial role in recovering from or slowing the cognitive decline in dementia. However, these processes are tedious and many patients give up before achieving desired benefits. Virtual Reality has evolved as an alternative to address this issue and it has two different paradigms in the rehabilitation process. The first one is a game-based approach that is designed to keep the participants engaged through enjoyable interactions. The second one provides a structured environment intended to facilitate functional recovery. A few prior studies have compared these paradigms in terms of clinical outcomes. The findings in the previous reviews are inconsistent. In addition, whether these labels identify systems that actually differ in design or delivery remains unexplored. Furthermore, whether these technological differences contribute to the inconsistencies found in the literature leaves an open question which should be investigated. This study addresses this gap in the literature. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematize 34 studies published between 2015 and 2026, including 16 controlled efficacy trials and 18 design and feasibility studies focused on mild cognitive impairment, dementia and Alzheimer’s disease. We initially built a taxonomy to classify each system according to design paradigm, immersion level, feedback modality, difficulty adaptation mechanisms and hardware. Our findings indicate that both game-based and training-based approaches exhibit some common characteristics, which made it challenging to clearly differentiate these paradigms on technological grounds. We further develop an evaluation framework, VR-RES, and apply it across existing studies. This framework highlights the limitations of previous work, particularly the tendency to neglect demographic factors such as age, sex, and education when analyzing the effectiveness of these paradigms. Finally, we outline a set of recommendations to guide future study design, evaluation and reporting practice.
