items.title: When It All Falls On the Physicians: A Qualitative Study of Physician Workforce Changes Post-Dobbs in Four States With Abortion Bans.
items.abstract: Objectives We aimed to explore how abortion bans in four highly restrictive states affected physician workforce dynamics among physicians of diverse specialties after the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision. Methods The Medical Integrity Initiative conducted in-depth interviews with physicians in Alabama, Idaho, Oklahoma, and Tennessee, states with strict abortion bans and severe legal penalties for physicians. Participants included specialists in emergency medicine, maternal-fetal medicine, medical genetics, obstetrics, oncology, and reproductive endocrinology and infertility. We used stratified and snowball sampling and conducted interviews via Zoom from July to October 2024. Grounded theory methodology informed the inductive approach to data analysis. We began with open (descriptive) coding and followed it with axial (interpretive) analysis. Results Thirty-two physicians across all specialties reported new challenges following the Dobbs decision. We identified the following overarching themes: 1) heightened liability concerns, 2) shifting burden of care onto academic hospitals, 3) added advocacy responsibilities, 4) emotional strain and ethical dilemma of leaving the state, and 5) increased challenges regarding workforce size and workload. Challenges that participants described included colleagues' exodus, difficulty recruiting providers and trainees, and labor and delivery unit closures. Many reported that they considered leaving their state. Participants expressed a desire for their institutions to support evidence-based clinical practice. Conclusion Physicians experienced changes in workforce composition and responsibilities following the Dobbs decision. Collective action and robust occupational, legal, and mental health support from their institutions and medical societies might enable physicians to safely stay and sustainably advocate in states with abortion bans.

items.title: Microbiota transplant therapy improves ulcerative colitis symptoms independent of donor engraftment in a pilot randomized placebo-controlled trial.
items.abstract: Background Several clinical trials have assessed microbiota transplant therapy (MTT) in ulcerative colitis (UC); however, none have assessed a standardized MTT product. We developed a standardized, oral, lyophilized MTT product and previously reported the primary endpoint of engraftment at week 12. Here, we assessed clinical outcomes and the association with donor engraftment. Methods A single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial of patients with UC with an endoscopic Mayo score ≥1, who received MTT or placebo for 8 weeks. Symptom and fecal assessments occurred at baseline and weeks 4, 8, and 12. Secondary outcomes included the partial Mayo score (pMS) and correlation to donor engraftment. Stool microbiota were assessed via 16S rRNA sequencing and donor engraftment measured using SourceTracker. Results Participants receiving MTT (n = 13) had significantly higher donor engraftment at all measured time points compared with placebo (n = 14). Compared with baseline symptoms, participants who received MTT had significantly lower pMS at weeks 4 and 8, while no significant changes in pMS were noted in those randomized to placebo. There was no correlation between donor engraftment and pMS or clinical response. There was no significant pattern in engrafting donor taxa in those that met the threshold of clinical response at week 4 vs participants that did not meet clinical response. Conclusions Daily dosing of encapsulated MTT for 8 weeks reduces symptoms of UC as measured by the pMS. However, donor engraftment did not correlate to pMS or clinical responses.NCT03948919, Fecal Transplant for Ulcerative Colitis, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03948919.

items.title: Tex11 mutant mouse models of human azoospermia.
items.abstract: Study question Do different patient TEX11 mutations lead to non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) when modeled in mice? Summary answer A frameshift mutation in Tex11 leads to azoospermia in mice (Tex11D); a missense mutation had no impact on fertility (Tex11A); and a splice site mutation caused reduced testis weights and sperm counts with variable sub-fertility (Tex11L). What is known already Half of all NOA cases are unexplained but may arise from unidentified genetic mutations. Several variants in TEX11 have been identified in men with NOA; and Tex11 knockout in mice causes NOA. Study design, size, duration For fertility analysis of the different mutations, the sample sizes were as follows: n = 3 wild-type controls; n = 5 Tex11D; n = 3 Tex11A; and n = 3 Tex11L. Wild-type males and hemizygous mutant male mice in each Tex11 line were bred with two to four different wild-type females for fertility analysis. At 12 weeks, testes and epidiymides were then collected for histological analysis and sperm counts. Additional Tex11L mice (n = 3) and wild-type controls (n = 3) were bred for 52 weeks with 2 new wild-type females every 2-3 weeks, then testes and epididymides were collected for further analysis. Testes and epididymides from Tex11L mice (n = 3 for wild type and mutants) were also collected at 24 and 36 weeks of age for histological analyses. Participants/materials, setting, methods TEX11 variants identified in male patients with NOA were introduced into the orthologous region of the mouse genome using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. Lines were expanded onto a DBA/2 background by breeding female heterozygous carriers to wild-type DBA/2 males. Hemizygous males from the third generation and beyond were used for fertility studies, gross tissue morphology, sperm counts, and histological analysis. Main results and the role of chance Compared to wild-type mice (145.0 ± 17.56 mg testis weight; 1.72 ± 0.50 million sperm/cauda epididymis; 6.42 ± 0.73 pups/breeding), Tex11D mice had reduced testis weight (28.33 ± 0.68 mg), no sperm in the epididymis, and were infertile with a maturation arrest testicular phenotype. We did not observe any spermatogenesis or fertility defects in Tex11A mice (145.0 mg ± 0 mg; 1.52 ± 0.11 million sperm/cauda; 5.83 ± 0.81 pups/breeding) compared to wild type. Tex11L mice had reduced testis weight (78.33 ± 16.41 mg) and reduced epididymal sperm counts (0.33 ± 0.13 million/cauda epididymis) but a variable fertility phenotype (5.42 ± 1.13 pups/breeding), with 2 out of 6 mice being subfertile. Tex11L mice also had variable testicular and epididymal defects, classified as mild or severe. Large scale data Not applicable for this study. Limitations, reasons for caution The sample sizes were limited for each mouse line. Wider implications of the findings Our study shows the importance of validating NOA-associated variants in a mouse model. Our data suggest that different TEX11 variants produce a variety of phenotypes which could impact genetic counselling of patients with NOA. Funding This study was supported by the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute for Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) grant HD096723 to A.N.Y. and K.E.O. G.R.A. was supported by NICHD grant HD114406. Disclosures K.E.O. was an advisor to Paterna Biosciences. The authors declare that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.

items.title: Nonlinear effect of serum sodium within 24 hours after brain tumor surgery on clinical outcomes: A prospective study.
items.abstract: Neurosurgical management of brain tumour patients includes the prompt recognition and individualized treatment of sodium disorders to optimize recovery. The study aimed to assess the effect of serum sodium within 24 hours after brain tumour surgery on clinical outcomes. Prospective study of 117 patients undergoing brain tumour surgery. The worst serum sodium value within 24 hours after surgery was recorded. Primary outcome was composite hospital mortality and readmission to the ICU. A generalized linear mixed model was used to assess the effect of serum sodium on the primary outcome. Neurosurgical procedures were supratentorial craniotomy (52.1%), infratentorial craniotomy (29.9%), and endoscopic endonasal surgery (17.9%). Hyperosmolar therapy was associated with higher serum sodium (p = 0.001). Serum sodium was significantly lower in patients with neurological complications than in those without complications (p = 0.008). In the quadratic regression model, serum sodium revealed a U-shaped relationship with ICU length of stay (p < 0.0001; adjusted R2 = 0.680) and a Ո-shaped relationship with FOUR score (p < 0.0001; adjusted R2 = 0.782). The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (19.7%). Serum sodium had a nonlinear relationship with the primary outcome (p = 0.014) in the multivariate generalized linear mixed model, with an inflexion point at 142.7 mmol/L. Serum sodium within 24 hours is associated with worse postoperative clinical outcomes and could be used as prognostic biomarker for patients after brain tumour surgery, but further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these results.

items.title: DEGORA: turning heterogeneous published DEG summaries into an inspectable gene-evidence atlas.
items.abstract: Published tables of differentially expressed genes (DEG tables) can support secondary transcriptomic analyses when expression matrices or variance estimates are unavailable, but they are not consistently deposited in public repositories. DEGORA converts curated DEG tables into a local database that links gene-level evidence to original studies. It standardizes gene identifiers, collapses related contrasts within studies so that each study contributes once, applies fixed heuristic quality weights, and ranks genes by cross-study support and directional concordance. An optional search module identifies potentially reusable tables. We evaluated DEGORA using four human transcriptional programs as positive-control benchmarks, each represented by 2 to 15 publication-level source units and by up to 20 after human microarray sources were added. DEG tables for three programs were generated from publicly available count matrices, whereas those for the fourth were obtained from the original publications. Using RNA-seq evidence, DEGORA recovered 93% of interferon, 59% of endoplasmic reticulum stress, 73% of heat-shock, and 85% of hypoxia markers among the top 100 ranked genes. In three confirmatory datasets, DEGORA showed no consistent ranking advantage over alternative methods applied to the same tables. The same workflow organized published Alzheimer's disease cohort evidence without recomputing differential expression. Across ten evaluated datasets, performance varied with how the input tables were generated. Overall, DEGORA organizes differential expression evidence at the study level and keeps every ranked gene linked to the publications, assays, and reported statistics behind it.

items.title: Accessibility of pharmacy services for southeastern U.S. college and university students.
items.abstract: Background College and university students are primarily emerging adults in a formative period, acquiring knowledge and skills to function independently. Emerging adults are underrepresented in studies evaluating social determinants of health (SDOH). Access to pharmacy services may be impeded by cost, class schedules, lack of prior experience interacting with the healthcare system, and barriers to transportation. In rural communities, these SDOH gaps are often exacerbated by a lack of public transit and provider shortages. On-campus pharmacy and health services aim to address some of these barriers to care, yet prescription abandonment rates are higher than those in the general population. Self-reported medication adherence rates are low, with only 53% of doses taken in one study. Pharmacists are trained and capable of addressing these concerns. While published survey data provides a snapshot of the types of services offered by on-campus pharmacies, the prevalence of these services remains unclear. Objectives To evaluate the visibility and accessibility of pharmacist-provided services on rural and non-rural college campuses. Methods This study evaluated accredited, residential 2- and 4-year undergraduate institutions in the southeastern United States from September 2025 to March 2026. Institutional websites and search engines were audited to assess student access to pharmacist-provided services, defined as an on-campus pharmacy or a publicized list of local off-campus pharmacies. Rurality was classified using the Federal Office of Rural Health Policy "Am I Rural?" tool. Chi-square tests compared the availability of pharmacist-provided services between rural and non-rural campuses. Results Of the 369 colleges and universities identified, 24.1% provided on-campus pharmacist-provided services or a listing of local pharmacies. There was a statistically significant difference between the accessibility and visibility of pharmacist-provided services on rural campuses (14.6%) compared to urban campuses (29.3%) (p = 0.002). Conclusion This study identified a disparity between accessibility and visibility of pharmacist-provided services between rural and non-rural institutions.

items.title: Impact of a multi-site, multidisciplinary self-measured blood pressure monitoring program.
items.abstract: Improving hypertension control is designated as a Healthy People 2030 Leading Health Indicator. Self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) monitoring programs can help fill care gaps for underserved patients, including patients in rural locations. Local community healthcare institutions can expand SMBP program access to people with transportation and telemedicine barriers. To quantify the effects of a multi-site, multidisciplinary SMBP monitoring program on participant blood pressure measurements in 11 rural, underserved counties. The MPower Consortium, a regional health improvement network, serves 11 Southeast Missouri counties through collaborations among community pharmacies, public health departments, non-profit organizations, Federally Qualified Health Centers, and behavioral health organizations. Following a successful pilot, a SMBP monitoring program was expanded across the consortium. This study evaluated the first year of the MPower Consortium SMBP monitoring program. The program included initial patient education and three follow-up visits conducted by Community Health Workers, pharmacists, and nursing professionals in 11 counties. Outcomes included change in blood pressure and percent of participants meeting hypertension treatment goals. There were 302 patients included in the intent-to-treat analysis. Mean systolic blood pressure decreased from 144.3±21.9 mmHg to 134.2±14.8 mmHg (p<0.001) and mean diastolic blood pressure decreased from 83.1±13.3 mmHg to 77.5±9.0 mmHg (p<0.001). There was a statistically significant increase in percent of participants meeting goal blood pressure (p=0.008). The ANOVA analysis was significant for decrease in systolic blood pressure at each visit (p<0.001). There was no significant difference in the average systolic blood pressure decrease between the intent-to-treat and per-protocol groups (p=0.85). This multisite, multidisciplinary SMBP monitoring program lowered blood pressures in patients in rural, underserved areas. This study demonstrates benefit of a collaborative SMBP monitoring program performed by a multidisciplinary group of local healthcare organizations in reaching a vulnerable population.

items.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation Has Coronary and Other Selective Health Benefits: Comprehensive Results from the VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL).
items.abstract: Background The VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL) is the only large-scale randomized trial of marine omega-3 fatty acid (n-3 FA) supplementation for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cancer in a general population unselected for elevated risk. This article provides an integrated overview of the results of the n-3 FA component and its ancillary studies. Methods VITAL is a completed nationwide, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2x2 factorial trial of n-3 FAs (1 g/day) and vitamin D 3 (2000 IU/day) for a median of 5.3 years for primary prevention of CVD and cancer among 25,871 U.S. men aged ≥50 and women aged ≥55 years. Ancillary studies investigated effects on heart failure, atrial fibrillation (AF), autoimmune disease, and other endpoints. Results Compared with placebo, the n-3 FA supplement did not significantly reduce the primary endpoint of major CVD events (hazard ratio [HR]=0.92 [95% confidence interval 0.80-1.06]) but did significantly reduce total myocardial infarction (MI; HR=0.72 [0.59-0.90]), fatal MI (HR=0.50 [0.26-0.97]), percutaneous coronary intervention (HR=0.78 [0.63-0.95]), and recurrent hospitalization for heart failure (HR=0.86 [0.74-0.998]). The intervention was not associated with AF risk. Supplemental n-3 FAs did not reduce total cancer incidence, other cancer endpoints, or all-cause mortality but was associated with significantly decreased risk of autoimmune disease (confirmed plus probable cases; HR=0.82 [0.68-0.99]). Effect modification by demographic, dietary, and clinical factors was observed for several endpoints, with greater benefits in Black participants and those with lower fish intake or cardiovascular risk factors, but with variable effects in women vs. men. Conclusion Supplemental n-3 FAs did not significantly reduce major CVD events or cancer but decreased multiple cardiac endpoints and autoimmune disease. Several factors modified treatment effects. Although the findings do not support routine n-3 FA supplementation among healthy adults for prevention of chronic disease, targeted supplementation of those with low fish intake and other select groups warrants consideration.

items.title: Azole resistance in Aspergillus series Nigri and possible link with environmental selection route.
items.abstract: Background Resistance to medical azoles has been well investigated in Aspergillus fumigatus, which is primarily driven by exposure to azole fungicides. Azole resistance selection in other Aspergillus species remains understudied. We investigated azole resistance selection in Aspergillus series Nigri. Methods 165 clinical series Nigri isolates were collected from Dutch and Belgian hospitals and 77 environmental isolates were obtained from air and other environmental sources, including known hotspots for azole resistance selection. Isolates were screened for resistance to medical azoles and selected fungicides using the EUCAST microbroth dilution reference method. Epidemiological cut-off values were used to identify non-wildtype isolates. All isolates were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, and global sequence databases were used for population genomic analyses. Clinical information was collected for azole-resistant isolates. Findings Aspergillus tubingensis was the dominant species lineage among the clinical isolates (120/165, 72·7%), whereas species of the A. niger lineage were more frequently identified in environmental samples (55/78, 70·5%). Overall A. tubingensis isolates showed higher minimum inhibitory concentrations than A. niger isolates; 27 clinical isolates (17·0%) showed a non-wildtype phenotype for medical azoles as well as 24 of 78 (30·8%) environmental isolates. Sequencing revealed a worldwide distribution of multiple clonal groups. Cross resistance between medical azoles and azole fungicides was observed in A. tubingensis lineage isolates, which were recovered from hotspots, air and patient samples. Pan-azole resistant A. tubingensis was recovered from five mould-active azole-naïve patients, including a patient with proven invasive aspergillosis. Interpretation Our study shows azole resistance in A. tubingensis lineage isolates and evidence that supports environmental resistance selection. Population genomics indicate a risk of global migration of resistant clones in A. tubingensis. Next to confirmative studies regarding black aspergilli, mycobiome analysis of hotspots are needed to identify potential selection of intrinsic or acquired resistant fungal species that may cause infections.

items.title: Emergencies at Sea: Sudden Death on Cruise Ships For the BELTRAN Study (BaskEtbaLl and soccer sTadiums: Registry on Automatic exterNal defibrillators).
items.abstract: Sudden death on cruise ships represents a rare but critical public health and medical concern, occurring in a uniquely resource-limited, geographically isolated environment, with delayed access to definitive hospital care. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the incidence, causes, circumstances, and response systems related to sudden death on cruise ships, and to examine the medical, logistical, legal, and public health frameworks relevant to these events. A literature search of PubMed, MEDLINE, and EMBASE was conducted using terms related to sudden death and cruise ships, with inclusion of English-language studies from 2010 to 2025. Results suggest that sudden death on cruise ships is rare, with reported mortality estimates of approximately 1.8 deaths per 100,000 cruise passengers. Research highlights that deaths occurring among passengers are predominantly due to natural causes, especially cardiovascular disease, including myocardial infarction and cardiac arrest. Factors such as delayed diagnosis, limited onboard diagnostic capacity, and barriers to timely evacuation have been noted to contribute to preventable mortality. However, deaths occurring among crew are predominantly due to traumatic deaths, particularly falls overboard, and suicide, which calls for increased safety measures and better mental health support for crew. Substantial variability remains in standards for onboard medical response, including accessibility of automated external defibrillator (AED) availability, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, and emergency preparedness. Overall, the findings highlight the need for stronger cardiac emergency protocols, broader AED deployment, enhanced crew training, improved telemedicine and medevac coordination, and regulatory frameworks to reduce preventable deaths at sea.

items.title: Using hip-worn accelerometer non-wear time to assess sleep duration and sleep midpoint.
items.abstract: We sought to validate non-wear time of accelerometers worn on the hip for all waking hours as an estimate of sleep duration and midpoint. If valid, this may allow research studies to leverage previously collected physical activity data for sleep research. In 2019-2023, 21,325 Cancer Prevention Study-3 participants (mean age 58 years, SD=9.8) were provided a hip-worn accelerometer and sleep diaries for a week. Time in bed (TIB) was defined as the duration of non-wear time between two consecutive wear days (e.g. wear on Monday and Tuesday correspond to Monday night sleep). A total of 17,855 participants had at least 3 weekday and 1 weekend sleep measurements. Bland-Altman plots compared TIB and midpoint calculated from accelerometer non-wear and from sleep diaries. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated for TIB to assess convergent validity, and a Two One-Sided Test (TOST) was calculated for midpoint to assess equivalence (± 15 minutes). Participants were mostly non-Hispanic white (87%) and female (77%). On average, TIB was 41.1 (SD=44.6) minutes longer on weekdays (r = 0.72) and 41.3 (SD=61.0) minutes longer on weekend days (r = 0.67) compared to sleep diary. Accelerometry sleep midpoint was 1.3 minutes earlier compared to diary on weekdays and 1.6 minutes later on weekends (TOST p-value < 0.01). TIB calculated from non-wear time of hip accelerometry demonstrated convergent validity with sleep duration assessed from sleep diary. Midpoint based on non-wear time was equivalent to sleep diary.

items.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics enhance the environmental persistence and toxic effects of chlortetracycline by inhibiting its photodegradation.
items.abstract: Beyond their effects on fate of antibiotics in aquatic environments, nanoplastics (NPs) can also influence photodegradation and biological hazards of antibiotics, which remain poorly understood. This study demonstrated that PS NPs can suppress chlortetracycline (CTC) photodegradation, with decreasing photodegradation rate constant from 0.0132 to 0.0110 min ‒1 . In detail, the PS NPs inhibited direct photodegradation pathway of CTC via light-shielding effects and inhibitory effect of PS-DOM, while concurrently promote indirect photodegradation through reactive species generated (eg., O 2 •- , •OH, 1 O 2 and 3 PS*). Accordingly, the PS NPs yielded distinct transformation products, some of which exhibited toxicity significantly exceeding that of the parent compound, thereby causing severe toxicity effects, as manifested by growth inhibition and elevated intracellular ROS levels toward E. coli. Notably, such suppression of CTC photodegradation by PS NPs was also observed in different natural waters, where it was even more pronounced, as reflected by photodegradation rate constant decreasing from 0.0132 to 0.0052 min ‒1 . Consequently, the PS NPs could significantly enhance both the environmental persistence and toxic effects of CTC in natural waters, thereby aggravating its ecological risks. Ultimately, this study suggests that the coexistence and combined effects of nanoplastics should be carefully considered when assessing the fate and ecological risks of antibiotics in aquatic environments.

items.title: Time-series modelling and forecasting of acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) in the Gaza Strip before and during the war in October 2023.
items.abstract: Objectives This study aims to evaluate the temporal consistency and plausibility of manually collected data on acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) consultations reported by UNRWA staff based in Gaza and Cairo relative to the historical surveillance baseline. Further, the study aims to show the impact of the war in the Gaza Strip that began in October 2023 and the massive forced displacement of the Gaza population from Rafah governorate on the shape of the AWD curve. Study design We used epidemiological modelling with time-series analysis and forecasting. Methods Negative Binomial Regression was chosen based on the results of over-dispersion test. We obtained data prior to the war from UNRWA's electronic health system, while the health team (HT) collected data during the war manually during the war, and the Gaza office in Cairo audited them. We used October 7, 2023, and the Rafah mass incursion in late May (Epidemiological week 22) as cut-off points for forecasting. Results The regression model showed good reliability in trend prediction, though confidence declined during the war. Decomposition revealed a hump-shaped trend between 2023 and 2025, with descriptive seasonality and notable white noise. The model adequately addressed overdispersion in the weekly counts but did not completely capture their short-term temporal correlation. The outbreak prediction model showed an exponential rise in cases at the onset of the war. Forecasts exhibited similar trends between observed and predicted data before and after the cut-off points. Conclusions The analysis supports the accuracy and credibility of the reported data during the catastrophic humanitarian conditions and acknowledges the efforts of UNRWA Gaza HT. Time series analysis is a robust method for evaluating and interpreting humanitarian data.

items.title: Quadriceps and hamstring tendon autografts show similar clinical outcomes but distinct strength-recovery profiles after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Importance Graft choice remains a central controversy in primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). Quadriceps tendon (QT) and hamstring tendon (HT) autografts may provided similar clinical outcomes but differ in donor-site morbidity and postoperative strength recovery. Objective To determine whether QT and HT autografts differ in patient-reported outcomes, knee stability, functional performance, strength recovery, donor-site morbidity, and safety after primary ACLR. Evidence review PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from inception to March 17, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) directly comparing QT and HT autografts. The protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261340928). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MDs) or standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. No external funding was received. Findings Fifteen RCTs involving 936 participants were included, with 470 participants receiving QT autografts and 466 receiving HT autografts. Mean ages ranged from 18.7 to 32.7 years, and most studies reported follow-up at 12 or 24 months. At 24 months, no statistically significant differences were detected between QT and HT autografts in IKDC score (MD = -1.19; 95% CI, -3.84 to 1.47; p = 0.38), Lysholm score (MD = 1.42; 95% CI, -0.60 to 3.45; p = 0.17), or Tegner score (MD = -0.15; 95% CI, -0.70 to 0.39; p = 0.58). At the final available follow-up, graft failure occurred in 12 of 265 participants (4.5%) in the QT group and 11 of 261 participants (4.2%) in the HT group, without a statistically significant difference (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.49 to 2.48; p = 0.81). Overall adverse events also showed no statistically significant difference (RR = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.45 to 1.11; p = 0.13). QT autografts were associated with lower donor-site morbidity scores at 24 months (MD = -4.62; 95% CI, -9.21 to -0.03; p = 0.048), although this secondary finding was based on two trials. Knee stability, range of motion, return-to-sport, and hop-test outcomes showed no consistent differences. At 12 months, HT autografts were associated with relatively greater quadriceps strength symmetry, whereas QT autografts were associated with relatively greater hamstring strength symmetry and higher hamstring-to-quadriceps (H/Q) strength ratios. - conclusion and relevance QT and HT autografts produced similar patient-reported, stability, return-to-sport, and safety outcomes after primary ACLR but demonstrated distinct graft-specific strength-recovery profiles. These findings support individualized graft selection rather than consistent clinical superiority of either graft. Level of evidence Level II, systematic review, and meta-analysis of RCTs.

items.title: Preparing nurse scientists to translate evidence into policy impact.
items.abstract: Background Nurse scientists generate evidence that could meaningfully shape health policy, yet many nurse scientists are not explicitly prepared to translate research into policy impact. Purpose and methods This invited paper builds on the authors' keynote presentation at the 2025 State of the Science Conference on Preparing Nurse Scientists to Create Policy Change. Using examples from nursing science and the lead author's career trajectory, we discuss strategies for translating evidence into policy impact and introduce career cartography as a framework for intentionally building careers that advance such impact. Throughout, we use the term policy impact to refer broadly to the ways evidence influences agendas, decision-making, implementation efforts, organizational practices, public discourse, and legislation. Stakeholder engagement refers to meaningful involvement of individuals and groups affected by an issue, as well as those positioned to act on the evidence, including community members, practitioners, organizational leaders, advocates, and policymakers. Discussion Nurse scientists can increase their potential for policy impact by intentionally aligning training, research, relationships, and dissemination activities with long-term policy goals. Seeking experiences in policy, advocacy, community, and interdisciplinary settings can strengthen the skills, relationships, and confidence needed to translate evidence into policy impact. Career Cartography provides a framework for identifying and leveraging these opportunities throughout a career. Conclusion Preparing nurse scientists for policy impact requires intentional career mapping, stakeholder engagement, and communication strategies that position evidence to inform policy and practice.

items.title: The impact of temperature variation on the incidence of cardiovascular diseases in hypertensive populations: Evidence from CHARLS and the UK biobank.
items.abstract: Hypertension is the most prevalent chronic disease. The link between temperature changes and cardiovascular disease incidence in hypertensive populations is not well understood. To explore how temperature fluctuations affect cardiovascular disease incidence in hypertensive populations and identify the most impacted cardiovascular diseases. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and the UK Biobank, which provide long-term follow-up information on hypertensive patients, we applied logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards regression models to analyze the relationship between temperature and cardiovascular disease occurrence. In CHARLS (2011-2020), 4321 hypertensive individuals were studied, with 1079 developing cardiovascular diseases. A significant positive correlation was found between annual average daily temperature difference and cardiovascular disease incidence (OR: 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, P < 0.001). In the UK Biobank, 30,551 participants were followed for an average of 12.4 years, with 3611 diagnosed with cardiovascular diseases. Those exposed to alternating cold and hot temperatures had a higher risk of cardiovascular events (HR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.09-1.29, P < 0.001). Specifically, heart failure (HR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.21-1.73, P < 0.001), multivalvular disease (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.04-1.68, P < 0.05), and chronic ischemic heart disease (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.28, P < 0.05) were associated with such temperature exposure. Our study highlights the need to enhance cardiovascular disease monitoring and management in hypertensive populations under varying temperatures, which is crucial for disease prevention and control.

items.title: Developmental pathways of online grooming victimisation: Understanding adolescent vulnerability.
items.abstract: Adolescents increasingly engage with digital environments as a central part of their daily lives. While digital environments offer valuable opportunities, they also expose young users to risks, such as online grooming, a manipulative process in which adults build deceptive relationships with minors for sexual exploitation. Recent policy debates in Europe have reignited concern over the need to regulate adolescents' Internet use, especially given their developmental vulnerabilities. This study aimed to identify psychological, behavioural, relational, and contextual factors associated with online grooming victimisation in adolescents and to explore how these vulnerabilities vary across developmental stages, informing prevention strategies. Data were collected from 240 Portuguese adolescents aged 12-19 in schools in Porto, Portugal. A quantitative cross-sectional design was used. Online grooming victimisation was coded as a dichotomous outcome based on reported grooming-related experiences. Individual, relational, behavioural, and victimisation factors were analysed. Descriptive analyses, group comparisons, and binary logistic regression models were conducted for the overall sample and separately by developmental group. Three predictors of online grooming victimisation emerged: risky online behaviours (OR = 1.21; 95% CI[1.10, 1.33]; p < .001), gender (OR = 2.49; 95% CI[1.22, 5.06]; p = .012), and (cyber)bullying (OR = 2.21; 95% CI[1.19, 4.10]; p = .012). Age-stratified models showed developmentally contingent vulnerability: early adolescence involved behavioural exposure, experiences of (cyber)bullying, and gendered vulnerability, whereas in later adolescence, risk was associated with risky online behaviours. Prevention should adopt age-sensitive approaches addressing behavioural exposure, victimisation, and gendered vulnerability.

items.title: A practical evaluation of finite-sample BOIN calibration and Bayesian smoothing in phase I dose finding.
items.abstract: We evaluated an asymmetric loss-based BOIN boundary and a monotone Bernstein estimator. The boundary preserved lookup-table operation but did not improve correct selection uniformly in seven monotone scenarios. It reduced overdose selection relative to BOIN, aBOIN, and gBOINS in six. Its accuracy depended on MTD position and overdose aversion. Bernstein selection reduced accuracy in most scenarios, especially for middle and high MTDs. Reference MCMC showed that importance-sampling error did not explain these losses. Target-based elimination eventually removes a repeatedly sampled MTD when toxicity exceeds the target. An upper-equivalence-bound threshold avoids this asymptotic conflict but not finite-sample elimination. Standard BOIN should remain the default. The loss-based boundary is justified only when the protocol prespecifies overdose avoidance and calibration shows an acceptable tradeoff. The Bernstein estimator is not recommended in its present form.

items.title: Recent Advancements in Bio-Derived Fuels: Technological Pathways and Data-Driven Intelligence.
items.abstract: Bio-derived fuel refers to biofuels produced from organic materials originating from biomass or biowaste, industrial byproducts, municipal wastes, and animal effluents. To date, no single technology utilizes biomass and biowaste effectively to maximize bioenergy generation, as these technologies are at varying levels of technical and economic maturity. This review critically compares direct combustion, pyrolysis, transesterification, fermentation, and anaerobic digestion, together with mechanical, physicochemical, chemical, and biological pretreatment methods. Technologies of converting biomass and biowaste into bioenergy were critically evaluated based on conversion efficiency, processing time, energy density, emissions, technological maturity, and economic feasibility. Conventional and modern technologies for bio-derived fuels were reviewed in terms of processing time, energy density, emissions, and cost. Biorefinery and bio-derived fuel properties were compared with those of non-renewable fuels. The review highlights advanced approaches for process optimization, bioreactor stability, and bio-product improvement. Integrated biorefineries capable of co-processing multi-biomass and biowaste represent key future opportunities for producing multiple fuels and value-added co-products.

items.title: Immune system challenges posed by Brucella : mechanisms of evasion and immune provocation.
items.abstract: Brucella spp. are stealthy intracellular Gram-negative zoonotic bacteria triggering brucellosis in humans and animals worldwide. These pathogens have evolved robust mechanisms to colonize hosts, withstand immune attack, escape clearance, and sustain long-term survival and transmission. Their full infection cycle depends on dual capacities to evade and reprogramme host immunity, creating a balanced state between host immune control and bacterial persistence. Recent research reveals diverse immune cell populations responding to infection and continuous shifts of bacterial intracellular niches over disease progression. A core pathogenic trait of Brucella spp. is weakly immunogenic pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), notably its unusual lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Unlike LPS from enteric bacteria, this molecule triggers mild, delayed inflammation, enabling unnoticeable early bacterial proliferation. The VirB type IV secretion system (T4SS) secretes numerous protein and lipid effectors to reshape macrophage physiology and suppress protective immunity. Still, the stage and cell-reservoir-specific functions of these virulence factors remain poorly defined. This review traces the complete Brucella spp. infection cascade: mucosal invasion, early immune camouflage, intracellular compartment remodelling, systemic immune suppression, impaired adaptive immunity, chronic tissue reservoir formation, and disease relapse. We address how concurrent immune evasion and mild inflammatory stimulation support persistent infection, summarize latest research progress and unresolved questions, and translate these mechanistic findings into practical applications. These include refined diagnostic tools, DIVA vaccines, host-targeted therapeutics, combined antibiotic-immunomodulator regimens, and integrated One Health interventions for brucellosis control.

items.title: Children in contact with security units in Türkiye: a nationwide forensic analysis of victimization and delinquency patterns.
items.abstract: Children's interaction with security units reflects both victimization and delinquency, representing a critical forensic medicine and public health concern. Concurrent national analyses addressing both dimensions remain scarce in Türkiye. This study aimed to evaluate children in contact with security units in Türkiye using national data, focusing on admission reasons, demographic characteristics, victimization types, and offense patterns. This descriptive study used publicly available TÜİK data on "Children Brought to Security Units, 2024," covering 2020-2024. Variables included admission reason, sex, age group, victimization types, and alleged offenses. Results were presented as numbers and percentages. In 2024, a total of 612,651 registered contacts/cases involving children were recorded at security units; 66.6% were male and 33.4% female. Victimization was the leading admission reason (45.6%), followed by delinquency-related contacts (33.1%). Most cases involved the 15-17 age group. Delinquency-related contacts were markedly higher among boys, while girls were more represented in certain victimization types. Injury, sexual crimes, and migrant smuggling were the most prevalent victimization categories, with sexual crimes disproportionately affecting girls. Among alleged delinquent contacts, injury (40.4%) and theft (16.6%) were leading offenses. Substance-related offenses were notable among boys. Registered delinquency-related contacts increased by 80.8% between 2020 and 2024, a trend that may partly reflect changes in reporting, registration, or enforcement practices. Children's contact with security units is shaped by victimization and delinquency, with clear age and sex variations. Forensic medicine specialists play a critical role in medicolegal evaluation and prevention. Gender-sensitive, age-specific, and multidisciplinary strategies are urgently needed.

items.title: Probiotic-Mediated Mitigation of Metal(loid)-Induced Toxicity: Mechanisms, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Translation.
items.abstract: Heavy metal(loid)s contamination remains a major environmental and public health concern because toxic metal(loid)s such as lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, and chromium are persistent, non-biodegradable, and bioaccumulative. Chronic exposure disrupts cellular homeostasis through oxidative stress, enzyme inhibition, genotoxicity, inflammatory signalling, and gut microbiota dysbiosis, thereby contributing to multi organ injury and chronic disease. Conventional detoxification approaches, particularly chelation therapy, are constrained by limited specificity, adverse effects, and poor suitability for long-term low-dose exposure. In this context, probiotics have emerged as promising biological agents for mitigating metal(loid)s-induced toxicity. This review summarises current evidence from mechanistic studies, in vitro experiments, animal models, and human trials regarding the protective role of probiotics against metal(loid)s toxicity. Probiotics reduce metal(loid)s bioavailability through biosorption, bioaccumulation, and biotransformation, while also strengthening intestinal barrier integrity, restoring microbial balance, suppressing inflammation, and enhancing antioxidant defence pathways, especially Nrf2-mediated responses. Selected preclinical studies report reductions in tissue metal(loid) accumulation and attenuation of oxidative, inflammatory, and histopathological injury; however, these effects are strain- and exposure-dependent, and the limited human evidence does not establish consistent clinical detoxification efficacy. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains limited by strain-specific variability, non-standardised dosing, inter-individual heterogeneity, and the scarcity of large-scale randomised trials. Overall, selected probiotic strains show potential as adjunct interventions for mitigating metal(loid)-associated toxicity; however, their clinical efficacy, strain-specific safety, optimal dosing, and long-term tolerability remain insufficiently established, particularly in vulnerable populations. Rigorous clinical evaluation is therefore essential before therapeutic or preventive implementation.

items.title: Dietary Clostridium butyricum NCU-02 and Its Postbiotic Butyrate Ameliorate Autism Spectrum Disorder-like Symptoms: Involvement of Hippocampal Oxidative Stress Modulation.
items.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition closely linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, yet effective dietary interventions remain limited. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Clostridium butyricum NCU-02, a probiotic candidate, and its sterile supernatant in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced mouse model of ASD, with emphasis on their postbiotic properties. Both treatments significantly ameliorated core ASD-like behaviors, attenuating repetitive marble-burying by over 35% and restoring social novelty preference to near-control levels (p < 0.05 for both). These interventions were associated with improved intestinal barrier integrity, upregulated tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and occludin), and suppressed colonic and hippocampal pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Metabolomics profiling identified butyrate as a key differential metabolite, with butyrate levels elevated by approximately 1.3- to 2.5-fold following interventions (all p < 0.05 vs. M group). Correlation analyses further linked butyrate elevation to activation of the hippocampal GPR109A/AMPK/Nrf2 pathway and reduction of oxidative stress markers. Collectively, these findings suggest that C. butyricum NCU-02 and its sterile supernatant are associated with protective effects against ASD-like symptoms, and that the postbiotic metabolite butyrate may contribute to these benefits through dual modulation of gut homeostasis and neuroprotective signaling. A sodium-butyrate comparison group reproduced several of these effects, indicating that exogenous butyrate is sufficient to reproduce several of these effects, although the present design does not establish butyrate as a necessary mediator for the live-strain effects. These findings position butyrate, and butyrate-producing probiotics, as promising candidates for dietary intervention in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Manganese exposure in women of the Kosi-Seemanchal Region, Bihar, India: insights from drinking water, diet and biological fluids.
items.abstract: Manganese (Mn) is an essential trace element that becomes neurotoxic at elevated exposure levels. Geogenic Mn contamination in groundwater is an emerging public health concern in the Gangetic and Kosi-river plain region of Bihar, India. Lactating women and their breastfed infants are particularly the most vulnerable group, as Mn is absorbed through drinking water and food in their body which are transferred into their breast milk. The present study aims to determine Mn concentrations in household drinking water sources, staple dietary sources and biological fluids (such as blood, breast milk and urine) among lactating women of the Kosi-Seemanchal region of Bihar. It was a cross-sectional study involving 100 lactating females (aged 16-46 years) across five districts of the Kosi-Seemanchal region (Madhepura, Saharsa, Supaul, Bhagalpur and Katihar). Samples of blood, breast milk, urine, household groundwater and staple foods (rice, wheat and pulses) were obtained from each participant, with manganese content subsequently determined through Graphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (GF-AAS). Groundwater Mn exceeded the reference limit (100 µg/L) in 78% of samples (range 6.54-3318.0 µg/L). Among biological fluids, 27% of blood samples exceeded 15 µg/L (range 14.92-2232.0 µg/L), 21% of breast milk samples exceeded 18 µg/L (range 57.06-3634.0 µg/L) and 30% of urine samples exceeded 8 µg/L (range 11.64-5448.0 µg/L). In contrast, the food crops cultivated in this area, such as wheat, pulse and rice samples, remained within their respective permissible dietary limits. Groundwater, rather than diet, is the predominant Mn exposure pathway for breastfeeding females in the Kosi-Seemanchal region of Bihar. The detection of elevated Mn in a substantial proportion of breast milk samples raises concern for secondary exposure in breastfed infants, underscoring the need for groundwater remediation and continued biomonitoring in this population.

items.title: Association between screen-detected health-related social needs and nonadherence to endocrine therapy in patients with nonmetastatic breast cancer: an observational study.
items.abstract: Endocrine therapy (ET) reduces recurrence and improves survival in patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer (BC), yet many patients are nonadherent. The impact of health-related social needs (HRSN) on ET nonadherence remains poorly understood. We extracted electronic health record data on patients with nonmetastatic BC followed at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia University Irving Medical Center. Patients were eligible if they were adults, prescribed ET, and screened for HRSN (food insecurity, housing instability, transportation needs). ET nonadherence during the 6 months after HRSN screening was determined using proportion of days covered (PDC), with PDC < 80% considered nonadherent. Logistic regression models estimated associations between each HRSN and ET nonadherence, adjusting for demographics, BC characteristics, medication count, and comorbidities. We identified 960 eligible BC patients between January 2022 and October 2024 (median age 67 [IQR 58-75] years, 99% female, 12% Black, 41% Hispanic, 38% non-English speaking, 67% publicly insured, 63% stage 0-I BC, 18% tamoxifen use, 13% chemotherapy use, 80% prescribed ≥ 3 medications). Overall, 275 (29%) patients were nonadherent to ET; 15% reported food insecurity, 10% housing instability, and 6% transportation needs. In adjusted analyses, housing instability (OR 1.97, 95% CI 1.11-3.46, p = 0.02) and transportation needs (OR 3.43, 95% CI 1.69-7.07, p < 0.01), but not food insecurity (OR 1.40, 95% CI 0.89-2.19, p = 0.15) were significantly associated with ET nonadherence. Housing instability and transportation needs were independently associated with higher odds of ET nonadherence in our sample. Screening for and addressing HRSN may represent an effective strategy for improving ET adherence and cancer-related outcomes.

items.title: Systemic cytokine profiling reveals distinct pro-inflammatory signatures of arboviruses infections.
items.abstract: Arboviruses are a growing public health concern in tropical regions, where dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and oropouche virus (OROV) frequently co-circulate and cause overlapping clinical manifestations. In this study, we characterised the systemic inflammatory response by quantifying 12 cytokines and chemokines using a multiplex immunoassay in 163 patients with laboratory-confirmed acute arboviral infection: DENV1 (n = 28) and DENV2 (n = 39) patients without warning signs, CHIKV (n = 42) and OROV (n = 54). Thirty-one healthy controls (HC, n = 31) were also included. Clinically, arthralgia was the only feature that reliably distinguished the infections, occurring in 57.1% of CHIKV patients compared with 7.4-30.8% in the other groups, whereas fever, headache and myalgia overlapped substantially across all four. Immunologically, OROV induced a selective response with elevated IL-18 and CCL2/MCP-1 alongside reduced IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-23 and IL-17 A; DENV1 and DENV2 elicited broad activation of pro-inflammatory and antiviral mediators, with DENV1 engaging a wider range of cytokines than DENV2; and CHIKV elevated IFN-α2, IFN-γ, IL-18, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and IL-17 A. Cytokine network analysis revealed virus-specific patterns of immune connectivity, with OROV showing the most coordinated cytokines and chemokine response and CHIKV the most fragmented. Circulating cytokine concentrations were largely independent of viral load across all viruses, indicating that systemic inflammation during acute arboviral infection is driven primarily by host immune activation rather than by viral replication kinetics. These findings establish distinct immunological signatures for DENV, CHIKV, and OROV that may support differential diagnosis and inform the development of pathogen-specific therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Changes in functional capacity, flexibility and depressive symptoms in women with breast cancer submitted to adjuvant radiotherapy: randomized controlled clinical trial with mat pilates.
items.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the impact of Mat Pilates on functional capacity, flexibility, and depressive symptoms in women diagnosed with breast cancer who received adjuvant radiotherapy. Methods In this randomized clinical trial, 164 women with breast cancer (stages 0-III), aged 18 years or older, were randomized, and 156 were included in the analyses (79 in the Mat Pilates group and 77 in the control group). Handgrip strength, functional exercise capacity assessed by the 2-Minute Step Test (2MST), flexibility, and depressive symptoms were evaluated at baseline, at the end of radiotherapy (RT), and at 30 days, 3 months, and 6 months after RT. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to analyze functional capacity and flexibility, while the cumulative incidence of new depressive symptoms was estimated among participants without depressive symptoms at baseline. Results No significant group × time interactions were observed for handgrip strength (Wald χ 2 = 7.834; df = 4; p = 0.098), the 2-Minute Step Test (Wald χ 2 = 6.877; df = 4; p = 0.143), or flexibility (Wald χ 2 = 3.728; df = 4; p = 0.444). During the RT period, the cumulative of new depressive symptoms was 14.8%. Conclusion Functional capacity and flexibility improved over time, but their trajectories did not differ significantly between the Mat Pilates and control groups. No significant between-group difference was observed in the cumulative incidence of new depressive symptoms.

items.title: Between promise and guidance: a systematic review of normative documents on polygenic risk scores in healthcare contexts.
items.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) have shown increasing predictive value for several common complex diseases and generated expectations regarding their potential clinical and public health applications. Despite growing research and translational initiatives, PRS have yet to be integrated into routine clinical practice. The limited uptake of PRS has been linked to scientific limitations and a lack of clear guidance. More recently, the emergence of professional and policy documents addressing PRS points to an evolving normative landscape that warrants careful consideration. To this end, we conducted a systematic review of normative documents addressing the prospective use of PRS in healthcare contexts, including clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and policy reports issued by professional societies, regulatory bodies, and healthcare institutions. Searches were conducted across major biomedical and policy databases, complemented by grey literature sources and targeted website searches. Twenty-six documents met the inclusion criteria. None explicitly endorsed the routine implementation of PRS in healthcare at present. Most adopted cautious positions, citing limited evidence of clinical utility, concerns about transferability, and ethical risks. Substantial variation was observed in scope and degree of prescriptivity. While broad agreement existed on general best practices-such as defining test purpose, integrating PRS with other risk factors, and ensuring appropriate counsel​ing-guidance was often non-prescriptive, leaving key implementation thresholds and value commitments implicit. The findings highlight an emerging but fragmented normative landscape in which guidance has not yet globally translated into clear, action-guiding standards for clinical practice and implementation in healthcare. Clarifying how evidence, value commitments, and responsibilities translate into statements is essential to inform ongoing and future deliberations on the responsible use and implementation of PRS.

items.title: Association between Brain Amyloid Status and Cognitive and Physical Performance in Older Adults with Frailty Criteria: Longitudinal Data from the CogFrail Study.
items.abstract: Background The impact of cerebral amyloid pathology on cognitive and functional decline may differ with age. Evidence linking brain amyloidopathy to physical decline remains limited and inconsistent. This study investigated the association between brain amyloid status and cognitive and physical decline in (pre)frail older adults with cognitive impairment. Methods This longitudinal analysis used data from the CogFrail study. Brain amyloid pathology was assessed using amyloid-positron emission tomography (visual reading). Linear mixed-effects models examined differences over a two-year follow-up between amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative participants in cognitive, functional, and physical trajectories. Cognitive and functional outcomes included the Mini-Mental State Examination, the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes, the Activities of Daily Living Index, and a neuropsychological battery, while the physical domain was assessed using handgrip strength, chair rise time, gait speed, and the Short Physical Performance Battery. Results Among 199 participants (mean age 82.3 ± 4.8 years; 65.3% women), 108(54.3%) were amyloid-positive. Amyloid-positive participants experienced greater decline in the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (β = 0.30, 95% CI 0.10-0.49; p = 0.003, log-transformed) and the Mini-Mental State Examination (β = -1.62, 95% CI -2.74 to -0.49; p = 0.005). No significant longitudinal differences were observed between groups in the Activities of Daily Living Index, neuropsychological outcomes, or physical performance measures. Conclusion Amyloid pathology assessment may help differentiate cognitive trajectories in cognitively impaired (pre)frail older adults. Greater cognitive decline in amyloid-positive participants was not associated with greater loss of independence or additional physical decline over time. Trial registration NCT03129269.

items.title: Association between clinician-rated oral mucositis severity and oral mucositis-specific quality of life: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the association between clinician-rated oral mucositis (OM) severity and oral mucositis-specific quality of life (OMQoL) in adults undergoing antineoplastic therapy or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Methods This cross-sectional study included 56 adults undergoing chemotherapy, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or head and neck radiotherapy with or without concurrent systemic chemotherapy at a Brazilian public university hospital. OM was assessed clinically according to the World Health Organization (WHO) grading scale, and oral mucositis specific quality of life (OMQoL) was assessed using the shortened Brazilian version of the questionnaire, comprising four domains: Diet, Symptoms, Social Functioning, and Swallowing. Associations between WHO grades and OMQoL scores were analyzed using non-parametric tests. Descriptive and bivariate analyses (Mann-Whitney and Kruskal-Wallis tests) was performed to evaluate associations between clinical variables and QoL scores (p Results Among the 56 participants, 32 (57.1%) were female, and the mean age was 51 years. WHO grades 3 and 4 were observed in 29 participants (51.8%). OMQoL scores differed significantly according to WHO grade across all domains (p = 0.001), with mean total scores ranging from 24.36 among participants with grade 0 OM to 48.67 among those with grade 4 OM. Female participants had higher OMQoL scores in the Diet domain (p = 0.023), although this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. Age and diagnostic category were not significantly associated with OMQoL scores. The sensitivity analysis excluding patients with non-malignant hematologic disease yielded similar findings. Conclusion Higher clinician-rated WHO grades of OM were associated with poorer OM-specific quality of life in this sample. The association was particularly relevant for domains related to diet, symptoms, social functioning, and swallowing. Because WHO grading incorporates functional criteria related to oral intake, the observed associations should be interpreted considering the partial overlap between clinician-rated OM severity and patient-reported functional impairment. Longitudinal studies are warranted to clarify temporal relationships between OM severity and quality of life.

items.title: From Consumption to Harm: Socioeconomic Inequalities and Recovery Models in Addiction.
items.abstract: Introduction Socioeconomic inequalities shape substance use (SU) and treatment utilisation across Europe. However, substance-use prevalence and treatment admissions may show different socioeconomic distributions. Spain offers a valuable setting to examine these regional patterns using national data sources. Methods We conducted an ecological, cross-sectional analysis across the 17 Spanish autonomous communities, integrating data on SU, treatment admissions, income and mental health indicators (2022-2024). Socioeconomic inequalities were quantified using the slope index of inequality and the concentration index. Ordinary least-squares models assessed associations between income and SU prevalence or treatment admission rates, and spatial autocorrelation was evaluated. Results Alcohol use in the past 30 days showed a positive income gradient (slope index of inequality 6.29 percentage points; +1.25 percentage points per €1,000; p<0.001), as did cannabis use in the past 12 months. In contrast, daily tobacco smoking was more prevalent in lower-income regions. More than 70% of publicly recorded SUD treatment admissions occurred in regions within the lowest-income terciles, and treatment-admission rates decreased by 8.9 admissions per 100,000 inhabitants for each €1,000 increase in income (p=0.015). Significant but weak negative spatial autocorrelation was observed. Conclusion Spain shows opposing socioeconomic gradients in regional substance-use prevalence and publicly recorded treatment admissions. Alcohol and cannabis use were more common in higher-income regions, whereas treatment-admission rates were higher in lower-income regions. These population-level patterns should be interpreted cautiously because public surveillance does not comprehensively capture private-sector treatment.

items.title: Cultural Adaptation of an Intervention Guide for a Non-pharmacological Palliative Care Intervention for People With Advanced Dementia: A Multi-Stakeholder Process Preparatory to the International In-Touch Trial.
items.abstract: Effective, internationally transferable interventions for people with advanced dementia are needed to enhance consistent, high-quality care and quality of life. The international In-Touch project includes a cluster randomised controlled trial of an intervention to improve the quality of life for people with advanced dementia within nursing homes. A structured cultural adaptation process is crucial to ensure the In-Touch intervention retains core principles while improving local feasibility and acceptability, thereby enabling a clear assessment of fidelity. Here, we detail the cultural adaptation of the 'In-Touch Practical Guide for Nursing Home Staff' to enhance its feasibility, usability, and relevance across nursing homes in seven European countries. A structured cultural adaptation process, inspired by the ADAPT framework, was guided by an international team of experts, including individuals with lived experience, and dementia and palliative care researchers. Within-country group interviews were conducted in the Czech Republic, Ireland, Italy, Poland, Portugal, the Netherlands and the UK with three key participant groups: (1) nursing home staff familiar with intervention components, (2) nursing home staff unfamiliar with the intervention, and (3) family carers of people with advanced dementia. Participants ( n = 97) evaluated the guide's clarity, cultural appropriateness, and feasibility. Cross-country consensus is presented here, with key themes including the need to simplify the guide to improve usability, ensure accessible language for all staff levels, and introduce discussion of flexibility in session length, structure, and available spaces to align with nursing home routines. Clearer guidance was needed on the roles of volunteers and family members. The guide was refined into a single, adaptable version, optimising its cultural relevance, usability, and practicality across diverse European settings. This collaborative adaptation process led to a culturally sensitive guide optimised for use in the In-Touch trial across Europe. The outlined methods can help adapt other interventions for future international palliative care research.

items.title: Non-inferiority of nurse-led Consultation compared to physician-led consultation in pre-Travel Medicine: results of the aCTIVE trial.
items.abstract: Background The pre-travel consultation is an important public health prevention measure with steadily increasing demand. Given the limited number of physicians, nurse involvement is key to meeting this demand, but few studies have evaluated it. This study aimed to assess whether a nurse-led pre-travel consultation could provide health information of comparable quality to a physician-led consultation. Methods The aCTIVE study was a prospective, single-blind, monocentric, randomised non-inferiority trial comparing travel medicine consultations led by a physician versus a trained travel nurse at Avicenne University Hospital (Bobigny, France). Eligible participants were adult travelers without significant comorbidities, immunodeficiency, recent hospitalisation, recent-onset medical conditions, pregnancy, or acute illness. The primary endpoint was short-term information retention. Results Between September 2017 and March 2019, 600 travelers were randomly assigned to a pre-travel consultation led by a physician (n=300) or a trained nurse (n=300). Mean memorisation score was 68.5% ± 18.7 (nurse) vs 63.9% ± 19.8 (physician); mean difference 4.57% (95% CI 0.97 to 8.17), confirming non-inferiority (margin -10%) and superiority for nurse-led consultations (p=0.01). Traveler satisfaction was non-inferior (1.93 ± 0.26 vs 1.94 ± 0.23; difference -0.01, 95% CI -0.05 to 0.03). The quality-of-care score was higher with nurses (14.4 ± 1.4 vs 14.1 ± 1.6; difference 0.35, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.58), confirming both non-inferiority and superiority. Prescription adequacy was non-inferior (98.7 ± 9.8 vs 98.5 ± 9.0; difference 0.17, 95% CI -1.47 to 1.82), as was vaccination appropriateness (98.54% vs 98.37%; difference 0.2%, 95% CI -1.80 to 2.15). Conclusion For healthy travelers, pre-travel consultation performed by a nurse was non-inferior to a consultation performed by a doctor.

items.title: Occupational impact and support needs following suicide loss: A scoping review.
items.abstract: BackgroundSuicide bereavement can profoundly affect occupational functioning, yet evidence on workplace experiences, support needs, and organizational responses remains fragmented.ObjectiveThis scoping review mapped the literature on the occupational impact of suicide loss across personal and professional contexts, including perceived support needs, workplace or psychosocial responses, and associated psychosocial and occupational outcomes.MethodsThe review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, PsycINFO, BASE, and CORE. Eligible studies examined work-related experiences or workplace responses following suicide loss among personally bereaved individuals or professionals affected by the suicide of a colleague, client, patient, or student. Findings were synthesized descriptively and thematically.ResultsFourteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Six themes were identified: occupational disruption; silence and pressure to continue working; blame, scrutiny, and stigma; unmet support needs; informal and self-initiated support; and limited and unstructured postvention responses. Across settings, suicide loss was associated with impaired concentration, emotional dysregulation, reduced confidence, altered professional practice, absenteeism, and, in some cases, withdrawal from work or non-employment. Support was often informal, relying on peers, colleagues, family, or self-initiated coping, while formal organizational responses were frequently absent, generic, or poorly matched to workers' needs.ConclusionsSuicide loss should be recognized as both a bereavement and an occupational issue, requiring suicide-informed, context-sensitive workplace support and postvention strategies across diverse occupational, professional, and organizational settings.

items.title: Infant Linear Anthropometry at 6 Months Following Maternal Moringa oleifera -Royal Jelly Compared With Multiple Micronutrient Supplementation: A Follow-Up Study With Exploratory Gut Microbiota Analyses.
items.abstract: BackgroundMaternal nutrition during pregnancy may influence infant growth, while the developing gut microbiota may represent an additional biological correlate of early-life nutritional status. Evidence comparing food-based maternal supplementation with multiple micronutrient supplementation (MMS) in relation to infant linear anthropometry remains limited.ObjectiveTo compare 6-month linear anthropometric outcomes between maternal Moringa oleifera enriched with royal jelly (MRJ) and MMS groups and to explore associations between selected gut bacteria and length-for-age z-score (LAZ).MethodsThis 6-month follow-up included 88 infants (MRJ, n = 42; MMS, n = 46) from a randomized maternal supplementation trial. Infant length and LAZ were compared using linear regression, with additional adjustment for birth length. Stunting was examined descriptively. Five prespecified bacterial genera were quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, and their associations with LAZ were explored using multivariable regression.ResultsAfter adjustment for birth length, no significant differences were observed between MRJ and MMS in infant length (β = -0.24 cm; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.35 to 0.87; P = .66) or LAZ (β = 0.11; 95% CI, -0.36 to 0.59; P = .64). Stunting occurred in 4.8% and 15.2% of infants, respectively. Higher Clostridium (β = -0.114; P = .02) and Lactobacillus (β = -0.163; P = .03) abundances were associated with lower LAZ in adjusted exploratory analyses.ConclusionsLinear anthropometric outcomes at 6 months did not differ significantly between the MRJ and MMS groups. Higher Clostridium and Lactobacillus abundances were cross-sectionally associated with lower LAZ and require confirmation in longitudinal studies.

items.title: Progress on Dengue Vaccines: A Comprehensive Review of Current and Emerging Vaccines.
items.abstract: The global burden of dengue virus continues to increase, driven by environmental changes, urban growth, and the widespread dissemination of Aedes mosquito vectors. Developing an effective dengue vaccine remains challenging because it must provide long-lasting, balanced immunity against each of the four circulating serotypes without increasing the risk of immune-mediated disease enhancement upon exposure to a different serotype. This review article summarizes current understanding of dengue immunopathogenesis, highlights the limitations of first-generation, live-attenuated vaccines, and explores how preexisting serostatus, efficacy across serotypes, and safety considerations affect vaccine implementation. We also review emerging vaccine platforms, including site-directed attenuation, heterologous prime-boost strategies, and mRNA, DNA, and peptide vaccines. Advances in antigen engineering, together with improved diagnostics and surveillance, will be essential to overcoming existing immunologic and implementation barriers. Ongoing innovation, equitable access, and public trust remain critical to achieving effective global dengue control.

items.title: Pharmacological modulation of the striatal mGluR5-NR2B association attenuates L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia in 6-OHDA lesioned parkinsonian rats.
items.abstract: Objective: The clinical utility of L-DOPA is severely limited by the development of L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID). Although metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) antagonists alleviate LID, the underlying molecular mechanisms, particularly those involving striatal glutamate receptor crosstalk, remain incompletely understood. Methods: Adult female Sprague-Dawley rats with unilateral 6-OHDA lesions were randomized into Sham, PD, LID, MTEP, and MK-801 groups (n=6/group). L-DOPA/benserazide was given twice daily for 14 days, with MTEP or MK-801 30 min before each dose. AIMs, open-field activity, striatal mGluR5-NR2B co-immunoprecipitation, PKC/MEK/ERK phosphorylation, and c-fos/Pdyn mRNA were assessed. Behavioral and molecular data were analyzed by mixed models, ANOVA, or Kruskal-Wallis tests. Results: We observed aberrant elevation of the mGluR5-NR2B interactions in the striatum of 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-lesioned parkinsonian rats exhibiting LID. Administration of the mGluR5 antagonist MTEP or the NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 reduced the co-immunoprecipitated association, reduced the synaptic association of mGluR5 with NR2B, and markedly attenuated LID severity. Mechanistically, the decoupling of these receptors was accompanied by decreased ERK1/2 phosphorylation, reduced PKC protein expression, and decreased L-DOPA-induced c-fos and prodynorphin mRNA levels. Furthermore, abnormal involuntary movement (AIM) scores significantly correlated with the extent of NR2B-mGluR5 interaction and downstream signaling activation. These findings suggest that increased mGluR5-NR2B association is associated with LID and may contribute to its expression. Conclusion: The therapeutic efficacy of MTEP or MK-801 is likely mediated by reducing this receptor interaction and downstream signaling, highlighting a potential molecular target for LID treatment.

items.title: Cohabiting microbes can impact one another's mutation rates creating a mutational eco-evo feedback loop
items.abstract: Eco-evolutionary feedbacks are typically thought to require an ecological change driving Darwinian selection. However, ecology can drive other evolutionary mechanisms too. In many microbial species mutation rates are elevated at low population density, mediated by nutrient availability and reactive oxygen species (ROS). These findings from monoculture populations led us to hypothesise that the presence and density of a cohabiting species will also affect mutation rates. Using Escherichia coli as a focal species we explore the mutational effects on both parties of co-culture with either Enterococcus faecalis or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These species co-occur in multiple clinical settings and have different abilities to degrade ROS. In both co-culture systems we find evidence that the presence of a stronger ROS degrader reduces mutation rates in the weaker ROS degrading species. At the same time increasing population density of the weaker ROS degrader increases mutation rates in the stronger ROS degrading species. Simultaneous mutation rate estimation in co-cultured species raises multiple experimental challenges addressed here. Despite these challenges, we find evidence for a novel form of eco-evo feedback in which the environment shapes the supply of mutational variation to the population. This in turn feeds back to alter the chance of evolutionary rescue for one species or another during a subsequent environmental change. Such effects potentially matter not only for our fundamental understanding of the interplay between ecology and evolution, but for the treatment of polymicrobial infections in which rates of resistance evolution may be altered by the cross-species mutational effects of cohabiting species.

items.title: Seed dispersal in a Landscape of Fear: a review of rodent foraging decisions under predation risk.
items.abstract: Rodents play a dual role in plant regeneration, acting both as seed predators and dispersers. Their foraging decisions are shaped by the trade-off between food acquisition and predation risk, a dynamic conceptualized within the Landscape of Fear framework. Despite numerous studies, the role of perceived predation risk across the multiple stages of rodent-mediated seed dispersal remains poorly understood. We reviewed 168 studies to investigate how risk perception influences rodents' foraging behaviour and the consequences for seed dispersal. We identified five major take-home messages. (1) The influence of perceived predation risk has been investigated unevenly across the seed dispersal process, with foraging site selection being the best-understood stage; (2) perceived predation risk can be easily manipulated, facilitating the interpretation of small mammals behavioural responses; (3) rodents mainly modify their decisions according to indirect cues of predation risk (e.g., vegetation cover and illumination), whereas direct cues have weaker and more variable effects; (4) outcomes of seed selection under predation risk are inconsistent, reporting both species-specific feeding habits and context-dependent strategies; (5) the majority of studies lacked individual identification of animals, potentially undermining data independence and possibly introducing bias. We argue that future research should adopt experimental designs that simultaneously address risk perception (and the various factors affecting it) and seed dispersal (across its multiple stages), as well as incorporating individual-level predictors. Such approaches are crucial to elucidate how fear shapes the outcome of rodent-plant interaction and, ultimately, ecosystem functioning.
