items.title: Testing a secondary motor integration account of confidence computation.
items.abstract: A growing body of empirical evidence suggests that confidence judgments are modulated by action-related cues, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Recent decision-making models propose that the evidence accumulation variable is continuously transmitted to the motor system, allowing motor plans to evolve in parallel with decision formation. At the motor level, a secondary leaky integration process acts as a filter that regulates the speed-accuracy tradeoff: the stronger the filter, the slower and more accurate the responses. Here, we tested whether action-related effects on confidence are mediated by this secondary motor integration process. We manipulated sensory noise using a doubly stochastic random dot motion task and varied the motor-level filter via speed-accuracy instructions. We reasoned that the positive effect of sensory noise on confidence observed in previous studies should be attenuated by stronger filtering in the accuracy condition compared to the speed condition. However, we found strong empirical evidence against this qualitative prediction. Computational modeling further revealed that the predicted attenuation was extremely small and that confidence predictions based on secondary motor integration offered no advantage over those based on evidence accumulation. Together, these results show that confidence need not be computed from secondary motor integration to account for the observed pattern.

items.title: Spatial organization of heterogeneities in the striatum.
items.abstract: The striatum is usually described through a binary taxonomy of D1/D2 spiny projection neurons and coarse basal ganglia pathways supporting action selection and reinforcement learning. Yet the striatum is also a recurrent inhibitory network with strong neuromodulatory control, and its cellular and synaptic properties are not uniformly distributed. Spatial transcriptomics reveal continuous gradients in gene expression across striatal territory, superimposed on the discrete striosome-matrix division. Other studies report that intrinsic properties (such as excitability), inhibitory interneuron abundance and neuromodulatory fields (e.g. terminal distribution, clearance kinetics, receptor expression) vary in space. These spatially structured heterogeneities seem to align with striatal topographic input and output maps, suggesting that its computation cannot be uniformly distributed as well. We propose that the striatum is best understood as a spatial dynamical field, meaning that neighboring striatal microcircuits have similar but not identical dynamical properties and these position-dependent parameters shape network dynamics affecting integration, competition, and plasticity differently in the striatal tissue.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Disease-Free Survival in Breast Cancer Incorporating Clinical and Treatment Information: Retrospective Cohort Study With External Validation.
items.abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer in women, and postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) is an important indicator of long-term prognosis. However, tumor, node, metastasis staging has limited ability to integrate multidimensional clinical, pathological, and treatment-related factors for individualized DFS prediction. Therefore, machine learning (ML) may provide a more comprehensive approach to prognostic risk assessment. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a ML-based model for predicting postoperative DFS in patients with breast cancer. This retrospective study included 2 cohorts: 1231 patients treated at an institutional center between 2012 and 2020 and 304 patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). The institutional cohort was divided into model development (n=861) and internal validation (n=370) sets, while the TCGA cohort served as an external validation cohort. Five ML algorithms were evaluated, with the Cox proportional hazards model additionally fitted as a conventional statistical reference. Model performance was assessed using the concordance index and time-dependent area under the curve (AUC). The net reclassification index and integrated discrimination improvement were used for comparative evaluation. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to assess predictor contributions, and patients were stratified into risk groups according to the median predicted risk score. Based on a comprehensive evaluation of model performance, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) with an accelerated failure time (AFT) was selected as the final model. The study included 1231 institutional patients, with 861 used for model development and 370 for internal validation, and 304 patients from TCGA for external validation. The 5-year time-dependent AUCs were 0.840, 0.822, and 0.762 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In the external validation cohort, the XGBoost (AFT) model achieved a concordance index of 0.750 (95% CI 0.654-0.843), with 3-, 5-, and 8-year AUCs of 0.791, 0.762, and 0.768, respectively. At 5 years, compared with Cox regression, XGBoost (AFT) showed improved reclassification (net reclassification index=0.311, 95% CI 0.172-0.458; P=.01; integrated discrimination improvement=0.166, 95% CI 0.095-0.235; P<.001). SHAP analysis identified endocrine therapy, pT, pN, lymph node ratio, Ki-67, and chemotherapy among the major contributors to model predictions. Risk stratification based on the median predicted risk score separated patients into groups with distinct DFS outcomes (hazard ratio 5.44, 95% CI 4.04-7.31). The ML-based model demonstrated favorable performance and external generalizability in predicting postoperative DFS. SHAP analysis provided interpretability for the model, and risk stratification identified patient subgroups with distinct prognostic risks.

items.title: Self-Reported Clinician Confidence in and Familiarity With Long COVID Care Following Continuing Medical Education Webinars: Unmatched Pre-Post Study.
items.abstract: An estimated 18-23 million Americans have had long COVID (LC), yet 54% and 72% of US physicians reported not being confident in diagnosing and treating LC, respectively. Continuing medical education (CME) is crucial to maintaining and improving clinical skills, and CME that incorporates need-based educational methods is associated with improved patient outcomes. Given limited clinician familiarity with LC, there is a need for an effective, widely accessible LC CME program. This study assessed the effectiveness of 2 Stanford University-organized LC CME webinars, which aimed to provide comprehensive, up-to-date evaluation and management strategies through multidisciplinary didactic presentations and question-and-answer sessions. Data from webinar attendees were collected through CME registration and prewebinar/postwebinar surveys. Registration surveys consisted of multiple-choice questions on profession, practice setting, experience treating vulnerable populations, and perception of LC. Prewebinar/postwebinar surveys consisted of multiple-choice questions on perception of LC, confidence in diagnosing LC, and familiarity with LC care. Prewebinar/postwebinar responses were compared using logistic regression, with Bonferroni adjustment to account for multiple testing. Statistical significance was defined as P .99). There were significant pre-to-post increases in the proportion of respondents indicating they were very confident in their LC diagnosis ability (11/102, 10.8% to 25/79, 31.6%; adjusted P=.004) and very familiar with LC care (10/91, 11.0% to 22/75, 29.3%; adjusted P=.02). The May 2025 webinar had 468 registrants: 52.6% (n=246) were physicians, and 24.8% (n=116) identified an academic medical center affiliation. The attendee count was 264, with 135 and 119 attendees completing the prewebinar and postwebinar surveys, respectively. The proportion of respondents indicating that LC is a very or somewhat serious problem did not significantly differ between the pre-CME (105/134, 78.4%) and post-CME (102/118, 86.4%) surveys (adjusted P=.49). There was a significant pre-to-post increase in the proportion of respondents indicating they were very familiar with LC care (12/116, 10.3% to 60/111, 54.1%; adjusted P<.001). CME participation was associated with significant increases in the proportions of respondents reporting confidence in diagnosing LC and familiarity with LC care, highlighting the potential of virtual CME programs to support clinician education.

items.title: Beyond the Squeeze: Nanodomain Control of Smooth Muscle Mechanotransduction in the Gut.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal smooth muscle cells (SMCs) generate the forces that drive digestion while continuously sensing and adapting to mechanical deformation. How SMCs detect force and convert it into localized chemical and electrical signals remains poorly understood. We propose that mechanosensory output depends on the spatial organization of the nanodomain a channel occupies, and not on the intrinsic properties of that channel alone. Within these environments, mechanosensitive channels integrate opposing depolarizing and hyperpolarizing currents, translating mechanical load into contraction, relaxation, mechanical compliance, or adaptive remodeling. This junction does not appear to be a permanent structure, because it is assembled during development, maintained under load, and eventually lost with age. Which of those elements fails may then determine the clinical phenotype that results. Two questions remain unresolved within this framework: whether stretch reorganizes the nanodomain itself and whether force is also sensed at organelle membranes rather than at the cell surface alone. Emerging tools may finally resolve these dynamics within the active syncytium, uncovering targets for treating dysmotility.

items.title: Lynx1 suppression reopens the window for effective rehabilitation after stroke in mice.
items.abstract: Rehabilitation is an effective and reliable approach for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, its efficacy decreases during the transition from the subacute to the chronic phase after stroke, posing a major barrier to complete functional recovery. This limited efficacy during the chronic phase is believed to result from declining neural plasticity. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms regulating neural plasticity and its temporal changes after stroke remain unclear. To address this gap, we established a focal ischemic stroke mouse model that allows causal interrogation of the mechanisms responsible for the reduced efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase. Using this model, we identified Lynx1, an endogenous negative allosteric modulator of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, as a negative regulator of post-stroke neural plasticity. Lynx1 expression in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was transiently down-regulated and returned to normal levels in the peri-infarct area. Longitudinal intravital imaging revealed that Lynx1 suppression promoted synaptic clustering with increased dendritic spine turnover in the peri-infarct area, an emerging structural basis for memory formation. As anticipated, Lynx1 suppression improved spontaneous motor recovery and the efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase after stroke. Furthermore, we developed a Lynx1-targeting antisense oligonucleotide and found that its administration during the chronic phase after stroke enhanced the efficacy of rehabilitation. These findings suggest that dendritic spine dynamics in the peri-infarct area are a key determinant of rehabilitation responsiveness through the regulation of clustered spine formation and that Lynx1 may represent a promising therapeutic target for augmenting dendritic plasticity after stroke.

items.title: Two-phase NEUROD1 pioneer activity synchronizes sensory neuronal differentiation and subtype specification.
items.abstract: Temporal control of neuronal differentiation is essential for establishing stable neuronal identities, yet the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. Using auditory neurons as an in vivo model, we investigate the role of the proneural factor NEUROD1 in regulating neuronal differentiation timing and subtype specification. To bypass early neuronal loss in germline Neurod1 deletion mutants, we generated a delayed, self-terminating conditional knockout mouse (Neurod1ST) that permits analysis of later differentiation stages. Integration of NEUROD1 chromatin binding and histone profiling at embryonic day (E) 11.5 with transcriptomic analyses across E11.5, E14.5, and E18.5 reveals a two-phase regulatory program during auditory neuron development that parallels dynamic Neurod1 expression. In the first phase, coinciding with Neurod1 upregulation during early neuronal differentiation, NEUROD1 preferentially binds putative enhancers of neuronal differentiation genes and promotes their transition to active chromatin states, consistent with pioneer factor activity. Loss of Neurod1 disrupts these epigenomic transitions, resulting in persistence of progenitor-like states with premature activation of differentiation and axonogenesis programs. This dysregulation is accompanied by activation of alternative regulatory networks, leading to defective neuronal migration and innervation, progressive identity instability, and apoptosis. In the second phase, marked by reexpression of Neurod1 in developing Type Ib/Ic precursors, Neurod1 deletion selectively impairs Type Ic specification while promoting a Type Ib-like identity. These findings identify NEUROD1 as a temporal regulator that coordinates developmental progression and stabilizes auditory neuron identity through phased regulatory activity, providing a mechanistic framework for how pioneer transcription factors couple chromatin remodeling to developmental timing.

items.title: The physiological demands of intermittent endurance exercise performed at different intensities within the anaerobic power reserve: Implications for fatigue development and performance.
items.abstract: This study aimed to describe the physiological demands of intermittent endurance exercise (cycling) performed at different intensities within the anaerobic power reserve (APR); assess if these intensities are sustainable; and determine their effect on subsequent performance. On three separate days, endurance-trained males (n = 15, 36.2 ± 9.4 years old; 84.9 ± 13.0 kg) completed a high-intensity intermittent protocol consisting of fifteen 10-second high-intensity efforts (i.e., surges in intensity) separated by 50 seconds of low intensity (60% maximal aerobic power - MAP) work. These surges were performed either at the intensity associated with the participant's MAP, or at 25% or 50% of their APR. A 30-second Wingate test (WG) was performed immediately after the protocol. Greater physiological and perceptual demands occurred during the APR conditions compared to MAP (p < .05), with very high demands occurring early in the protocol (surges 3-6) during the APR conditions. As such, only 8 and 4 participants completed all surges in the 25APR and 50APR conditions, respectively. Mean power output in the WG was significantly different between all conditions (p < .001), while maximal peak power (MPP) was only different between MAP and 50APR (p = .006). The results indicate that intermittent work at 25% and 50% APR lead to rapid increases in key physiological markers, altering the intramuscular environment, resulting in both severe leg discomfort and a perceived inability to cope with recurring surges. Consequently, the ability to perform a finishing sprint is also affected. Athletes involved in endurance events that require supramaximal efforts should consider the impact of performing high-intensity intermittent work relative to their ability to stay in the race and to maintain power output during the finishing sprint.

items.title: Lower symptom burden strengthens the association between DTI-ALPS index and brain aging in head and neck cancer survivors.
items.abstract: Head and neck (HN) cancer survivorship is associated with persistent symptom burden and long-term brain-behavioral health alterations, yet mechanisms underlying brain aging remain poorly understood. We investigated whether HN cancer survivors exhibit accelerated brain aging, whether limbic white matter (WM) pathways contribute to these changes, and whether measures associated with glymphatic function are associated with reduced brain aging. Diffusion MRI and symptom burden data were analyzed in 135 HN cancer survivors and compared with a normative cohort from the Human Connectome Project (n = 1,228). Two machine learning models (elastic net [ENET] and random forest [RF]) using fractional anisotropy (FA) and quantitative anisotropy (QA) from 45 WM tracts were trained to estimate brain age and compute brain age gap (BAG). Glymphatic-related processes were indirectly assessed using diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular spaces (DTI-ALPS). Moderation analyses examined whether symptom burden influenced associations among DTI-ALPS, BAG, and WM integrity. Survivors showed a negative mean BAG of -1.64 years in the ENET model, indicating a nonsignificant tendency toward delayed brain aging, whereas the RF model showed a positive mean BAG of 3.59 years, indicating accelerated brain aging. The RF model demonstrated stronger external generalizability and greater biological coherence, including associations with ALPS and symptom-related measures. The bilateral fornix and right U-fibers were among the strongest contributors to RF-based brain age prediction. Higher DTI-ALPS index values were associated with lower BAG and greater fornix integrity, particularly in survivors with lower symptom burden and reduced activity-related interference. HN cancer survivorship was associated with accelerated brain aging in the model demonstrating greater external generalizability and biological relevance, alongside alterations in limbic WM pathways. Higher DTI-ALPS was associated with reduced brain aging, with symptom burden modifying this relationship. These findings highlight brain health as an important component of cancer survivorship.

items.title: Dietary EPA + DHA and zerumbone attenuate inflammatory and eicosanoid pathway alterations and NF-κB activity in the brain of hyperlipidemic rats.
items.abstract: Previous research demonstrated that long-chain n-FAs, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) plus docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and zerumbone positively influenced the antioxidant defense system and prevented cognitive decline associated with hyperlipidemia. This study evaluated whether these dietary interventions were also associated with reductions in systemic and brain-specific inflammatory insults. Male Wistar rats were divided into five dietary groups: control, high-fat (HF), HF with fish oil (HF + F) providing EPA + DHA, HF with zerumbone (HF + Z), and HF supplemented with both fish oil and zerumbone (HF + F + Z). After 60 days, the rats were sacrificed, and serum and brain samples were analyzed for systemic and brain-specific inflammatory markers. The HF diet significantly increased cortical NF-κB levels by 67% compared to the control group, and the intervention with EPA + DHA, zerumbone, and their combination reduced NF-κB activity by 42%, 60%, and 64%, respectively, relative to the hyperlipidemic group. Also, the combined intervention (HF + F + Z) significantly reduced serum PGE2 and LTC4 by 55% and 60%, respectively, compared to the HF group. Similarly, hyperlipidemia resulted in elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, MCP-1, IL-1β, and IL-6); intervention with HF + F + Z resulted in significantly decreased levels. Furthermore, hyperlipidemia elevated the expression of COX-2, EP-1, EP-4, 5-LOX, and BLT-1 in the brain, while EPA + DHA treatment significantly restored the changes, and the combination of zerumbone with EPA + DHA demonstrated an even more pronounced effect. Dietary interventions with EPA + DHA and zerumbone, both individually and in combination, attenuate inflammatory and eicosanoid-associated alterations induced by hyperlipidemia.

items.title: Dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain axis induced by intermittent access to palatable food is associated with binge-like eating regardless of obesity development.
items.abstract: Recurrent consumption of energy dense palatable foods contributes to the rising prevalence of obesity and can also promote loss-of-control eating in a subset of individuals. Obesity is commonly associated with peripheral inflammation, impaired sensitivity to appetite-regulating hormones, and alterations in gut microbiota composition, all of which may exacerbate binge-eating behaviors. However, emerging evidence suggests that repeated exposure to palatable foods alone can induce maladaptive eating patterns even prior to the development of obesity. In this study, intermittent access to palatable food (e.g., cheesecake) induced binge-like eating behavior in non-obese female rats, accompanied by hypothalamic microglial reactivity and altered leptin signaling pathway. Additionally, even sporadic exposure to palatable food was sufficient to alter gut microbiota composition, increasing microbial diversity and promoting taxa adapted to high fat and sugar availability, including potential pathobionts (e.g., Escherichia, Streptococcus, and Clostridium spp.) as well as carbohydrate-fermenting bacteria such as Bifidobacterium and Roseburia. Notably, increased microbial diversity was associated with both hyperphagic behavior and reduced hypothalamic leptin pathway responsiveness. Overall, these findings suggest that gut microbiota imbalance and central neuroimmune adaptations occurred in the absence of significant weight gain. This highlights the potential value of early interventions which may represent promising candidate strategies for future investigation.

items.title: Cultural adaptation and discriminative validity of the Arizona Battery of Communication Disorders -Second Edition (ABCD-2) in neurodegenerative disorders.
items.abstract: The study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the ABCD-2 into Greek and investigate its discriminative ability in four neurodegenerative-disorder groups against healthy controls. About 315 participants, assigned into five diagnostic groups [Parkinson's Disease (PD, n = 57), Alzheimer's Disease (AD, n = 62), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI, n = 67), Mixed Dementia (MD, n = 18), and a Control Group (CG, n = 111)], were assessed with the ABCD-2 and Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-Revised (ACE-R) for convergent-validity comparison. Kruskal-Wallis tests showed significant group differences across all cognitive-communication domains (p < 0.001). The ABCD-2 Total Score showed excellent discrimination between patients and controls (AUC = 0.935, 95% CI 0.909-0.960; sensitivity = 85.8%, specificity = 89.2% at a cutoff of 25.2). Differential diagnostic accuracy was moderate-to-good for AD (AUC = 0.783) and MCI (AUC = 0.788), but limited for PD (AUC = 0.530) and MD (AUC = 0.620). Language Expression (AUC = 0.916) and Episodic Memory (AUC = 0.888) showed the highest diagnostic utility. The Total Score correlated strongly with the ACE-R (ρ = 0.888, p < 0.001), with excellent inter-rater reliability (ICC(2,1) = 0.997, 95% CI 0.989-0.999) and high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.92). The Greek version of the ABCD-2 is a reliable and valid battery for identifying cognitive-communication deficits in neurodegenerative conditions. Its discriminative validity may support the detection and individualized management of cognitive-communication disorders in these populations. Subgroup-specific and unadjusted cutoff scores should be regarded as exploratory pending external validation.

items.title: Assessing Psychopathological Risk for Hikikomori: Validation of the Hikikomori-Risk Inventory in Italian Adolescents.
items.abstract: Hikikomori refers to a syndrome of extreme and prolonged social withdrawal from the external world. Although first identified in Japan, Hikikomori is now recognized as a global phenomenon that typically emerges in adolescence and may persist into adulthood. The Hikikomori Risk Inventory (HRI-24) assesses five psychopathological dimensions associated with Hikikomori risk: Paranoia, Depressive Mood, Lethargy, Anthropophobia, and Agoraphobia. However, evidence regarding the psychometric properties of the HRI-24 in adolescent populations remains limited, particular with respect to its associations with broader indicators of psychological adjustment in community samples. The present study examined the psychometric properties of the HRI-24 in a community sample of 837 Italian adolescents aged 13-19 years. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) supported the original five-factor structure of the instrument, and multigroup CFA demonstrated measurement invariance across sex. Evidence for external validity was provided by positive associations between HRI-24 scores and Hikikomori-related traits, as well as internalizing and externalizing problems, alongside negative associations with self-esteem. Overall, the findings support the HRI-24 as a reliable and valid instrument for assessing risk for Hikikomori among Italian adolescents.

items.title: Healthcare Resource Utilization 12 Months Following Initiation of Olanzapine/Samidorphan: Real-World Assessment of Patients with Schizophrenia.
items.abstract: This study used real-world data to examine changes in healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) among patients with schizophrenia in the 12 months after initiating the combination of olanzapine and samidorphan (OLZ/SAM). This retrospective analysis used administrative claims data (October 18, 2020, to December 31, 2023) from the Komodo Healthcare Map. Adults with schizophrenia and continuous enrollment ≥ 12 months before (baseline) and after (follow-up) initiating OLZ/SAM were eligible. Inpatient (IP) admissions, emergency department (ED) and outpatient (OP) visits, and average numbers of IP days/patient were compared between baseline and follow-up. A subgroup analysis of patients receiving OLZ/SAM treatment for the full 12-month follow-up was conducted. A total of 1287 patients with schizophrenia initiating OLZ/SAM were included. Mean (SD) age was 38.8 (13.0) years; 53% were male. Patients were persistent for a mean (SD) of 196.6 (144.6) days. Overall, 481 (37.4%) patients received continuous OLZ/SAM treatment for the full 12-month follow-up. Proportions of patients with ≥ 1 all-cause, mental health-related, or schizophrenia-related IP admission or ED visit significantly decreased between baseline and follow-up (range - 13.0% to - 27.3%; all P < 0.001). Average numbers of all-cause, mental health-related, and schizophrenia-related inpatient days per patient decreased significantly (range - 5.2 to - 5.5 days; all P < 0.001). Proportions of patients with ≥ 1 OP visit were similar during baseline and follow-up, indicating that patients continued receiving outpatient care. Significant reductions in IP admissions and ED visits were also observed in patients receiving OLZ/SAM treatment for the full 12-month follow-up and were larger than those observed in the full cohort. Among patients with schizophrenia, initiating OLZ/SAM was associated with significant and clinically meaningful reductions in acute HCRU compared with baseline. Larger reductions in acute care HCRU were observed among patients who received continuous OLZ/SAM treatment throughout the 12-month follow-up period. A video abstract summarizing the study methods, results, and clinical implications is available in the online version of this article. Supplementary file1 (MP4 83203 kb).

items.title: Healthcare Resource Utilization 12 Months Following Initiation of Olanzapine/Samidorphan: Real-World Assessment of Patients with Bipolar I Disorder.
items.abstract: This real-world data analysis examined healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) among patients with bipolar I disorder (BD-I) in the 12 months before and after initiating a combination of olanzapine and samidorphan (OLZ/SAM). This retrospective analysis used administrative claims data (October 18, 2020-December 31, 2023) from the Komodo Healthcare Map. Eligibility criteria included age ≥ 18 years and continuous enrollment in medical and pharmacy benefits ≥ 12 months before (baseline) and after (follow-up) initiating OLZ/SAM. Comparisons between baseline and follow-up included inpatient (IP) admissions, emergency department (ED) and outpatient (OP) visits, and average number of IP days/patient. A subgroup analysis of patients receiving OLZ/SAM for the full 12-month follow-up period was conducted. Overall, 1004 patients with BD-I who initiated OLZ/SAM were included. Mean (SD) age was 39.0 (12.5) years; 691 (68.8%) were female. Mean (SD) persistence was 173.7 (139.9) days. Overall, 300 (29.9%) patients received continuous OLZ/SAM treatment for the full 12-month follow-up period. Proportions of patients with ≥ 1 all-cause, mental health-related, or BD-I-related IP admission or ED visit between baseline and follow-up were significantly reduced (range - 16.4% to - 42.1%; all P < 0.001), as were mean numbers of IP days/patient (range - 3.9 to - 4.6 days; all P < 0.001). Proportions of patients with ≥ 1 OP visit were similar before and after starting OLZ/SAM, indicating that patients continued receiving OP care. Significant reductions in IP admissions and ED visits were also observed in patients receiving OLZ/SAM treatment for the entire 12-month follow-up period; these reductions were observed to be larger than those observed in the full cohort. Among patients with BD-I, initiating OLZ/SAM was associated with significant and clinically meaningful reductions in acute care HCRU compared with baseline. Larger reductions in acute HCRU were observed among patients with greater treatment persistence. Video abstract available for this article. Supplementary file1 (mp4 225 KB).

items.title: PPARγ at the Nexus of Lipid Metabolism and Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's Disease: A Longitudinal Multi-omics Analysis.
items.abstract: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) has emerged as an important regulator linking lipid metabolism and neuroimmune responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Increasing evidence suggests that disruption of the lipid-immune axis contributes to disease progression and may underlie the heterogeneous therapeutic responses observed with PPARγ-targeted interventions. Experimental studies indicate that PPARγ activation influences multiple biological processes relevant to AD, including lipid homeostasis, mitochondrial function, inflammatory signaling, and amyloid-β clearance. However, the translation of these findings into consistent clinical benefit remains limited by challenges such as poor blood-brain barrier penetration, systemic adverse effects, and disease stage-dependent therapeutic responses. Recent advances in multi-omics technologies and single-cell transcriptomics have provided new insights into the context-dependent roles of PPARγ in different neural cell populations, highlighting dynamic interactions between lipid metabolism, neuroinflammation, and cellular function throughout AD progression. These findings suggest that PPARγ-associated pathways may represent an important regulatory interface linking metabolic and inflammatory processes, while emphasizing the complexity of their temporal and cell-specific regulation. This review synthesizes current evidence from experimental studies, human multi-omics investigations, and clinical research to provide an updated perspective on the role of PPARγ in coordinating lipid metabolism and neuroinflammation in AD. In addition, we discuss the major translational challenges and emerging therapeutic strategies, including selective PPARγ modulation, improved central nervous system delivery, and precision treatment approaches tailored to disease stage.

items.title: Depressive symptom dimensions, physical activity, and incident dementia: a longitudinal analysis of three international cohorts.
items.abstract: Depressive symptoms are increasingly recognized as a potentially modifiable risk factor for dementia. However, most studies have relied on total scores, thereby overlooking heterogeneity across symptom dimensions. We examined dimension-specific associations with incident dementia and the role of physical activity among 27,417 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS). Items from the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) were grouped into somatic symptoms, depressed affect, and positive affect. Incident dementia was algorithmically defined by concurrent education-stratified memory impairment and functional dependence. Cohort-specific associations were estimated using multivariable logistic regression with adjustment for baseline memory performance and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Higher scores for somatic symptoms and depressed affect were associated with incident dementia, with pooled odds ratios of 1.43 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.32-1.55) and 1.31 (95% CI 1.22-1.40), respectively, per 1-point increase. When all three dimensions were modeled simultaneously, somatic symptoms remained associated with incident dementia in all three cohorts, whereas associations for depressed affect and positive affect were substantially attenuated. Dose-response and sensitivity analyses supported the primary findings. No robust evidence indicated effect modification by physical activity. Mediation analyses suggested modest statistical indirect effects through physical activity in ELSA and HRS, with proportions mediated of 6.7-11.0% and 5.4-8.8%, respectively, whereas estimates in CHARLS were imprecise. Across cohorts, somatic symptoms showed the most robust independent association with incident dementia. Graphical abstract.

items.title: Investigating Context in How Clinicians Make Sense of AI: Qualitative Interview Study.
items.abstract: AI-driven clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) are increasingly being introduced to enhance clinical decision-making, yet their adoption in health care remains limited. Research has examined technical, organizational, and contextual barriers to adoption, but less attention has been paid to how knowledge, values, and responsibility around AI-CDSS are constructed and negotiated in practice. This study examines how clinicians and AI experts make sense of AI-CDSS by reanalyzing qualitative interview data through a feminist and constructivist science and technology studies (STS) perspective. Whereas the original study examined informational needs, this reanalysis asks how participants construct relevant knowledge, evaluate the value of AI-CDSS, and negotiate appropriate use and responsibility in clinical practice. The authors conducted a reanalysis of semistructured interviews held in 2024 with clinicians (n=8) and AI experts (n=8) in the Netherlands. The original study focused on informational needs for AI-CDSS. For this analysis, a deductive coding framework based on European Commission guidelines for trustworthy AI was first applied, and the material was then inductively reorganized into 5 empirical themes. Subsequently, feminist and constructivist STS concepts were used as sensitizing concepts in an abductive analysis, and these concepts were brought into dialogue with the empirical themes to examine the sociotechnical relations underlying participants' accounts. Situated knowledge shows that the informational needs of clinicians are not universal but relate to their roles and specific clinical contexts, with understanding oriented less toward technical transparency than toward actionable guidance, relevance, and integration into decision-making. Standpoint theory illuminates differences between stakeholder priorities: clinicians emphasize information on how to use and act on AI outputs within existing workflows, whereas AI experts focus more on providing technical characteristics and performance metrics. Tinkering captures how clinicians experiment with AI systems in practice to develop situated, lay forms of expertise. Situated value highlights that perceptions of an AI-CDSS's worth are relational, with clinicians valuing novel, context-sensitive insights and developers prioritizing performance metrics. Finally, response-ability reveals how trust and accountability are largely delegated to institutional structures, while clinicians report limited legal, organizational, and structural support to respond meaningfully to uncertainty or errors when using AI-CDSS. Reanalyzing the same interview material through an abductive STS approach makes sociotechnical dimensions visible that were not the focus of the original analysis. Rather than treating informational requirements as universal or adoption as primarily a matter of technical performance and communication, the findings show how knowledge, value, and responsibility are constituted through situated professional practices and institutional arrangements. Processes and considerations regarding how clinicians make sense of AI-CDSS are not universal but are shaped by social, cultural, and institutional contexts. This analytical perspective underscores the need for context-sensitive, multistakeholder strategies to support meaningful and responsible AI adoption in clinical practice.

items.title: Microstructural alterations of human medial temporal lobe in dementia: volumetric and DTI findings correlate with cell number and neuropathology.
items.abstract: Volumetric and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) alterations in medial temporal lobe (MTL) regions are consistently reported in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, their biological basis remains poorly understood. We combined Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) metrics with cellular quantification and neuropathological burden assessment to investigate microstructural substrates underlying MTL imaging alterations in human donors with known cognitive and neuropathological status. Absolute cell numbers were quantified in a cohort of 54 brain donors using the isotropic fractionator, and postmortem MRI was performed on a subset of 18 fixed brain hemispheres. To assess microstructural brain alterations associated with disease progression, in vivo volumetric and DTI metrics were analyzed in 39 cognitively unimpaired controls (CU), 31 individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 14 patients with clinical AD dementia. In the postmortem cohort, MTL diffusivity metrics showed moderate negative correlations with total cell numbers. Mean, axial, and radial diffusivity positively correlated with Braak stage, whereas fractional anisotropy (FA) correlated negatively with CERAD score, linking diffusion alterations to AD-related pathology. In vivo MTL analyses revealed increased mean, axial, and radial diffusivity, and reduced FA in AD patients compared with both CU and MCI individuals. The MCI group exhibited intermediate alterations in diffusivity. Differences between in vivo and postmortem diffusion values were consistent with tissue fixation, temperature, and variations in acquisition protocols. Our findings suggest that diffusion MRI alterations in the MTL are associated with reduced cellularity and neuropathological burden, supporting the biological relevance of DTI metrics as markers of microstructural degeneration in AD.

items.title: Municipal Wastewater is a Significant Source of Fibrous Microplastics in the Environment.
items.abstract: Microplastic fibers (MPFs) have been discovered as the most prevalent form of microplastics in the environment, especially in aquatic systems. Household laundries are considered to be a major source of MPFs entering our ecosystems through wastewater discharge. Here, we investigated the occurrence, distribution, and characterization of MPFs from the twenty municipal wastewater sites in Sialkot, Pakistan. Morphological analysis revealed a variety of microplastics, including fibers, fragments, films, beads/pellets, and rubber particles. The total abundance of microplastics was documented as 36.95 ± 10.39 particles/L. Fibers were noted as the most dominant forms, comprising diverse polymer types, including polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), polyamide (PA), and acrylic fibers, along with phthalic-related compounds associated with plastic additives. PVC fibers were the most abundant, contributing about 24% of the total MPFs. This study demonstrates that domestic wastewater discharge plays a key role in transporting MPFs into the aquatic environment.

items.title: Genome-wide analysis reveals altitude-associated divergence in a colour-polymorphic insect.
items.abstract: Environmental gradients provide powerful natural experiments for understanding how selection and gene flow interact to shape genomic and phenotypic variation. However, the genetic basis of adaptation across steep altitudinal clines remains poorly resolved, particularly in systems with high connectivity. We studied the montane bush cricket Isophya rizeensis, which exhibits a discrete male colour polymorphism along a continuous 450-2300 m elevational transect in the Fırtına Valley (Türkiye), with a sharp transition between dark and pale morphs near mid-elevations. Using genome-wide RAD sequencing of 71 individuals, we identified over 92,000 SNPs and detected weak overall population structure consistent with substantial connectivity along the gradient. Despite this, putatively adaptive loci showed markedly stronger spatial differentiation than neutral loci. Genome-wide association analyses identified 101 SNPs significantly associated with altitude, exhibiting reciprocal allele-frequency shifts and steep, narrow clines concentrated over short elevational distances. Discriminant analyses further revealed three loci of large effect that strongly differentiate colour morphs and are tightly linked to elevation. Together, these results indicate that spatially varying selection can maintain discrete phenotypic polymorphism and localized genomic divergence despite high connectivity. Our findings provide empirical support for clinal models of local adaptation under gene flow and highlight how environmental heterogeneity structures adaptive genetic variation in montane ecosystems.

items.title: Cell-type-specific dosage reprogramming reveals epidermal barrier-based gray mold defense strategy in autotetraploid strawberry.
items.abstract: Whole-genome duplication (WGD) triggers genetic and epigenetic remodeling that confers stress adaptation in plants, but how these responses act at single-cell resolution to shape adaptive phenotypes remains unclear. Here, we generated autotetraploid Fragaria nilgerrensis via colchicine treatment, which showed gigantism (enlarged leaves and stomata) and enhanced gray mold resistance. Integrated multi-omics analysis showed that while the expression of many genes remained close to the diploid levels post-WGD, defense pathway genes displayed dosage sensitivity contributing to adaptive traits. Genome-wide transposable element (TE) hypermethylation stabilized the genome and may contribute to dosage by suppressing adjacent gene expression, and differential promoter/gene-body methylation may contribute to distinct gene-dosage responses. Single-nucleus transcriptomics revealed cell-type heterogeneity in dosage responses, with epidermal cells undergoing regulatory network reprogramming toward enhanced physical barriers through increased expression of genes involved in cell wall and cuticle reinforcement. Functional validation confirmed LAC9 as a core gene governing gray mold resistance: Its overexpression improved resistance in diploids, whereas its silencing weakened resistance in tetraploids. LAC9 may increase lignin content to strengthen cell walls and restrain pathogen adhesion and penetration. This work elucidates how WGD enhances adaptive potential through coordinated gene dosage, DNA methylation, and cell-specific reprogramming, offering mechanistic insights and targets for polyploid-based crop improvement.

items.title: Experimental parameters influence thermal tolerance estimates in water beetles: effects of ramping rate and acclimation duration.
items.abstract: Experimental protocols can significantly influence the outcomes of thermal tolerance studies, yet the effects of methodological variation remain poorly quantified for many aquatic macroinvertebrates. For water beetles, a widely used model group in freshwater ecology and thermal tolerance research, dynamic exposures to estimate critical thermal maxima/minima frequently employ different acclimation durations and ramping rates, potentially limiting comparisons among studies. The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of these two parameters on estimates of upper thermal tolerance in water beetles. Consistent with expectations, faster ramping rates and longer acclimation durations generally resulted in higher thermal tolerance estimates than slower ramping rates and shorter acclimation durations. However, the magnitude and consistency of these effects varied across taxa and endpoints, particularly for ramping rate. Effect-size analyses of upper thermal limits (UTL) revealed that differences between the slowest and fastest ramping rates ranged from 0.38 to 4.26 °C among species, whereas differences between the shortest and longest acclimation durations ranged from 1.02 to 3.21 °C. Acclimation duration produced more consistent responses across species than ramping rate. These findings demonstrate that variation in experimental parameters can substantially alter thermal tolerance estimates and may limit the comparability of results across studies. Therefore, it is essential to understand the influence of these parameters and to standardise, or explicitly account for, their effects in experimental design to improve the reliability of thermal tolerance estimates and their comparability among studies of water beetles and other aquatic macroinvertebrates.

items.title: Polylactic acid microplastics alter dissolved organic matter transformation in karst and non-karst lake microcosms of the Tibetan Plateau.
items.abstract: Biodegradable plastics are widely promoted as eco-friendly alternatives, but their degradation generates biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) that threaten aquatic systems. This study compared the impacts of polylactic acid (PLA) microplastics and conventional polyethylene (PE) microplastics on dissolved organic matter (DOM) dynamics and microbial ecology in microcosms established with water from a karst and a non-karst lake on the Tibetan Plateau, using FT-ICR MS, metagenomics, machine learning and dPMD network analysis. Under extreme exposure, PLA microplastics suppressed DOM photodegradation by 28% in the karst-lake microcosms, compared with 20% for PE microplastics. PLA microplastics reshaped DOM composition by reducing recalcitrant lignin-like formulae while increasing bioavailable lipid- and protein-like formulae by 4.8- and 2.0-fold, and shifted DOM assembly toward stochastic processes. Machine learning identified PLA microplastic treatment as the dominant predictor of DOM reactivity in the karst-lake microcosms. PLA microplastics were associated with a selective decline in Dormibacteraeota and with a restructuring of key microbial guilds and putative enzymatic pathways toward carbon and nitrogen lyase reactions, whereas microbial co-occurrence networks in the non-karst-lake microcosms remained stable. These microcosm results challenge the eco-friendly narrative of biodegradable plastics by showing that, under extreme exposure, PLA can alter DOM molecular composition and potential DOM-transforming microbial groups in Karst lake water, underscoring the need for further validation under environmentally relevant field conditions.

items.title: Monitoring ecosystem biodiversity and interaction after forest wildfire: An environmental-DNA-satellite-data-driven artificial intelligence modeling framework.
items.abstract: Wildfire is an escalating threat to forest ecosystem health, yet post-fire management still lacks the timely and systematic consideration of biodiversity loss and biotic disruption. Here, we present an integrative eDNA-satellite-AI monitoring framework that combines environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, satellite-derived burn-severity mapping, and explainable AI (XAI) to quantify post-fire ecosystem changes. Using Sentinel-2 imagery, we first quantitatively assessed the wildfire severity at study sites differentiated by the extent of fire damage (control, damaged, and extremely damaged). eDNA was then collected from water basins installed at these sites and subjected to eDNA metabarcoding, sequencing, and bioinformatic analyses to characterize a wide range of forest eukaryotic groups (e.g., vertebrates, invertebrates, and other microeukaryotes). Ten supervised machine learning (ML) models were subsequently trained to predict burn severity using eDNA features. Systematic optimization of the ML models based on model selection, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning achieved a high prediction performance (R 2 = 0.76), suggesting eDNA data is reflective of post-fire consequences. XAI and co-occurrence network analysis identified the orders Stylommatophora (land snails and slugs), Rodentia (rodents), and Caudata (amphibians) as the taxonomic groups that were most sensitive to wildfire intensity, with eDNA metabarcoding providing phylogenetic and evolutionary information on these groups that is infeasible to obtain at comparable scale and throughput using traditional field surveys. The proposed eDNA-satellite-data-driven AI modeling framework integrates molecular ecology with remote sensing and XAI, thus advancing forest ecosystem monitoring beyond the passive, descriptive characterization of biota inventories towards predictive, explanatory, and risk-based digital ecosystem assessment.

items.title: Emerging and legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) in airborne particles in a fluorochemical industrial cluster: Occurrence, occupational exposure and health risk.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are extensively used in fluorochemical manufacturing, yet their occurrence in airborne particles and occupational health risk remain largely unknown. In this study, 26 emerging and legacy PFAS were measured in airborne particles from 19 production units within a worldwide mega fluorochemical industrial cluster. Particle-bound PFAS concentrations ranged from <1.2 to 255,000 pg/m3, with a hotspot found associated with polytetrafluoroethylene reaction. Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA, trade name "GenX") and perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) were the predominant substances detected. The fingerprint of PFAS profile in particles was characterized by a one-substance dominance by HFPO-DA or perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) or PFHxA in most locations. Exposure through inhalation was estimated to be 0.1 to 19400 pg/kg/day. Non-carcinogenic risk was screened for 9 PFAS with available reference dose and higher risk was noted for HFPO-DA and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The hazard index representing their sum risk was 4.7×10-3 to 8.3, with high risk at a location associated with polytetrafluoroethylene reaction. The carcinogenic risk for PFOA was estimated to be 1.3×10-8-1.5×10-3 among the production locations, of which six locations exceeded the risk screening level. The potential health concern warrants attention and reinforces the need for protective measures.

items.title: Translocation of the environmental bacterium Aquitalea magnusonii promotes systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.
items.abstract: Background & aims Impaired mucosal barrier integrity facilitates translocation of the gut microbiome into the circulation and the liver, thereby exacerbating the severity of chronic liver diseases (CLD). This study aimed to investigate the pathogenic role of non-commensal environmental bacteria, specifically Aquitalea magnusonii in CLD progression by assessing its ability to cross the intestinal barrier and induce systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis. Methods Using an integrated translational framework, patient blood analyses were combined with multi-omics profiling, human intestinal epithelial models, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), hepatic stellate cells (HSC), monocytes, and alcoholic (ALD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated (MASLD) models to evaluate the translocation, virulence, inflammatory and fibrotic potential of A. magnusonii in CLD. Results Non-commensal environmental bacteria, including Aquitalea spp. were detected in multiple organs in both ALD and MASLD models. Detection of Aquitalea DNA in patient samples and other non-commensal environmental bacteria in tap water suggested potential aquatic reservoirs. A. magnusonii produced 12 acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) associated metabolites and its outer membrane vesicles (OMV) were enriched in virulence-related proteins, supporting roles in adhesion, invasion, and immune activation. In addition, gavage with A. magnusonii led to a substantial dysbiotic shift in the gut microbiome. Mechanistically, the cell-free supernatant of A. magnusonii culture activated TLR2- and TLR4-dependent pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Exposure to A. magnusonii or its pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) significantly increased inflammation and fibrosis in vitro and in vivo. Conclusion Non-commensal environmental bacteria, in the example of A. magnusonii, can translocate across the intestinal barrier and promote liver inflammation and fibrogenesis via metabolite production, virulence-associated OMV, and innate immune activation. Impact and implications This study highlights an underrecognized role of non-commensal environmental bacteria in chronic liver disease. Beyond gut commensals, detection of non-commensal environmental microbes such as Aquitalea was associated with markers of more advanced liver disease, while experimental studies of A. magnusonii support biological plausibility for a potential contributory role. These findings highlight the importance of considering environmental reservoirs and non-commensal pathogens in microbial contributions to CLD pathogenesis.

items.title: κ-carrageenan/sodium alginate-based hydrogel microspheres integrated with ZIF-8 and biochar for high-capacity Pb(II) capture.
items.abstract: Lead (Pb) contamination in industrial wastewater continues to pose ecological and human health risks. Natural polysaccharides, such as κ-carrageenan and sodium alginate, are important biological macromolecules for constructing functional hydrogel materials due to their abundant functional groups and excellent gel-forming ability. In this study, a recyclable κ-carrageenan/sodium alginate polysaccharide-based hydrogel microsphere incorporated with ZIF-8 and biochar (BZ/PHM) was successfully fabricated through an in situ growth strategy. The integration of ZIF-8 and biochar within the polysaccharide network endowed the hydrogel microspheres with additional adsorption interfaces and hierarchical porous structures, improving Pb(II) capture performance and recyclability. The resulting composite material integrated ZIF-8-derived interfacial domains, biochar-induced porous interfaces, and abundant oxygen-containing functional groups in the polysaccharide network, thereby achieving efficient Pb(II) adsorption and convenient solid-liquid separation. The maximum experimentally observed Pb(II) adsorption capacity attained 913.93 mg g -1 at 313 K. The adsorption kinetics were better described by the pseudo-second-order model, reflecting the adsorption rate behavior of Pb(II) uptake. Whereas the equilibrium data were better fitted by the Freundlich isotherm model, suggesting heterogeneous adsorption characteristics associated with multiple binding domains. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Zeta-potential analyses suggested oxygen-group complexation, ZIF-8-associated interactions, electrostatic attraction, possible ion exchange as contribute to Pb(II) removal. BZ/PHM retained over 93% adsorption performance after five cycles and removed 97% Pb(II) from simulated battery wastewater, leaving 2.6 μg L -1 . These indicate that BZ/PHM, as a reusable macroscopic adsorbent, has broad application prospects in the treatment of lead-contaminated wastewater.

items.title: The OMM<sup>12</sup> model after ten years: what did we learn about the gut microbiome from a defined microbial community?
items.abstract: Over the past decade, the Oligo-Mouse-Microbiota (OMM 12 ) has emerged as a cornerstone model for mechanistic studies of the gut microbiome. As a rationally designed, defined microbial community, OMM 12 reduces the complexity of the native microbiota while preserving key ecological and functional traits of the murine gut ecosystem. Comprising twelve culturable, genome-sequenced, and phenotypically characterized strains of murine origin, the model enables reproducible and stable colonization across hosts and experimental settings. Initially developed to study colonization resistance, OMM 12 has since been widely applied across diverse fields, including microbial ecology, immunology, and computational biology, providing fundamental insights into host-microbe and microbe-microbe interactions. Its broad adoption has been supported by the development of a rich experimental and computational toolbox, including strain-resolved sequencing, metabolomics, and metabolic modeling approaches. Here, we review a decade of OMM 12 research, highlighting its design principles, methodological advances, and key scientific discoveries, and we additionally provide an overview of available resources, including a newly established website (daisybio.ls.tum.de/omm12/) that consolidates tools, protocols, and datasets to facilitate community use. Together, this review underscores the continued importance of OMM 12 as a versatile platform for causal and quantitative microbiome research.

items.title: Molecular mechanisms underlying differential toxicity of Cr and As to seagrass (Zostera marina L.) under dark conditions revealed by proteomics.
items.abstract: Light availability strongly regulates plant responses to environmental stress, yet how darkness differentially affects arsenic (As) and chromium (Cr) toxicity in the seagrass Zostera marina remains unclear. To address this question, plants were exposed to 46.15 μmol/L As or 0.85 mmol/L Cr under a 12 h light/12 h dark photoperiod or continuous darkness, followed by chlorophyll fluorescence measurements and data-independent acquisition (DIA)-based proteomic analysis. Arsenic stress significantly decreased PSII photochemical efficiency (Fv/Fm), and this inhibition was further aggravated under continuous darkness. In contrast, Cr-induced reductions in Fv/Fm were partially alleviated under dark conditions, indicating that darkness differentially regulates the toxicity of the two metals. Proteomic analysis revealed that darkness aggravated As toxicity through disruption of photosynthesis, phosphoinositide signaling, and energy metabolism, whereas Cr-treated plants activated compensatory pathways associated with metabolic regulation, defense responses, and cellular homeostasis. Overall, this study demonstrates that darkness acts as a metal-specific regulator rather than a universal stress enhancer, providing new insights into light-dependent heavy-metal toxicity in seagrasses. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating environmental light conditions into ecological risk assessments of heavy-metal contamination in coastal ecosystems.

items.title: Paradigm shift from linear discharge to closed-loop cycling: A synergistic phosphorus resource recovery strategy based on waste-treating-waste.
items.abstract: In the face of the dual challenges posed by the non-renewable crisis of phosphorus resources and the problem of water eutrophication, there is a pressing need to break free from the traditional linear economic model of extraction-use-discharge. Therefore, constructing a resource cycling system based on removal-recovery-reuse has become an essential mission for global sustainable development. This study focused on phosphorus resource recovery and reuse path using lotus leaves-derived biochar (LBC). Through further systematic characterization of surface properties and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the key role of oxygen-containing functional groups (e.g., hydroxyl and carboxyl) in phosphate adsorption was elucidated. In the continuous phosphorus enrichment experiment, the FCDI system concentrated phosphorus from a lower concentration influent solution (20 mg/L) into the electrolyte solution, achieving a high concentration of 185.7 mg/L. Finally, a closed-loop resource chain from waste to functional electrode to phosphorus fertilizer was established. This was achieved through differentiated resource utilization: phosphorus-saturated biochar was directly used in agricultural cultivation, and the concentrated electrolyte was converted into struvite. This study presents a lab-scale proof of concept for continuous phosphorus enrichment and dual-pathway recovery, linking wastewater treatment with resource recycling.

items.title: Host habitat environment and species shape the microbial community of Schizothoracinae fishes on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
items.abstract: Exploring the microbial diversity of endemic Schizothoracinae fish on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and its environmental drivers is critical for the conservation of these vulnerable species and plateau aquatic ecosystem stability. Here, we investigated tissue-specific microbiota of 120 Schizothoracinae individuals (7 species, 4 genera) across four basins in Qinghai, China. Using 16 S rRNA sequencing, we performed alpha diversity analysis, partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM), constrained PCoA, and regression models to disentangle drivers of microbial variation. Results showed that Proteobacteria (64.26%) and Firmicutes (12.22%) dominated all samples, with gut microbiota showing distinct signatures: lowest Proteobacteria (51.27%), highest Firmicutes (19.20%), and significantly higher alpha diversity compared with the other three tissues. Environmental factors were the primary contributors, with sampling site and host species being the core drivers. Notably, PLS-PM revealed water pH negatively correlated with gut microbial diversity (standardized path coefficient = -0.42, P< 0.001), while constrained PCoA showed sampling site explained the largest variance in gut and skin microbiota. Secondly, constrained PCoA indicated that the variance explained by sampling site was highest in the gut (28.1%) and skin (27.8%). Moreover, geographical distance of sampling sites was the major driving factor affecting the microbiota dissimilarity, and tissue type was also an important factor in closely related species by a least-squares linear regression model and clustering Barplot. Thirdly, the abundance of the top 10 bacteria phyla significantly correlated with water pH, temperature, altitude and body weight, particularly, the abundance of Proteobacteria and Firmicutes increased with rising water pH and temperature.

items.title: Seasonal variation in mercury contamination and feeding ecology in non-breeding common terns (Sterna hirundo).
items.abstract: Mercury (Hg) contamination in estuarine and coastal ecosystems represents a significant threat to wildlife due to its bioaccumulation and biomagnification across food webs. Particularly, Hg contamination of non-breeding migratory seabirds that inhabit these environments remains poorly documented, particularly at Neotropical latitudes. This study evaluated Hg contamination in relation to trophic ecology and physiology in Common terns (Sterna hirundo) at Punta Rasa, Bahía Samborombón, Buenos Aires, Argentina. Blood total Hg (THg), stable isotopes of carbon (δ 13 C) and sulfur (δ 34 S) as proxies of feeding habitat, and of nitrogen (δ 15 N) as a proxy of trophic position, biochemical markers of energy metabolism and body mass were assessed in individual sampled during three stages of the non-breeding season: i-early season (December), ii-mid-season (February), and iii-pre-migration period (April). Blood THg concentrations were quantified in all individuals (0.32-0.80 μg g -1 dry weight), increasing through the season. Stable isotope values varied seasonally and isotopic niches were wider in December than in February and April. Considering the month of the season, THg was positively associated with δ 34 S and negatively associated with δ 15 N, whereas a positive trend with δ 13 C was observed. These observations suggest that seasonal variation in feeding ecology and isotopic baselines may contribute to differences in Hg contamination. Body mass, triacylglycerol and cholesterol exhibited seasonal variations, nevertheless, under these blood THg concentrations no significant associations with the physiological markers were detected. Overall, our findings highlight the relevance of considering seasonal variation in feeding ecology and non-breeding habitats when assessing Hg contamination in migratory seabirds.

items.title: Divergent fates of cadmium, mercury, and lead in disturbed Chilean coastal food webs.
items.abstract: Anthropogenic activities have profoundly altered the biogeochemical cycling of hazardous trace metals, posing persistent risks to marine biodiversity and public health. However, it remains unclear whether extreme industrial loading fundamentally reshapes trophic transfer mechanisms or merely elevates environmental baselines. Here, we investigated the trophodynamics of cadmium (Cd), mercury (Hg) and lead (Pb), and across contrasting coastal ecosystems in central Chile to determine how anthropogenic stress modulates contaminant flux. By utilizing stable nitrogen isotopes (δ15N) to define trophic hierarchies, we demonstrate a functional dichotomy in metal fates. Hg consistently biomagnifies across both sites (Trophic magnification factor; TMF > 1), whereas Cd and Pb undergo systematic biodilution (TMF < 1), independent of the local pollution regime. Crucially, industrial impact shifted the isotopic nitrogen baseline shifted the δ15N of the basal compartment from 2.81 ‰ at the reference site to 4.54 ‰ at the impacted site, without restructuring the vertical integrity of the food web. Hg biomagnified at statistically indistinguishable rates at both sites (common TMF = 2.67), while concentrations at equivalent trophic position were 8.2 higher at the impacted site. Conversely, Cd and Pb transfer rates remained independent of basal loading, reflecting biologically conserved depuration mechanisms. Our results reveal that intrinsic metal chemistry and host physiology, rather than local contaminant magnitude, are the primary filters governing trophic transfer. These findings establish that industrial pollution transforms basal organisms into high-risk vectors, while preserving macroscopic ecosystem architecture. Such insights necessitate multi-marker monitoring strategies to safeguard sacrifice zones and track the cumulative risk of pervasive contaminants.

items.title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria.
items.abstract: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. We generated dynamic, patchy, nutrient landscapes in a large microfluidic arena and simultaneously tracked individual cells of the marine bacterium Vibrio anguillarum . Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. This work furthers our understanding of bacterial foraging strategies under ecologically relevant conditions.

items.title: Constructing preschool children's music subject key competencies in Henan province, China: A theoretical study based on interviews with kindergarten teachers and experts.
items.abstract: Background Competency-based reforms increasingly position preschool music as a foundation for children's holistic development. Yet in China, an operational and locally grounded framework of music subject key competencies for preschool children aged 3-6 remains under-specified, limiting the alignment of curriculum goals, classroom activities, and process-oriented assessment. Methods This study used an inductive qualitative design. Purposive stratified sampling and snowball sampling were used to recruit 30 participants (kindergarten teachers, managers, and preschool/music education experts) from model kindergartens and universities in Henan Province. Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted. Data were managed in NVivo 12 Plus and analyzed using an inductive qualitative approach informed by grounded theory coding procedures. Results The analysis yielded a seven-dimension framework of music subject key competencies-Music Aesthetic Perception, Artistic Expression, Musical Social Skills, Cultural Understanding, Autonomous Development, Imagination and Creativity, and Physical Movement-together with 24 secondary indicators and observable behaviours. The framework conceptualises early music learning as an integrated developmental process linking perception, embodied action, creative expression, social participation, and cultural meaning-making. Conclusions The framework offers music-centered, practice-grounded guidance for preschool music curriculum design and process-focused assessment, and provides a foundation for subsequent scale development, observation tools, and intervention studies in early childhood music education.

items.title: Mapping the applications of stable isotope analysis in rodent ecology: Protocol for a scoping review.
items.abstract: Background Rodents (order Rodentia) are the most diverse and geographically widespread order of mammals, occupying virtually all terrestrial ecosystems and playing key ecological roles in food webs and ecosystem functioning. Stable isotope analysis has become a tool for investigating trophic ecology, resource use, habitat use, and movement across spatial and temporal scales. Although isotope applications in rodent ecology have expanded in recent decades, the literature remains diverse, and no comprehensive synthesis currently maps this evidence. This scoping review aims to systematically map and synthesize how stable isotope analysis has been applied in ecological studies of the order Rodentia across diverse ecosystems. Methods This protocol follows the methodology of the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), Adelaide, South Australia for scoping reviews and will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches will be conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, SciELO, and Google Scholar (first 200 results sorted by relevance), covering studies from database inception to January 2026. Eligible sources will include peer-reviewed articles, master's theses, and doctoral dissertations published in any language, searches will be conducted in ProQuest, BTDT (Biblioteca digital brasileira de teses e dissertações) and CAPES Theses and Dissertations. Nine reviewers will screen randomized titles and abstracts in pairs, with a pilot-test of 100 random articles to ensure reviewers consistency. Full-text assessment and data charting will be conducted by the reviewer pairs using a standardized form, with a pilot-test verification of a subset of included studies to ensure consistency. No critical appraisal will be performed. Discussion This review will provide a structured overview of stable isotope applications in rodent ecology, identifying methodological patterns, ecosystem and geographic coverage, and knowledge gaps to inform future research and evidence syntheses. Registration This protocol has been registered in the Open Science Framework (OSF) 10.17605/OSF.IO/GQW3B.

items.title: Alkaloid-rich extracts from Solanum crinitum Lam. fruits: antioxidant activity and neuroprotective effects in mouse hippocampal cells.
items.abstract: The central nervous system is highly susceptible to oxidative damage; therefore, searching for neuroprotective compounds is a priority in pharmacological research. We investigated the chemical profile and antioxidant potential of Solanum crinitum Lam., specifically evaluating the impact of maturation stages on their metabolic composition. We observed the predominance of steroidal glycoalkaloids, with solasonine as the primary compound, alongside kukoamines. Fruit ripening triggers a significant metabolic shift, resulting in an approximately 10-fold increase in the abundance of hydroxylated alkaloids, representing an increment of 1-25%. These variations were reflected in the bioactivity: ripe extracts exhibited superior reducing capacity in the FRAP (527 mg TE/g for pulp), while green extracts showed slightly higher values in the ORAC assay (138 mg TE/g for pulp). Although green fruits possess higher toxicity, maturation improves the biological safety of the extracts. These results ratify the potential of S. crinitum as a promising source of neuroprotective molecules and the importance of the maturation stage in modulating its therapeutic properties.

items.title: Evolution as fitness landscape navigation: concepts, measures, and emerging questions.
items.abstract: Fitness landscapes are mappings between genotypes, phenotypes, and fitness that shape evolution. In recent years, empirical work and theoretical models have greatly advanced our understanding of how populations navigate rugged fitness landscapes. Here, we provide a timely review of the theoretical aspects of this field. Its rapidly growing literature employs a wide range of terms, which are sometimes used ambiguously or inconsistently. We therefore begin by defining the major concepts and the field's vocabulary, highlighting our own terminology choices wherever needed. We then review key results on the relationships between epistasis, ruggedness, accessibility, and navigability for genotype-fitness maps, highlighting several complex and sometimes counterintuitive connections that have emerged. Further, we review how the conserved structural properties of the underlying genotype-phenotype map, which can lead to the formation of large connected neutral networks of genotypes, influence dynamics on fitness landscapes. We then compare the two levels to study landscape navigation: the level of genotype-phenotype maps and the level of genotype-fitness maps. Our review leads us to propose a new measure of navigability, based on evolutionary outcomes, which is broadly applicable and overcomes limitations of existing measures. Finally, we highlight examples from the smaller body of work that relaxes the common assumption of fitness-monotonic paths on static landscapes, and discuss how this can fundamentally change the nature of fitness landscape navigation. Throughout the review, we identify directions for future work to fill existing gaps and to synthesize the disparate strands of research within the field.

items.title: Spectral landscape theory for genetic load.
items.abstract: Sewall Wright touched on 2 phenomena when he introduced the concept of fitness landscapes: the evolutionary traversal of the landscape, and the population at a fitness peak. Here, the property of fitness peaks is investigated, specifically the mathematical structures underlying mutation-selection balance. The genetic load at a mutation-selection balance is found to depend on the relationship between the fitnesses, and the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of its mutation matrix. This is an extension of spectral landscape theory into the regime of strong mutation and strong selection dynamics. The classical Haldane-Muller principle is the finding that the loss of fitness in a population due to mutations is nearly independent of selection strength, but instead is dominated by the mutation rate. Departures from the Haldane-Muller principle, where mutation-selection balance produces a mean fitness greater than Haldane's limits, have been documented in models of multilocus selection where there is threshold selection, truncation selection, synergistic epistasis, or evolution on neutral networks. The key finding here is that the departures from Haldane's limits may be estimated by how the fitnesses and reproductive values align with the eigenvectors of the mutation matrix: the closer the alignment with eigenvectors corresponding to the largest eigenvalues of the mutation matrix, the greater the equilibrium mean fitness will be. This yields a deep relationship: perturbations of haplotype frequencies that converge fastest to mutational equilibrium will, when used to perturb fitnesses, result in the greatest genetic loads at mutation-selection balance. The results are obtained for a haploid model with arbitrary fitnesses and reversible mutation patterns. The theory is applied to specific models from the literature, including house-of-cards mutation, threshold selection, and neutral networks. House-of-cards mutation is proven to remain close to the Haldane-Muller principle.

items.title: Characterisation and antioxidant properties of Cinnamomum cassia polysaccharides and the protective effect against methomyl-induced toxicity in human HEK293 cells line and rat testicles.
items.abstract: Polysaccharides are natural bioactive with notable antioxidant properties. This study aimed to characterise a polysaccharide (Cc-Ps) and assess its antioxidant potential, cytoprotective effect, and in vivo protection against methomyl (MET)-induced testicular toxicity. In vitro, Cc-Ps exhibited significant hydroxyl radical (OH•) scavenging activity, and GC-MS analysis revealed a monosaccharide composition, including glucose and arabinose likely contributing to its bioactivity. In HEK293 cells, pre-treatment with Cc-Ps markedly improved viability following MET exposure, demonstrating its cytoprotective capacity. In vivo, MET administration in rats led to decreased serum testosterone, LH, and FSH levels, elevated malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced activities of antioxidant enzymes (superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), glutathione peroxidase (GPx)), indicating oxidative stress. Cc-Ps pre-treatment significantly restored hormone levels, reduced MDA, and enhanced enzymatic antioxidant defence. Histological examination confirmed preservation of seminiferous tubules and spermatogenic cells. These findings highlight Cc-Ps as a potent antioxidant and cytoprotective agent with the ability to mitigate oxidative stress and reproductive toxicity induced by MET.
