items.title: Masculinity Norms in Men's Friendships: Social Cure and Curse Pathways From Gender Identity to Well-Being.
items.abstract: Men experience higher social isolation and lower emotional intimacy in friendships than women, yet the identity-based processes shaping men's same-gender friendships remain underexamined. Drawing on the Social Identity Approach to Health (SIAH), this preregistered study tested how gender identity centrality relates to cisgender men's same-gender friendships and well-being through men's endorsement and enactment of traditional friendship-related masculinity norms. A U.S. sample of 501 cisgender men completed measures of gender identification, endorsement of gender-traditional friendship norms, self-disclosure, expressive and instrumental friendships, social support, friendship satisfaction, mental well-being, and life satisfaction. Structural equation models revealed pathways through which gender identity centrality predicted lower well-being (i.e., "social curse" effects), in the form of serial mediation paths: Men higher in gender identity centrality more strongly endorsed gender-traditional friendship norms, which predicted lower comfort with self-disclosure and less expressive friendships. In turn, the pathway via lower self-disclosure predicted lower social support, friendship satisfaction, and mental well-being. The pathway via less expressive friendships in turn predicted lower social support and friendship satisfaction. Model comparisons supported the hypothesized serial mediation models - indicating a mechanism in which gender identity centrality shapes friendship experiences through endorsement of masculinity norms - over moderation and additive prediction structures as plausible alternatives. Findings highlight how restrictive masculine norms can undermine men's relational well-being, and underscore the importance of interventions that broaden acceptable expressions of emotionality in men's friendships.

items.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology.
items.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies. This case-control study included 4 biorepositories based in the US that contributed CSF and plasma samples from participants with and without tauopathies, many of whom had antemortem biofluid samples paired with autopsy or genetically defined neuropathology. Samples were analyzed between August 2023 and December 2025. Data analysis occurred from August 2024 to July 2026. CSF and plasma eMTBR-tau243 concentrations measured using a mass spectrometry-based assay. Outcomes included mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (eg, AD and CTE) based on autopsy, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with MAPT variants (FTLD-MAPT), and CTE stage. Differences in biomarker levels between groups were evaluated using analysis of variance or analysis of covariance, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the discriminative performance of fluid eMTBR-tau243. Among the 229 participants (196 with CSF samples and 55 with plasma samples [22 with both]), mean (SD) age at fluid sample collection was 63 (13) years and 108 (47%) were female. Median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 10 patients with AD (0.459 [0.246-0.801] fmol/mL) compared with 29 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.002 [0.001-0.005] fmol/mL) (adjusted P < .001), but other autopsy-confirmed non-AD tauopathies (which included 52 individuals with conditions including progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration) did not demonstrate an increase (0.015 [0.008, 0.039] fmol/mL). Six symptomatic FTLD-MAPT variant carriers with mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (R406W, V337M, and G389R) had increased median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 (0.140 [0.055-0.174] fmol/mL) compared with 15 4R tauopathy variant carriers including N279K and P301L (0.004 [0.001-0.044] fmol/mL) (P = .001). Median (IQR) plasma eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 11 patients with CTE (1.93 [0.42-3.68] fmol/L) compared with 20 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.29 [0.05-0.62] fmol/L) (adjusted P = .007), but did not increase as high as among 14 patients with AD (11.25 [2.29-19.38] fmol/L). Plasma eMTBR-tau243 distinguished CTE stage III and IV from controls (AUC, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.92-1.00), but not CTE stage I from controls (AUC, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97). This study found that plasma and CSF eMTBR-tau243 were increased in mixed 3R/4R tauopathies including AD, high-stage CTE, and a subset of genetic FTLD-MAPT, compared with cognitively unimpaired controls. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine the clinical utility of eMTBR-tau243 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for CTE and other tauopathies beyond AD.

items.title: Revealing the hidden spatial distribution of visual attention through pupillometry.
items.abstract: Visual attention selects which visual information is processed at a given moment. Its spatial distribution, the size and shape, constitute the attentional field. This field can be flexibly adjusted and is central to everyday behavior, yet how it changes over time is challenging to capture. In the present study, we introduce a pupillometry approach that uses luminance tagging to track changes in the attentional field continuously. Previous work has shown that attending to a brighter location causes pupil constriction compared to attending a darker location. Here, we extend these findings by demonstrating that this technique can capture changes in the attentional field. In Experiment 1, a static luminance-tagged background was used to track expansions and contractions of attentional breadth indirectly. In Experiment 2, this method appeared sensitive to changes in attentional shape, suggesting it could distinguish an annular from a circular attentional distribution. Together, this shows that luminance tagging combined with pupillometry provides a continuous and objective measure of attentional field allocations that can be flexibly combined with secondary tasks.

items.title: Unraveling physical literacy: a psychological network approach to understanding youth physical activity.
items.abstract: Physical activity (PA) is essential for healthy development, yet less than a quarter of U.S. youth meet the recommended PA levels. Physical literacy (PL) has emerged as a holistic framework to support sustained PA through the integration of motivation, confidence, physical competence, and knowledge and understanding; however, the field remains limited by measurement challenges and insufficient attention to the social climate in which PA is experienced. To address this gap, the present study proposes and empirically tests social climate as a fifth core domain of PL and examines PL as a dynamic, interconnected system using psychological network analysis. Cross-sectional data were collected from 771 youth (ages 8-14) enrolled in 24 afterschool programs serving underserved communities in the southeastern United States (2018-2024). Validated questionnaires assessed knowledge and understanding, motivation, confidence, and social climate, while physical competence was operationalized as objectively measured moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA; daily and afterschool) using ActiGraph GT3X accelerometers. Domain-level networks revealed that all five domains were positively interconnected, with a particularly salient Social Climate-Motivation-Knowledge association. At the scale level, regulatory motivation showed the highest node strength, followed by social support from friends and autonomous self-regulation. Bridge analyses identified autonomous self-regulation (TSRQA), need for relatedness, and perceived PA ability as key connectors linking social, motivational, and cognitive processes. Findings provide preliminary empirical support for social climate as a core PL domain and highlight the integrated roles of regulatory motivation, intrinsic enjoyment, and autonomous self-regulation as strategic targets for PA interventions aimed at strengthening PL and promoting sustained youth PA engagement.

items.title: "Aguantarse, Sacar Adelante": A Hermeneutic Phenomenological Account of Paternal Postpartum Distress among Mexican Fathers.
items.abstract: Paternal perinatal distress is increasingly recognized as a clinical and family-systems concern, yet remains underexamined in Mexico and across Latin America. Situated within Mexican ethnopsychology and the study of cultural idioms of distress, this hermeneutic phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of three first-time Mexican fathers navigating emotional difficulty during the first 24 months following childbirth. Interviews were conducted in Spanish and analyzed through the hermeneutic circle, with attention to the cultural-moral frameworks within which fathers' narratives became sayable. Three themes were identified: the cultural shape of paternal distress in fathers' own vocabulary; the script of endurance and silence organized around aguantarse (to endure silently) and sacar adelante (to push forward for the family); and the invisibility of paternal distress within clinical, familial, and structural support systems. Findings indicate that paternal postpartum distress in Mexican contexts is produced and obscured by a culturally specific masculine script that constitutes a meaningful and addressable target for clinical and policy intervention.

items.title: When standard two-method measurement planned missing designs reach their limits: Time-embedded adaptations for intensive longitudinal studies.
items.abstract: Two-method measurement planned missing designs (TMM-PMD) offer a cost-efficient approach to balancing measurement quality and statistical power by strategically administering both gold-standard and efficient measures. While well established in cross-sectional and traditional longitudinal studies, their applicability in intensive longitudinal studies (ILS) remains underexplored. This study evaluates the performance of standard TMM-PMD in ILS and proposes two time-embedded adaptations: a time-embedded version (T-TMM-PMD) and a time-embedded and person-balanced version (TP-TMM-PMD). Through two simulation studies based on bivariate dynamic structural equation models (DSEM), we show that the standard TMM-PMD encounters convergence issues, whereas the time-embedded adaptations substantially improve convergence while preserving estimation accuracy and statistical power. Although the differences between the two adaptations are generally small, TP-TMM-PMD shows modest advantages under conditions with relatively lower within-person reliability of the efficient measure and fewer time points. To assist applied researchers, we provide step-by-step simulation-based guidance for selecting optimal TMM-PMD configurations under budget constraints. This practical framework enables pre-study evaluation of design trade-offs tailored to specific research contexts. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of aligning TMM-PMD with the temporal structure of ILS and offer actionable solutions to improve design efficiency and feasibility in applied settings.

items.title: "Maa. She is Me": Gendered Emotional Climate in the Making of Therapists in India.
items.abstract: In contemporary India, gendered injuries such as affinal violence, son preference, and female feticide may endure within families as mental distress among women. Drawing on twelve months of ethnographic fieldwork at a postgraduate counseling psychology program in Bangalore, this paper examines how trainees' gendered subjectivities are shaped by growing up within what I call a gendered emotional climate: the durable affective condition that forms as the emotional circumstances of a household, where structural violence is absorbed into kinship, recur and settle over the long arc of growing up. Through a person-centered account of a trainee whose path to becoming a counselor was inseparable from her mother's history of abuse and chronic distress, I argue that counseling training functions as a form of repair of the emotional climate. It sets in motion the processing of the psychic afterlives of gendered injury and equips trainees to partially rework the gendered emotional climate in their natal households. Training-mandated self-work thus becomes inseparable from filial work. Rather than isolating the subject from family life, counseling may cultivate an ethic of self-making that remains embedded in kinship while partly reworking inherited emotional worlds. This finding has significant implications for clinical understandings of the relationship between gender justice and mental health in post-liberalization India.

items.title: Navigating Social Suffering: Meaning-Making Through the Idiom "Political Depression" Among Young Weibo Users in China.
items.abstract: "Political depression" (/, zhengzhixingyiyu/zhengzhiyiyu) has emerged in recent years as a widely circulated idiom of distress among young Weibo users in China, gaining visibility on social media from 2019 onward and peaking in public discussion during the COVID-19 pandemic. Drawing on sustained reading and reflexive thematic analysis of posts published from 2019 to 2025 on Weibo, one of China's largest social media platforms, this study examines how users employ the idiom to articulate, interpret, and navigate experiences of distress. The analysis suggests that young Weibo users draw on the idiom to negotiate social suffering in the context of witnessing and experiencing injustice. In naming their own suffering, they produce new forms of subjectivity that unsettle the authority of psychiatry and psychology, while also revealing a dynamic interplay between distress and resilience.

items.title: Pathology-Triggered Cascade-Responsive Implants for Converting Diabetic Microenvironment Signals Into Osteogenic Drivers.
items.abstract: Hyperglycemia severely impairs implant osseointegration due to a hostile bone microenvironment of glycemic fluctuations and oxidative stress. Although responsive biomaterials can dynamically regulate pathological issues, converting harmful signals into a continuous driving force that promotes bone formation remains challenging. Herein, we present a cascade-responsive poly(aryl ether sulfone ketone) (PPESK) implant designed to actively leverage pathological signals for bone regeneration. PPESK features a chitosan-based surface modified with glucose oxidase (GOD), encapsulating black phosphorus (BP)-based nanoparticles loaded with in situ mineralized IGF-1 (mBI). Underlying this design is a glucose/pH/ROS cascade-responsive mechanism where local glucose triggers the catalytic activity of GOD, leading to acid-induced swelling of chitosan and subsequent exposure of mBI. Subsequently, the intrinsic oxidative responsiveness of BP to reactive oxygen species (ROS) facilitates the controlled release of IGF-1. It not only utilizes pathological signal transduction for targeted drug delivery to enhance the osteogenic differentiation potential of BMSCs but also establishes a self-regulated feedback path. By continuously consuming excess glucose and ROS, the implant improves the adverse local environment while promoting bone regeneration. Consequently, the PPESK implant accelerates bone remodeling in vivo, transforming the hyperglycemic microenvironment into an active driver for diabetic bone regeneration and offers a novel therapeutic strategy for stagnated bone repair.

items.title: Parents' perspectives on a modified sports intervention for autistic children: Insights from the Sports Stars Brazil programme.
items.abstract: To understand parents' perceptions of the impacts of a modified sports intervention, Sports Stars Brazil, for autistic children, based on the F-words for child development framework. This descriptive qualitative study included four focus groups with parents of autistic children who participated in the Sports Stars Brazil intervention. Data collection was guided by open-ended questions exploring the perceived impact of the intervention across all F-words (Fitness, Functioning, Family, Friends, Fun, and Future). Data were analysed thematically and organized into three categories: (1) individual F-words; (2) integration of the F-words; and (3) general perceptions. Parents perceived positive impacts across all F-words, particularly in relation to children's socialization, motivation, functioning, and well-being. The F-words were described as integrated rather than isolated, with emphasis on play, increased autonomy, and a sense of belonging within the group. Parents also reported personal emotional changes, including shifts in how they perceived their children's abilities and how they engaged in daily caregiving. Sports Stars Brazil was experienced not only as a motor intervention but also as a context for family strengthening, emotional growth, and hope for the future, highlighting the value of integrated, fun, group-based sports interventions for autistic children and their families.

items.title: Does early childhood education and care for infants and toddlers cause behavior problems up to age 8?
items.abstract: The causal effect of attending Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) for infants and toddlers on child behavior problems is contested. Yet, most previous research is correlational. Findings from previous research are mixed, but with some evidence of harmful effects on children's behavior. Some correlational studies also suggest that ECEC may be most harmful for children from socioeconomically advantaged families. We estimate the effect of age of entry into ECEC on externalizing behavior problems at ages 3, 5, and 8 years in a large sample (n = 66,394) from The Norwegian Mother, Father, and Child Cohort study (MoBa). We use two quasi-experimental methods, Two-way fixed-effects models and instrumental variable models, that exploit variations in how early families enrolled their children in ECEC due to a national scale-up of publicly funded centers. In this high-powered, rigorous approach to testing the causal impact of age of entry into ECEC, we find no evidence that entry around age 1 relative to later affects behavior problems either during preschool years (at ages 3 or 5) or after school entry (at age 8 years). We also find no evidence that these effects vary by parental education or family income. We find no evidence suggesting that early entry into ECEC has harmful consequences for children's behavior regulation during the preschool years or after school entry. We argue that our null results may be due to ECEC pedagogy in Norway that emphasizes young children's well-being and playful learning experiences.

items.title: Editorial: The complex case of neurocognitive functioning and externalizing problems.
items.abstract: Neurocognitive functioning has attracted specific attention with regard to its role in externalizing disorders. However, important knowledge gaps remain regarding how studying youth neurocognitive functioning will meaningfully advance our understanding of the role of neurocognition in the development of complex problems and whether it has the potential to improve treatment outcomes. In this issue, three studies may help close these gaps. Focusing on different populations, they all show that neurocognitive functioning in childhood prospectively predicts later externalizing disorders and related behaviours. At the same time, the role of executive functioning varied considerably across outcomes, informants, and assessment methods. Moreover, executive function deficits partly reflected the developmental consequences of early adversity rather than operating as an independent characteristic. Together, these studies provide helpful ground for reflecting on the promise (and perhaps limitations) of the integration of neurocognitive functioning for advancing our knowledge on the development and treatment of externalizing and related problems.

items.title: Longitudinal patterns of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder medication use and subsequent incident substance use among US youth.
items.abstract: Understanding potential substance use risks or protection associated with ADHD medication use over time among US youth with ADHD has clinical and public health importance. Using longitudinal nationally representative data and accounting for pre-existing differences in youth can shed light on these associations. This study used longitudinal prospective data from the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study (2013/14-2023). Analyses included youth ages 12-17 with a parent-reported history of an ADHD diagnosis by a doctor, nurse, or health professional (n = 4,700 observations; n = 2,140 unique individuals). Using propensity score weighting to account for pre-exposure differences, the effect of ADHD medication initiation compared to no ADHD medication use and the effect of ADHD medication discontinuation compared to continuation on five incident substance use outcomes (alcohol, nicotine/tobacco, e-cigarettes, cannabis, other drugs) 1 year later were examined. Among youth with parent-reported ADHD, those who initiated ADHD medication did not differ from youth who did not use ADHD medication in subsequent incident substance use risk (adjusted odds ratios ranged from 0.94 to 1.36). Similarly, those who discontinued ADHD medication did not differ from youth who continued ADHD medication in subsequent risk for incident substance use (adjusted odds ratios ranged from 0.98 to 1.02). These results add to the evidence that ADHD medication use initiation and medication discontinuation patterns are not related to an increased risk for incident substance use among US youth. This study highlights the importance of considering baseline differences between youth when considering the effect of ADHD medication on future substance use risk.

items.title: The Necessary Role of Leader-Employee Exchange Relationships on Employee Performance.
items.abstract: Do employees need a favorable relationship with their leader to excel at work? Research indicates that to perform at work it is nice to have a favorable relationship with one's leader, but in the current study we test whether it is necessary. Utilizing a different paradigm, necessity logic across two samples (N1 = 127, N2 = 131) of leader-employee dyads, we test the extent to which the leader-employee exchange relationship is a necessary condition for employee performance (i.e., work effort, work quality, work engagement, and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB)). We find that very high work engagement and OCBO rarely occur unless leaders are satisfied with their exchange relationship with the employee. We also find that very low work effort and work quality rarely occur unless leaders are dissatisfied with their exchange relationship with the employee. Finally, very low work quality appears primarily when leader and employee perceptions of the exchange relationship are misaligned; when their perceptions align, the lowest levels of work quality are largely absent. Thus, there are significant benefits for managers in maintaining alignment in perceptions of the exchange relationship.

items.title: Longitudinal associations of anemia and iron status on early learning and memory: Evidence from eye-tracking assessments.
items.abstract: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) remain prevalent among young children and may influence cognitive domains. We examined associations of anemia and iron status at 6-9 months with attention, memory, and social visual engagement six months later using eye-tracking. We analyzed cohort data from a randomized egg provision trial in rural Mangochi District, Malawi (n=660). In a subgroup (n=406), baseline biomarkers were measured, including hemoglobin, plasma ferritin, soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR), and body iron index (BII). Children were categorized as anemic (hemoglobin 8.3 mg/L, or BII <0 mg/kg), and iron deficient anemic (IDA). At 12-15 months, attention was assessed using eye-tracking-based Infant Orienting with Attention task; recognition memory and social visual engagement were assessed using Visual Paired Comparison. Associations were evaluated using mixed-effect models adjusted for child, parental, and household characteristics. Among 406 children, 185 (45.6%) had anemia at baseline. Of 366 with iron data, 308 (84.2%) had ID, including 150 with IDA. Hemoglobin was associated with social visual engagement, and iron-specific biomarkers with memory. Per interquartile range (IQR) increase in hemoglobin, eyes dwell time decreased by 4% (95%CI -6%, -1%), mouth dwell time increased by 2% (95%CI 0%, 6%), and eye-mouth index decreased by 0.04 (95%CI -0.08, 0.00). IQR increases in ferritin, sTfR, and BII were associated with higher novelty preference (0.02; 95%CI 0.00, 0.02), lower peak look duration (-9.5%; 95%CI -14.8%, -2.9%), and lower shift rate (-0.02 shifts/s; 95%CI -0.04, 0.00), respectively. In multiplicity-corrected sensitivity analyses, only the sTfR-peak look duration association remained significant. Categorical anemia, ID, and IDA were not associated with outcomes. Exploratory findings suggest that hemoglobin at 6-9 months was associated with social visual engagement, and iron-specific biomarkers with memory. Small effect sizes indicate modest longitudinal associations in this high-burden setting. NCT03385252 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03385252).

items.title: Greater Translocator Protein Distribution Volume in Neurocircuitry of Anorexia Nervosa.
items.abstract: Inflammatory stimuli are associated with onset of anorexia nervosa (AN) but whether inflammation occurs in the brain of AN is unknown. The primary objective is to determine whether [18F]FEPPA total distribution volume ([18F]FEPPA VT), PET index of translocator protein density and inflammatory marker of gliosis, is elevated in AN in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), ventral striatum (VS), dorsal caudate (DC), dorsal putamen (DP), thalamus, orbitofrontal cortex and insula. Secondary objectives are to determine the relationship of [18F]FEPPA VT in ACC to rumination severity and [18F]FEPPA VT to body mass index (BMI). [18F]FEPPA VT was measured in 20 medication free AN participants and 20 healthy controls. Correlations of [18F]FEPPA VT with rumination severity, and BMI, were determined. [18F]FEPPA VT was elevated in AN in all ROI (linear mixed model (LMM), group effect, P = 4×10-7), particularly ACC, VS, DC and thalamus (mean 52% elevation; LMM, region by group interaction, P = 4×10-4). ACC [18F]FEPPA VT correlated positively with eating concerns (Eating Disorder Examination, r = 0.58, P = .007; Inventory of Depression and Anxiety Symptoms-II, r = 0.66, P = .002). There were no significant correlations between [18F]FEPPA VT and BMI. Greater [18F]FEPPA VT is strong evidence for neuroinflammation and gliosis, particularly in ACC, VS, DC and thalamus in AN. Given such, it may be of interest to assess interventions that influence gliosis towards curative roles in future clinical trials in AN.

items.title: Algorithmic obesogenicity: a conceptual framework for algorithmically mediated commercial influence in digital food environments.
items.abstract: This article proposes 'Algorithmic Obesogenicity' as an integrative construct describing how behavioural data and optimisation systems mediate a structural pathway of commercial influence in digital food environments. Drawing on research on commercial determinants of health, digital food environments, food marketing, platform design, and data governance, the framework comprises five analytical levels: enabling conditions, algorithmic operations, commercial practices and interface mechanisms, intermediate outcomes, and potential longer-term outcomes. Three interrelated enabling conditions are developed: unbounded digital access, data asymmetry, and regulatory lag. Within these conditions, digital architectures can select, rank, personalise, time, and adapt food-related commercial exposure and purchasing opportunities. Food marketing can influence attention, preferences, purchasing, and consumption-related outcomes, but the contribution of personalised algorithmic exposure to sustained dietary change, metabolic risk, and obesity remains unquantified. The framework specifies observable processes and generates research propositions that can be investigated across users, population groups, platforms, and regulatory contexts. Algorithmically mediated commercial influence does not remove agency but may modulate the informational and practical conditions under which food-related decisions are made. Algorithmic accountability, digital data sovereignty, and transnational regulatory alignment correspond most directly to the mechanisms identified, whereas digital food sovereignty and health-related digital levies remain areas for policy development and evaluation.

items.title: A scoping review of food insecurity in U.S. higher education by state's congressional delegation majority.
items.abstract: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the literature on U.S. college student food insecurity has expanded, warranting an updated review. The pandemic represented a unique period in which emergency aid may have influenced students' food security status, highlighting the importance of examining the prevalence of food insecurity before, during, and after the pandemic. Additionally, introduced federal legislation aimed at addressing student food insecurity has yet to be enacted. Because congressional delegates help shape the federal policy landscape, examining food insecurity in relation to states' congressional delegations may offer new insight. This scoping review aimed to critically synthesize peer-reviewed publications and grey literature (i.e., institutional reports) on the prevalence of food insecurity among college students attending U.S. four-year public institutions by pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods, and to document the prevalence by U.S. states' congressional delegation majorities. MEDLINE-PubMed, Web of Science, ProQuest, and EBSCO Host Academic Search Complete were searched for articles published between September 1995 and July 2026. Search terms included "food security" or "food insecurity", "university" or "college" or "students", and "prevalence" or "rate". A hand search was conducted to identify institutional reports on student food insecurity. A total of 48 studies were eligible for full-text analysis. The mean prevalence of food insecurity was 39% pre-pandemic (n=18), 36% during the pandemic (n=12), and 41% post-pandemic (n=18). Higher proportions of food insecurity were observed in states with Republican-majority congressional delegations (43%) compared to those with Democratic-majority (35%) or split delegations (35%). College student food insecurity remains high across the U.S., regardless of state congressional delegation majority, suggesting federal action is needed, such as expanding student access to federal food assistance programs.

items.title: EEG-based Deep Learning Reveals Cortical Sensitivity to Small Changes in Deep Brain Stimulation Parameters.
items.abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) is an invasive procedure used to alleviate motor symptoms in Parkinson's Disease (PD) patients. Despite its effectiveness, the impact of DBS on brain activity and the way to optimise stimulation parameters remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to map the sensitivity of cortical neural response to changes in DBS parameters in real-world clinical settings. We recorded in-clinic EEG data from PD patients during their clinical DBS programming sessions, both at rest and during arm movement. A siamese variant of the EEGNet deep learning architecture was trained independently for each patient and parameter combination to determine whether two 1-sec-long EEG segments were recorded under the same or different DBS parameters, yielding 30 independently trained models. Our models achieved an average accuracy of 74% in classifying whether two 1-second EEG segments corresponded to the same or different DBS parameters. Explainability methods were then applied to extract the neural oscillations learned by the models. Ablation studies identified mid-gamma oscillations (55-90Hz) as the key band for classifying these changes. Importantly, that was not driven by 1:2 gamma entrainment. In a sub-group of patients, the theta-alpha oscillations (4-12Hz) also contributed to detecting changes in DBS parameters. We demonstrate that small DBS parameter changes modify cortical activity in a consistent manner that can be detected using shallow convolutional networks on low-density EEG. Our findings suggest that cortical mid-gamma oscillations (55-90Hz) are highly sensitive to small changes in DBS settings. Our approach and findings could be leveraged towards identifying and defining novel digital biomarkers to guide DBS programming and adaptive DBS systems.

items.title: Age and Within-Session Countermovement Jump Response in Professional Soccer Players.
items.abstract: Chronological age may influence how professional soccer players respond to a standardized testing sequence, yet this has rarely been examined within a single session. This secondary analysis included 227 professional male outfield players who contributed data from 243 preseason testing sessions. Squat jump, countermovement jump, and arm-swing countermovement jump tests were performed before isokinetic knee-strength testing and a maximal treadmill cardiopulmonary test and were repeated after only 3 minutes of recovery. Linear mixed-effects models included time, mean-centered age, and their interaction, with random intercepts for player and testing sessions. Countermovement jump increased by 1.91 cm (95% confidence interval: 1.64-2.17; p<0.001), with a significant time×age interaction (B=0.078 cm y-1; 95% confidence interval: 0.028-0.129; p=0.002). A similar interaction was observed for arm-swing countermovement jump (B=0.080 cm y-1; p=0.007), whereas the squat jump estimate was smaller and statistically inconclusive (B=0.027 cm y-1; p=0.291). The countermovement jump interaction remained broadly consistent in post hoc analyses accounting for body fat, relative knee strength, maximal oxygen uptake, and baseline countermovement jump. Older players therefore showed a slightly larger countermovement jump improvement across this demanding sequence. Although the test position was not manipulated, these findings suggest that the placement of the countermovement jump within a testing battery should be kept consistent when repeated jump assessments are compared.

items.title: Assessing advanced theory of mind in middle childhood: psychometric evaluation and responsiveness to training of a comprehensive AToM battery.
items.abstract: This study examined the psychometric properties and responsiveness to training of a comprehensive Advanced Theory of Mind (AToM) Battery in middle childhood. In Study 1, 168 eight- to nine-year-old children participated (Mage = 8.61 years, SD = 0.64; 88 girls, 79 boys, one preferred not to say). Children completed the AToM Battery, the Strange Stories task, and measures of language, inhibition, working memory, and nonverbal intelligence. Confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) largely supported the proposed three-factor structure. At the same time, the CFA indicated that several items, particularly within the Social Reasoning component, showed comparatively weak loadings. The AToM Battery showed moderate convergent validity with the Strange Stories task, r = .37, p < .001. Language ability significantly predicted overall AToM performance, R2 = .16, with effects primarily driven by the Social Reasoning component, R2 = .15. In Study 2, 126 children completed the battery at pretest, posttest, and follow-up after participating in either a conversation-based training or a control training. Linear mixed-effects models indicated general improvements over time across groups. Training-specific gains emerged most consistently for Recognition of Transgressions of Social Norms at posttest [t(247.20) = 3.45, p < .001] and follow-up [t(247.20) = 3.23, p = .001]. Stability correlations in the control group indicated moderate temporal stability over a three-month interval, r = .55, p < .001. Overall, the findings support the AToM Battery as a multidimensional and psychometrically useful measure of advanced social-cognitive reasoning, while highlighting the importance of considering language demands and subscale-specific responsiveness.

items.title: Gesture use in autobiographical memory narration: The comparison of blind and sighted early teenagers.
items.abstract: Gestures are an integral component of speech. During autobiographical memory narration, gestures can be linked to the episodic quality of recalled events, facilitating speech production or supporting visuospatial processing. Gestures' role in children's autobiographical memory, particularly in blindness, remains unclear. The present study examined how cue modality (visually known, haptically known, abstract) related to episodic details of autobiographical memories and gesture use in blind and sighted early teenagers, and whether gesture use was associated with the episodic richness of recalled memories. Thirty-three blind and thirty-six sighted early teenagers were asked to recall autobiographical memories using a cue-word methodology. The recalled memories were subsequently coded for episodic and non-episodic details, as well as for representational and non-representational gesture use. Results showed that memory content varied as a function of cue modality in a similar manner across groups, with haptically-known cues eliciting fewer episodic details than visually-known and abstract cues. This cue-modality effect was attenuated when controlling for age, suggesting it may be partly age-driven. Blind teenagers produced more non-episodic details than sighted ones despite comparable levels of episodic content. Sighted teenagers gestured more frequently than blind teenagers, although gesture use did not vary by cue modality. Crucially, gesture frequency was not related to episodic quality of autobiographical memories in either group. These findings suggest that while gestures may support autobiographical retrieval in adults capable of producing extended, coherent narratives, their role may be more limited in sighted and blind teenagers, potentially due to developmental differences in scene construction and narrative ability.

items.title: Psychological foundations of ecosystem longevity: A framework of sustained participation in digital ecosystems.
items.abstract: Digital ecosystems depend on the continued participation of diverse actors who create, share, and consume value. While prior research has largely explained ecosystem success through structural mechanisms such as network effects, governance arrangements, ecosystem design, and business models, it has paid less attention to the psychological processes that sustain participation over time. This paper examines how ecosystem characteristics shape the psychological experiences that motivate participants to remain engaged over time, thereby contributing to ecosystem longevity. To address this gap, we conduct an integrative conceptual review that synthesizes research from digital ecosystems and psychology to develop a conceptual framework. Drawing on theories of trust, self-determination, psychological ownership, and social identity, we develop a framework explaining how ecosystem characteristics influence continued participation through three key psychological mechanisms: trust, autonomy, and psychological attachment. Specifically, we propose that pricing arrangements shape fairness judgments that inform trust; governance structures influence trust and autonomy by shaping predictability, transparency, and participant agency; boundary expansion influences trust by altering perceptions of vulnerability and future opportunities for value creation; and ecosystem design fosters psychological attachment through psychological ownership and social identification. These psychological experiences ultimately shape participants' willingness to remain engaged and contribute to ecosystem longevity. Using real-world illustrations from digital ecosystems, we develop a set of propositions linking ecosystem structures to continued participation and ecosystem longevity. By specifying the participant-level psychological processes through which ecosystem characteristics influence continued participation, this study provides a micro-foundational explanation of ecosystem longevity that complements existing structural and economic explanations of ecosystem persistence.

items.title: Domain-general skills predict individual differences in linguistic knowledge and spontaneous language use.
items.abstract: The present study investigated predictors of individual differences in linguistic knowledge and spontaneous language use in adults. Specifically, we examined the role of domain-general cognitive abilities-working memory, nonverbal reasoning, and processing speed-alongside implicit motivational factors, including achievement, power, and affiliation motives and activity inhibition. Linguistic knowledge was assessed through multiple tests covering receptive and productive vocabulary, grammar, spelling, and comprehension of fixed expressions, whereas language use was examined through participants' written narratives in the Picture Story Exercise (PSE), analyzed with the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) framework. Network and path analyses revealed that auditory working memory positively predicted linguistic knowledge and analytic language use, highlighting its role in the sequential organization and consolidation of verbal material. Visual working memory was unrelated to knowledge but predicted more authentic language use, suggesting a link to imagery-based and self-referential expression. Nonverbal reasoning supported knowledge but was negatively related to authenticity, indicating a trade-off between systematic abstraction and spontaneity. Processing speed, while crucial in early language development, did not predict knowledge in adults and was negatively associated with narrative word count, suggesting that efficiency may reduce elaboration in spontaneous production. Contrary to our predictions, implicit motives and activity inhibition were unrelated to both linguistic knowledge and language use. Together, these findings underscore how distinct domain-general abilities shape static linguistic knowledge and dynamic language use, highlighting the need for integrative models of adult language skills.

items.title: The spatial updating mechanism of different field cognitive styles in various perspective orientations: Evidence from behavior and fNIRS.
items.abstract: Spatial updating, the dynamic maintenance of self-environment spatial relations, is a core process in human navigation. It nevertheless remains unclear how field cognitive style (field-dependent [FD] vs. field-independent [FI]) and perspective orientation jointly shape this process. We therefore combined a judgment of relative direction (JRD) task with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in a 2 (field cognitive style: FD, FI) × 2 (perspective orientation: memory consistent, sensorimotor consistent) mixed design with 40 college students (20 FD, 20 FI). FI participants responded faster and more accurately than FD participants, and all participants performed better under the memory consistent orientation than the sensorimotor consistent orientation. The two factors interacted for reaction time but not for accuracy. FI participants responded faster than FD participants under the sensorimotor consistent orientation, whereas the two groups did not differ under the memory consistent orientation. This pattern suggests greater reference frame flexibility in FI participants. Exploratory fNIRS analyses showed numerically higher oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) in several fronto-parietal channels (e.g., precentral gyrus, precuneus, superior parietal lobule, and paracentral lobule) in FI participants. However, no channel survived Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction across the 49 channels, so these neural findings are exploratory and should not be read as statistically significant. Taken together, the results indicate that field cognitive style and perspective orientation jointly shape spatial updating. They advance the understanding of individual differences in spatial cognition and suggest that interfaces adapted to users' field cognitive style, together with training that targets reference frame flexibility, may benefit FD and FI individuals differently. Given the modest sample, the extreme group design, and the homogeneous student sample, however, these implications require validation in larger and more diverse samples and in real world settings.

items.title: Prospective memory deficit associated with major depressive disorder: Causality, clinical impact, and potential molecular mechanisms.
items.abstract: Prospective memory (PM) impairment is frequently observed in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet its causal relationship, clinical impact, and molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To clarify causality between MDD and PM deficits, bidirectional mendelian randomization (MR) was conducted (MDD: n = 1639572; PM deficits: n = 152605). Genetic liability to MDD significantly increased the risk of PM deficits (OR = 1.045, P -7.5 kcal/mol) of commonly used antidepressants to these targets. Virtual screening of psychiatric compounds identified Hypericin, with strong affinity to the core targets (mean -9.06 kcal/mol). In conclusion, MDD may increase the risk of PM deficits, which are associated with poorer treatment response and show limited improvement following current antidepressant treatments. Rap1-related mechanisms may be involved, and Hypericin may be considered a compound for further investigation.

items.title: How explanations evolve: Social learning and the explore-exploit trade-off.
items.abstract: Explanations are social objects, and when people try to explain something, they usually have at hand the explanations that others have tried before. We present a theory of how people use the explanations they encounter as clues to the broader landscape of possible explanations for the phenomenon to hand, which in turn informs their decisions about how and when to forage further for the explanations they wish to adopt. The challenge of coming up with novel explanations draws people to exploit or imitate appealing ones they have already encountered; this draw increases as less appealing alternatives become more distant (the "strawman" effect). Conversely, when presented with distinct, high-quality explanations, people can synthesize them, recombining the appealing features in new ways. We test and confirm these predictions using a two-stage transmission chain experiment. In Stage One, 101 participants were asked to explain unusual scenarios. In Stage Two, a separate group of 995 participants were asked to explain the same scenarios after reading pairs of explanations drawn from Stage One. We found that participants in Stage Two were more likely to exploit, or imitate, explanations when at least one was high in quality and particularly when it was paired with a weaker alternative. Participants were also more likely to synthesize perspectives from prior explanations when the two explanations were both high-quality and conceptually distinct. In contrast, participants were more likely to explore, or diverge, from prior explanations when the two explanations were both of low quality and distinct. Our work provides new insight into how collective exploration can be promoted, or stalled, by implicit information about what is yet to be discovered.

items.title: Workload matters: A quantitative examination of caseload reform & job satisfaction in South African child protection.
items.abstract: Child protection social work in South Africa is characterized by unmanageable caseloads, escalating administrative demands, and chronic resource constraints. Guided by Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, this pilot study explored caseload and workload conditions and the association between caseload size and job satisfaction among child protection social workers in South Africa where limited studies have quantitatively explored these issues. Child protection social workers (N = 66) were sampled from Child Protection Organisations across six provinces in South Africa through purposive sampling. A demographic questionnaire and the Child Welfare Employee Feedback Scale - Revised (CWEFS-R) were distributed electronically (Griffiths et al., 2023). The average caseload size for all participants (N = 66) was 96.42, which is above the broadly recommended national guideline of 60 cases per month. Significant negative correlations were found between caseload size and job satisfaction (p < .05), indicating an association between larger caseloads and lower job satisfaction. Job satisfaction varied significantly by province (Kruskal-Wallis H = 11.147, p = .025) with η2 = 0.199 and and f value of 0.368, indicating a large effect size. Findings reveal systemic challenges associated with excessive caseloads and dissatisfaction with key workplace conditions, including workload. Viewed through Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, the findings suggest that inadequate hygiene factors may contribute to job dissatisfaction despite the presence of positive intrinsic workplace factors. The results provide an initial evidence-based justification for supporting workload reform.

items.title: Effectiveness of Conversational Agents for Depression and Anxiety: Systematic Review and Network Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Agent Types, Dose, and Human Support.
items.abstract: Conversational agents (CAs) are increasingly used to deliver scalable interventions for depression and anxiety, but existing evidence has often treated these tools as a single category. The comparative effectiveness of different agent types, intervention doses, and levels of human support remains unclear. This review systematically evaluated the comparative effectiveness of various CA modalities and levels of human support, as well as potential dose-response relationships across different CA types. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Ovid, CINAHL, and Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection (PBSC) databases was conducted from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating CA-based interventions. We conducted a random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) using postintervention outcomes and assessed inconsistency and risk of bias (RoB). Evidence certainty was assessed using the CINeMA (confidence in network meta-analysis) framework. Where data permitted, model-based network dose-response meta-analysis (MBNMA) was performed to examine dose-response associations. A total of 41 studies (n=7577) were included. NMA showed that AI-enhanced intensive human support (AEIHS) appeared to produce greater symptom improvement for depression and anxiety compared with pure human digital guidance (PHDG; Hedges g=-4.28, 95% CI -5.56 to -2.99) and open-ended multimodal-enhanced chatbot (OEMM; Hedges g=-4.49, 95% CI -6.31 to -2.66), whereas most other comparisons were not statistically significant. MBNMA indicated that goal-oriented conversational agent (GOCA) and highly structured modular chatbot (HSMC) appeared to exhibit nonlinear effects, with preliminary evidence suggesting potentially enhanced response at low-to-moderate doses, though these findings require further investigation. However, publication bias was detected for depression (Egger P=.02), and the overall certainty of evidence was very low, primarily due to RoB, indirectness, and imprecision. While hybrid CA models with enhanced human involvement appeared to show potential advantages over fully automated systems, the evidence base remains limited. The very low certainty of evidence constrains confidence in comparative rankings and dose recommendations. Future high-quality trials are needed to establish optimal CA architectures and intervention doses for scalable mental health care. items.title: Psychopathology and Suicidal Ideation Among Female Veterans Exposed to Military Sexual Trauma.
items.abstract: Female veterans die by suicide at roughly twice the rate of female civilians, and military sexual trauma is a known risk factor. Little is known, however, about the relation between personality disorders and suicidal ideation in female veterans who have experienced military sexual trauma. This study examined personality disorder symptoms and other clinical conditions in relation to suicidal ideation. Participants were 92 female veterans who endorsed military sexual trauma anonymously completed five measures assessing for suicidal ideation and psychopathology. Ordinal logistic regression models tested associations between suicidal ideation and (a) ten personality disorder symptom scales and (b) post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms, depression, anxiety, and substance use disorders, tested both together and separately. Nearly half of participants (48.9%) reported suicidal ideation at the highest risk level. Borderline personality disorder symptoms were associated with more severe suicidal ideation (OR = 1.26, 95% CI [1.14, 1.41]); the other nine personality disorder symptom scales were not significantly associated with suicidal ideation. Post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms, depression, and anxiety were each associated with suicidal ideation in separate models, but none remained significant when entered together with alcohol and drug use disorders. Substance use disorders were not associated with suicidal ideation in either set of models. Borderline features may be an informative marker of risk for suicidal ideation among female veterans with military sexual trauma. However, these findings require replication in larger samples, and causality ought to be explored in longitudinal designs.

items.title: Digital Phenotyping of Voice Biomarkers for Psychological States in College Students: Longitudinal Mobile App Study.
items.abstract: College students face significant mental health challenges, yet traditional assessments often rely on in-person self-reports and long-form self-report survey approaches. The prevalence of smartphones and longitudinal digital phenotyping-using data from devices to rapidly monitor mental health processes-offers an opportunity to assess well-being using a nondisruptive, prevention-focused "light touch" approach via voice journaling and emoji-based expression. While voice biomarkers are associated with clinical anxiety and depression, little research has explored voice biomarkers' relation to psychological predictors of mental health processes in young adults. This study aimed to explore the utility of smartphone-captured voice biomarkers as objective indicators of psychological predictors of affective states in college students. College students (N=289) used the Meet Pandora smartphone app for over 2 months. Approximately 3 times per week, participants responded to voice journal prompts, such as "Describe a place you like to visit." Voice biomarkers were extracted from responses, and their association with concurrent psychological measurements (ie, voice journaling measured closest in time to psychology surveys) was modeled using multivariable, mixed-effects, covariate-adjusted (gender, baseline mental health diagnosis, prompt sentiment, foreign national status, and time) models. Random intercepts were included to control for baseline individual differences, and all analyses were adjusted for multiple comparisons. Associations were predominantly within students. On the 5-point daily affect scale (higher scores indicate more negative affect), negative affect was characterized by more utterances than usual (odds ratio [OR] 1.16, 95% CI 1.09-1.23; adjusted P<.001) and less positive language (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.97; adjusted P=.007), accompanied by reduced vocal energy and pitch: magnitude mean (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.78-0.88), pitch mean (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73-0.86), and root-mean-square energy (OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.85-0.95; all adjusted P<.001), with harmonics-to-noise ratio and pitch variance showing the same pattern (both adjusted P≤.01). Among students who used more positive language than their peers on average, stress was lower (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.50-0.92; adjusted P=.049) and their self-regard was higher (adjusted P=.04). While speech and acoustic features did not predict weekly measures of loneliness or acceptance, they were associated with stress, self-regard, and daily affect fluctuations. More positive language was associated with lower stress and higher self-regard. These findings highlight the utility of high-frequency assessments via voice biomarkers as signals of affective changes in college students. This work highlights that brief vocal samples may be able to detect early, affect-specific signs of mental health risks in young adults, which has important implications for psychopathology prevention and improving well-being.

items.title: Studies Using the Multiphase Optimization Strategy in Digital Mental Health: Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Improving the cost-effectiveness and scalability of mental health interventions remains challenging. The Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) framework provides a structured approach for developing, optimizing, and evaluating behavioral interventions by balancing effectiveness with efficiency, economy, and scalability. It does so across 3 phases: preparation (theoretical grounding and component selection), optimization (experimental testing), and evaluation (confirmatory trial). Digital mental health interventions are especially suited to this modular approach, as they enable researchers to easily manipulate components and personalize delivery. This study aims to examine how the MOST framework has been applied in the digital mental health field and to provide recommendations for future application. Systematic searches were conducted in Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, PsycInfo, and PubMed. Papers were included if they used the MOST to develop or optimize a digitally delivered mental health intervention. Studies targeting children aged under 12 years, reviews, and theoretical or simulated applications were excluded. Thirty-seven papers representing 18 research projects met the inclusion criteria. The preparation phase was often incomplete and inconsistently reported, with optimization criteria largely absent and conceptual models often lacking specificity. Eight projects completed at least 1 optimization trial, typically using factorial designs, but progression to intervention refinement or evaluation was limited. Projects conducting multiple optimization rounds were more likely to achieve an optimized intervention. The MOST is increasingly applied in digital mental health research but often only partially implemented. While factorial designs are widely adopted, critical preparatory elements are frequently missing. To fully realize the MOST's potential, future research should emphasize comprehensive application across all phases, iterative refinement, and transparent reporting.

items.title: Trapped Between Mirrors and Screens: The Role of Offline and Online Appearance Concerns in Adolescent Mental Health.
items.abstract: Offline appearance concerns are closely linked to mental health difficulties, such as depression, anxiety, and stress, as well as to concerns about appearance in online contexts. However, empirical evidence remains limited within non-Western cultural contexts such as Türkiye, where cultural norms reflect a dynamic interplay between autonomy and relatedness. The present study aimed to investigate the mediating role of online appearance concern, conceptualized through appearance-based social comparison and objectified body consciousness, in the relationship between offline appearance concern and psychological distress among adolescents. A nationally representative sample of 1,045 adolescents (M = 15.75, SD = 1.09, Range = 13-19) from diverse regions of Türkiye participated in the study. The study's findings revealed that offline appearance concerns, together with online appearance concerns, were significantly and positively associated with an increased risk of psychological distress (i.e., depression, anxiety, and stress) among adolescents in Türkiye. The statistical mediation of online appearance concerns in the association between offline appearance concerns and mental health symptoms was also significant. The study's results underscore the importance of addressing both offline and online appearance-related pressures in adolescent mental health by considering the intersection of traditional cultural values and global media influences.

items.title: Trajectories of post-traumatic stress symptoms following traumatic injury: a secondary analysis of the recovery after stress treatment randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: To characterize heterogeneous post-traumatic stress (PTSS) recovery trajectories following pediatric traumatic injuries and identify clinical and psychological factors associated with trajectory membership. Secondary analyses of a two-arm multisite randomized controlled trial comparing a brief online trauma-focused treatment [Reducing Stress after Trauma (ReSeT)] to usual care. Participants included children, ages 8-17, hospitalized following traumatic injuries and reporting elevated PTSS (per combined child and parent report), at 1 month post-injury. PTSS symptoms, measured by the Child Post-traumatic Stress Scale (CPSS), were assessed prior to randomization, weekly during the 8-week intervention period, and at post-intervention (week 10). We modeled child CPSS scores over time using group-based trajectory modeling. We included the following covariates: intervention group, age, sex, injury severity, resilience, post-traumatic cognitions, family functioning, and family income. Eighty-seven participants, average age of 11.67 years (2.44), were included. Three trajectories were identified: resilient (n = 18), recovering (n = 49), and chronic (n = 20). Exploratory analyses examining the treatment conditions separately indicated similar trajectories. Treatment condition, injury severity, and post-traumatic cognitions distinguished the trajectories, with those in the chronic trajectory belonging to the usual care group, having lower injury severity, and higher post-traumatic cognitions relative to those in the resilient trajectory. Findings provide support for the three-trajectory model of PTSS recovery following pediatric injury and highlight the potential efficacy of ReSeT in reducing chronic PTSS. Post-traumatic cognitions emerged as potent and potentially modifiable correlates of chronicity, underscoring the utility of addressing them in risk stratification and intervention.

items.title: Person-centered analyses demonstrate physical health is associated with depression, anxiety, and suicide propensity over 6-month period in the Texas Youth Depression and Suicide Research Network1.
items.abstract: The objectives of the current study were (a) to identify profiles of treatment-seeking youth with depression and/or suicidal thoughts and behaviors based on patterns of physical health (i.e., functioning-mobility, fatigue, pain interference, pain severity, medical comorbidities), (b) to explore demographic and treatment correlates of profiles (i.e., age, sex, race, ethnicity, family income, and treatment type), (c) to explore associations among profiles and mental health outcomes (i.e., anxiety, depression, suicidal risk, suicidal propensity) at baseline, and (d) to examine whether the profiles were associated with mental health changes over time (i.e., 6 months). Participants were 1,174 youth ages 8-17 (M age = 14.5; 70.9% female; 69.6% White, 44.8% Hispanic/Latino). Youth completed measures of physical health, depression, anxiety, and suicide symptoms. Latent variable mixture modeling was conducted. Three profiles emerged: (1) "High Physical Health" (49.3%), (2) "Moderate Physical Health" (39.9%), and (3) "Low Physical Health" (10.7%). Youth in the "High Physical Health" profile had the lowest depression, anxiety, suicide propensity, and suicide risk, and youth in the "Low Physical Health" profile had the highest depression, anxiety, and suicide propensity. Mental health symptoms improved over time for all profiles, and the rate of change was not different. Results highlight the importance of examining physical health in treatment-seeking youth, as physical health symptoms may impact depression, anxiety, and suicide propensity over time and indicate a treatment targeting both mental and physical health.

items.title: Developmental Aspects of Language Mapping with Stereoelectroencephalography.
items.abstract: This review examines developmental perspectives on the use of stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) for delineating language areas and networks in pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, both as a clinical tool for presurgical evaluation and as a modality for gaining neuroscientific insights into speech and language development. Language development is a dynamic process that begins before birth and continues into adulthood, shaped by the maturation of brain networks. SEEG allows high-resolution study of these networks, providing a unique perspective on the organization of language systems. This review traces language acquisition from early infancy through adolescence and adulthood, highlighting the pivotal role of neural oscillations. We then summarize classical and contemporary neural models of language organization, highlighting the distributed and hierarchical networks, and emphasize the high spatial and temporal resolution of SEEG for presurgical planning that enables clinicians to optimize neurosurgical interventions while preserving essential language areas and the tracts connecting them. Our review also addresses the human brain's remarkable plasticity and capacity for reorganization, which are especially pronounced in children and vital for adaptation to and recovery from neurologic injury or surgery. We focus specifically on developmental reorganization in pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and its implications for language mapping with SEEG. The review concludes with recommendations for designing language-mapping batteries tailored to the unique needs of pediatric patients.

items.title: Suicide in former reserve UK Armed Forces personnel, 1996-2018: A whole population cohort study.
items.abstract: "Reserve Personnel", who serve voluntarily, comprise around a fifth of the UK Armed Forces (UKAF). Little is known about their suicide risk, or factors associated with suicide in this population. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of suicide in reserve personnel who left the UKAF between 1996 and 2018 by linking national databases. We examined the risk of suicide in this group of veterans compared to the general population and identified the factors most strongly associated with suicide after discharge. We also compared reserve veterans' rates of and risk factors for suicide with our previous findings on regular veterans of the UKAF. The 265,941 former reserve veterans had over 4,227,131 person years at risk, and were mostly male (86%). In total, 584 (0.2%) died by suicide. Their overall rate of suicide was lower than the general population (standardised mortality ratio [95% confidence interval] 76 [70-83]), with significantly lower rates in those aged 25-29 years (age specific mortality ratios 46-87). Overall, rates were similar to age-matched regular veterans (96 [89-105]), however, risk was lower in reserve veterans aged under 25 and higher in those aged 50-59 years. Factors associated with a higher suicide risk were being male, serving in the Army, and discharge between the ages of 45-49 years. Length of service of 3-4 years and more than 5 years, and being a non-commissioned officer (NCO) were associated with a reduced risk. There was no evidence of an association with deployment. Rates of contact with specialist NHS mental health services were low (21%). Prevention should focus on ensuring reserves are aware of and have access to appropriate health, employment and social support tailored to their needs. Addressing specific stressors common in men in mid-life, such as economic adversity and isolation, may also help reduce risk.

items.title: Enhancing diagnostic and intervention-related skills with adaptive feedback: Study protocol for a simulation-based learning study on symptoms of learning and behavioural difficulties.
items.abstract: This project uses simulated digital case scenarios to analyse diagnostic and intervention-related skills of teacher, school psychology, and medical students concerning primary school children's difficulties in mathematics and their hyperactive, inattentive and impulsive behaviours. Here, the conditions for an effective use of macro- and micro-adaptive feedback - powered by natural language processing (NLP) methods - compared to static feedback will be the focus. The aim is to identify effective types of feedback for students who differ in their prior diagnostic and intervention-related knowledge. We compare three groups of university students (medical students, school psychology students, and pre-service teachers) with varying professional specialisations and corresponding knowledge bases as learning prerequisites using simulated digital case scenarios. In validation study 1a, we analyse students' case processing and validate our measures for students' prior knowledge. Furthermore, the results are used for informing the design and refinement of micro- and macro-adaptive feedback. Validation study 1b investigates static, macro-adaptive, and micro-adaptive feedback. In Study 2, by using "think aloud"-methods and trace data, we investigate to what extent learners benefit differently from the processing of digital case scenarios in the absence of any feedback and what kind of cognitive, metacognitive, motivational learning processes occur. In study 3, we investigate how the form of feedback in the digital case scenarios affects students' acquisition of new diagnostic and intervention-related skills and how students process the different forms of feedback. Finally, Study 4 examines the extent to which different forms of feedback are helpful for students with low vs. high prior knowledge. This project will analyse which benefits feedback with different degrees of adaptivity can provide for learning diagnostic reasoning and the planning of related interventions, especially when considering potential interaction effects with learners' varying prior professional as well as diagnostic and intervention-related knowledge and diagnostic processing.

items.title: People know who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance.
items.abstract: Whether and how people approach social interactions hinges on how they expect others to respond. Extensive social psychology research suggests that people are inaccurate interpersonal perceivers, overestimating negative responses (e.g., discomfort) and underestimating positive responses (e.g., appreciation) across a variety of social situations. However, this conclusion is based almost exclusively on mean-level bias analyses that obscure the dyadic nature of interpersonal judgment and rely on a narrow conceptualization of interpersonal accuracy. Leveraging research on favor-asking and anticipated compliance as an exemplar, we demonstrate that interpersonal accuracy takes multiple theoretically distinct forms, and that the prevailing conclusion that people misunderstand their influence over others-because they tend to underestimate compliance-is likely overgeneralized. Across four studies (13,196 directed dyadic ratings), we show that people accurately differentiate between who will comply with their favor requests (dyadic meta-accuracy) despite the average tendency to underestimate compliance (mean-level bias). This pattern emerged for specific and general favor requests, among well- and newly-acquainted individuals, and beyond what could be expected due to self-projection. Through this dyadic lens, people are highly adept judges of their influence over others, as they are able to target their requests toward individuals who are uniquely likely to acquiesce to them-and can avoid wasting time on those who are not. Thus, our research refines existing implications for how people approach asking for favors. More broadly, by aligning theory, measurement, and level of analysis, our studies elucidate the need for greater theoretical precision and empirical breadth in interpersonal accuracy research.

items.title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity.
items.abstract: Molecules implicated in host defense can, independent of their roles as immune mediators, regulate sleep. In mammals, cytokines such as Tumor Necrosis Factor α (TNF α) and Interleukin1β (IL1β) promote sleep. In Drosophila, infection stimulates the systemic release of a battery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). These fly immune effectors have been understudied as sleep modulators. We obtained mutants in different AMPs and characterized their functions in sleep and plasticity. AMP mutants slept less with a longer sleep latency, and lowered arousal thresholds. Group C mutant flies, doubly mutant for the anti-fungal peptides Metchnikowin (Mtk) and Drosomycin (Drs), showed the greatest impairments. These Group C mutants also showed an exaggerated sleep rebound, sleep rebound was unaltered in other mutants. While many classes of AMPs showed sleep deficits, different sets of AMP mutants exhibited specific disruptions in socialization and rocking induced sleep. To determine whether sleep amount and sleep functions were dissociable, we evaluated memory and quantified synapse abundance. Group C mutants uniquely exhibited normal learning and memory, and lower synapse abundance, despite sleeping the least. Group C mutants are thus able to carry out some sleep functions without sleeping much. Glial knockdown of Metchnikowin and Drosomycin mimicked the sleep phenotypes of the null mutants, these genes thus act from glia. While Group C mutants retained normal cognitive function, other AMP mutants showed impairments in sleep and memory. Sleep and memory defects in these AMP mutants were reversible - enhancing sleep of Bomanin mutants pharmacologically or behaviorally improved learning and memory. Together, these data suggest that AMPs are potent sleep modulators and that different classes of AMPs differently affect sleep and sleep dependent outcomes.

items.title: The missing Nobels: Mapping the landscape of prestigious scientific prizes.
items.abstract: Prestigious recognition prizes, like the Nobel Prizes, can shape scientists' career decisions and how science is seen. Yet the landscape of such prizes is not well understood. We screen roughly 2,700 international scientific prizes and rank the 99 most prestigious using a novel prestige index. Recognition is unevenly distributed across fields: physics, life sciences, and mathematics are heavily recognized relative to field size, while computer science, engineering, psychology, and the social sciences are under-served. Only three of the 99 prizes target early-career scientists.

items.title: Informal Digital Information Use in Hospital Mass Casualty Incident Management During Wartime: Multicenter Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study.
items.abstract: Managing mass casualty incidents (MCIs) during an active warfare environment presents unique challenges, including operating under extreme uncertainty. Traditionally, emergency communications rely on strict, hierarchical channels from prehospital services to receiving hospitals. However, informal digital communication streams, particularly instant messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram, are increasingly used within medical workflows. Despite international interest in public social media during disasters, empirical research regarding how hospital leadership echelons use informal messaging tools for real-time operational and clinical decision-making during active warfare remains sparse. This study aimed to characterize the adoption of social media and instant messaging platforms as early information sources among hospital-based MCI managers during wartime and to evaluate their specific impact on real-time operational and clinical decision-making. A multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured questionnaire distributed across all 24 national medical centers authorized to receive MCIs during wartime in Israel. Target respondents encompassed diverse leadership echelons, including emergency department directors, trauma service directors, trauma coordinators, charge nurses, emergency team members, and hospital executive leadership. Overall, 76 medical professionals representing key decision-makers across national receiving centers completed the survey. WhatsApp emerged as the most frequently used platform (median 3.0, IQR 2.00-4.00). Although these informal channels provided rapid initial intelligence, 65.3% (49/75) of respondents encountered false information during emergency events. Consequently, 81.3% (n=61) reported routinely verifying social media data against official channels before executing major actions. Multivariate regression analysis revealed distinct pathways of influence: higher platform use intensity was strongly and independently associated with enhanced situational awareness (P=.002) and greater operational decision-making influence (P=.02). In addition, participants' level of trust and reliance was associated with clinical decisions (P=.01) and real-time team management (P=.03). Furthermore, active platform engagement during live threat conditions was positively correlated with heightened situational awareness during missile launch alerts (P<.001) and missile fall alerts (P<.001). Platform use and trust behaviors remained consistent across years of professional experience, qualifications, and executive roles. Informal digital platforms, dominated by WhatsApp, serve as vital, rapid early information channels for hospital MCI leadership during wartime emergencies. While use intensity directly enhances situational awareness and operational control during active missile threats, clinical and team management actions remain strictly contingent on trust. Given the high exposure to unverified data, formalizing structured verification protocols and incorporating informal digital communication strategies into hospital disaster preparedness frameworks are essential to optimize real-time decision-making in future large-scale health emergencies.
